civility.statement: The coalition documents read like a manifesto of white supremacy and cultural genocide.
civility.explanation: Extreme, inflammatory characterisation of opponents' agenda rather than engagement with specific provisions.

civility.statement: I want to mihi and thank the Government made up of parties funded and supported by the hyper-rich, the 2 percenters who own more than 50 percent of the wealth
civility.explanation: Sarcastic 'thank you' framing characterising opponents as captured by the rich; rhetorical jab.

civility.statement: ACT and New Zealand First's combined vote is less than the 20 percent who you have offended the hell out of
civility.explanation: Combative framing ('offended the hell out of') but anchored to a legitimate point about vote share.

civility.statement: I look opposite me and I see tobacco lobbyists, I see gun lobbyists, I see Hobson's Pledge lobbyists, I see absolute profiteers, landlords, conspirators, and climate change deniers.
civility.explanation: A string of pejorative labels applied to opponents personally rather than addressing their arguments.

civility.statement: Do not be hateful or angry, whānau mā. Do not be hateful or angry at this new Government's treatment and disrespect. Be inspired. Be motivated to be more ourselves.
civility.explanation: Counsels against hatefulness, a relatively constructive note amid an adversarial speech.

civility.statement: I urge this Prime Minister to take balanced counsel and immerse himself in communities who are proud of their culture, who have their own solutions, and are not embarrassed about who they are
civility.explanation: Frames criticism as advice rather than insult, having earlier called him 'a decent bloke'.

civility.statement: I came into Parliament in 1999 and never would have thought he would have got up there. But he will be, I think, a very, very good Speaker.
civility.explanation: Gracious, respectful endorsement of the new Speaker from across the House.

civility.statement: Seymour knows nothing about the Treaty. He's been expelled by his own iwi. He got kicked out of the tribe the other day.
civility.explanation: Personal attack on Seymour's competence and standing rather than his Treaty argument.

civility.statement: He knows more than Jim Bolger, he knows more than Jenny Shipley, he knows more than Bill English, he knows more than Jacinda Ardern—he knows more than every Prime Minister who has supported the Treaty principles since 1987!
civility.explanation: Sarcastic ridicule of Seymour, though aimed at his Treaty stance rather than his person directly.

civility.statement: Already, we have seen, at the current climate talks, that New Zealand received the "Fossil of the Day" award... This was the very first country to be singled out, and it is because of this Government's winding back the clock to bring back oil and gas exploration.
civility.explanation: Pointed criticism of government policy and its international standing, but substantive rather than a personal attack.

civility.statement: that is the prerogative of the Government of the day to reverse decisions of previous Governments. It is what Governments do.
civility.explanation: Even-handed acknowledgement of the government's mandate before pressing her critique.

civility.statement: Labour were a party at the election who stood for nothing.
civility.explanation: Sweeping dismissive characterisation of opponents rather than engagement with their policies.

civility.statement: The worst defeat of any Government in this country ever was this previous Government because they stood for nothing.
civility.explanation: Triumphalist jab at opponents rather than substantive critique.

veracity.statement: We're not going to have a French Polynesian name that's an insult to everybody in the South Island.
veracity.explanation: Claiming 'Aotearoa' is a 'French Polynesian name' is misleading; it is a Māori name for New Zealand.

veracity.statement: if they're the Māori voice and they got only 3 percent of the vote most of the time, and yet they say the Māori people are 18 percent of the population, it means that one-sixth of the Māori people might support them and five-sixths don't. How can they call themselves the Māori voice?
veracity.explanation: Rough figures are in the right range but the derived 'five-sixths don't' is an oversimplified, misleading construction.

veracity.statement: may I remind Winston: you only won five seats; we won six.
veracity.explanation: A checkable factual claim about seat counts, consistent with the 2023 result.

veracity.statement: The coalition documents read like a manifesto of white supremacy and cultural genocide.
veracity.explanation: Hyperbolic equating of policy documents with 'genocide'; misleading.

veracity.statement: Scrapping Aotearoa's world-leading smokefree laws will sacrifice Māori lives to fund tax cuts for the wealthy.
veracity.explanation: The link between smokefree-repeal revenue and tax cuts was openly stated by the government, but 'sacrifice Māori lives' is emotive framing of an uncertain outcome.

veracity.statement: We are rangatira who never ceded our sovereignty, never bowed down to a foreign power.
veracity.explanation: Contested historical/constitutional claim; supported by the Māori-text reading of Te Tiriti and the Waitangi Tribunal's Stage 1 finding, but disputed in law.

veracity.statement: I want to mihi and thank the Government made up of parties funded and supported by the hyper-rich, the 2 percenters who own more than 50 percent of the wealth
veracity.explanation: Wealth-concentration claim is in the right direction for NZ inequality but the specific '2 percent own >50 percent' figure is overstated/imprecise.

veracity.statement: I am proud as heck that we showed those who paid $440,000 to get a single MP in that our little $17,000 per candidate goes a long way.
veracity.explanation: Specific spend figures are asserted without source; plausible but unverified here.

veracity.statement: ACT and New Zealand First's combined vote is less than the 20 percent who you have offended the hell out of
veracity.explanation: ACT (~8.6%) plus NZ First (~6%) combined is indeed under 20%; broadly accurate, though '20 percent offended' is rhetorical.

veracity.statement: Seymour knows nothing about the Treaty. He's been expelled by his own iwi. He got kicked out of the tribe the other day.
veracity.explanation: 'Knows nothing' is hyperbole, and the 'expelled by his iwi' claim is an overstated characterisation of a contested incident.

veracity.statement: I was the Minister who was in charge of overseeing the language, and part of that strategy is getting 1 million speakers by 2040.
veracity.explanation: Accurately states the Maihi Karauna goal of one million te reo speakers by 2040 and his ministerial role.

veracity.statement: There are 21,000 new public housing places funded by the previous Governments between 2017 and 2023. We delivered over 13,000 of them in the six years that we were in Government; the most public housing of any Government since Walter Nash
veracity.explanation: Figures are broadly consistent with the public housing build under Labour 2017–2023; the 'since Walter Nash' superlative is harder to verify and she herself flags uncertainty.

veracity.statement: Already, we have seen, at the current climate talks, that New Zealand received the "Fossil of the Day" award... This was the very first country to be singled out, and it is because of this Government's winding back the clock to bring back oil and gas exploration.
veracity.explanation: NZ did receive a Fossil of the Day award at COP28 over the oil and gas reversal; broadly accurate, with some rhetorical framing around 'very first'.

veracity.statement: We're no longer hearing the Minister of Finance, the Hon Nicola Willis, tell us that it is a fiscally neutral tax package.
veracity.explanation: A characterisation of a shift in the Minister's messaging; plausible but stated without the specific evidence, partly interpretive.

veracity.statement: The worst defeat of any Government in this country ever was this previous Government because they stood for nothing.
veracity.explanation: Labour's 2023 result was its worst in decades, but 'worst defeat of any Government ever' is an overstatement, and the causal claim is editorial.

veracity.statement: Under Chris Hipkins' watch as Minister of Education... our achievement went backwards... The Programme for International Student Assessment results last night just confirmed that decline.
veracity.explanation: NZ's PISA results did show long-run decline; broadly accurate, though attributing it specifically to one minister's 'watch' is contestable.

specificity.statement: We want this country to be called New Zealand, and if we're going to change the name, then we're going to ask all New Zealanders first.
specificity.explanation: States a clear position (retain 'New Zealand', any change via public consultation) but no mechanism, timeframe, or named process.

specificity.statement: Repealing section 7AA of the Oranga Tamariki Act will undo all the progress that has been made to try and fix a systemically racist organisation that, over generations, has stolen our kids.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific provision (s7AA) and Act, giving concrete reference points.

specificity.statement: We will welcome you. We will feed you. We will house you. We will connect you. We will educate you. We will care for you. We will hear you. We will love you.
specificity.explanation: Aspirational marae-welcome metaphor with no concrete mechanism.

specificity.statement: As Moana Jackson laid out in the Matike Mai kaupapa, we must strive for self-determination, self-sufficiency to be implemented by 2040, on the 200th anniversary of the Treaty of Waitangi.
specificity.explanation: Names a framework (Matike Mai) and a target date (2040) but no concrete steps or mechanisms.

specificity.statement: I am proud as heck that we showed those who paid $440,000 to get a single MP in that our little $17,000 per candidate goes a long way.
specificity.explanation: Cites concrete dollar figures contrasting campaign spend per MP.

specificity.statement: We want to end poverty. We want to have a tax policy where we would have 2.2 million people living better.
specificity.explanation: Attaches a figure (2.2 million people) to a tax aim but gives no rates, thresholds, or mechanism.

specificity.statement: We wanted to see GST off kai. We wanted to see an end to duopolies in supermarkets. We wanted to see the end to seabed mining
specificity.explanation: Lists concrete, named policy positions (remove GST on food, break supermarket duopoly, end seabed mining).

specificity.statement: I was the Minister who was in charge of overseeing the language, and part of that strategy is getting 1 million speakers by 2040.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete target (1 million speakers) and date (2040).

specificity.statement: All that the principles talk about is partnership. They talk about good faith. They talk about participation. That's what the principles are about.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific Treaty principles (partnership, good faith, participation) rather than speaking generally.

specificity.statement: That is the job of an Opposition—it is to hold the Government of the day to account, and that is what we will be doing.
specificity.explanation: Clear statement of intent but general; defines a role without concrete measures yet.

specificity.statement: There are 21,000 new public housing places funded by the previous Governments between 2017 and 2023. We delivered over 13,000 of them in the six years that we were in Government; the most public housing of any Government since Walter Nash
specificity.explanation: Concrete figures (21,000 funded, 13,000+ delivered) with timeframe.

specificity.statement: I have set a very ambitious target of getting 80 percent of our kids to curriculum by the time they leave intermediate.
specificity.explanation: Concrete numeric target (80%) with a defined milestone (by end of intermediate/year 8).

specificity.statement: We will remove the distraction of cellphones in our schools, because we know that the evidence shows that our kids improve their achievement and also their wellbeing.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete action (cellphone ban) though without timing detail here.

specificity.statement: National will return a curriculum that is knowledge-rich; that lays out the core content knowledge, every year, in order of how it should be taught to ensure that there is consistency across the country.
specificity.explanation: Describes a concrete approach (year-by-year sequenced, knowledge-rich curriculum) though without dates or detail of content.

specificity.statement: We will ensure that every single child in this country at primary school will learn to read through structured literacy, and we will ensure that structured mathematics is embedded
specificity.explanation: Names specific methods (structured literacy, structured maths) and the target group (every primary child).

specificity.statement: In our first 100 days... we are ensuring that every child—no matter where they go to school—has access to an hour a day of reading, writing, and maths.
specificity.explanation: Concrete commitment with quantity (one hour/day) and timeframe (first 100 days).

charisma.statement: We want this country to be called New Zealand, and if we're going to change the name, then we're going to ask all New Zealanders first.
charisma.explanation: Appeals to majority inclusion ('ask all New Zealanders') but is framed against a minority, so only partially unifying.

charisma.statement: We are rangatira who never ceded our sovereignty, never bowed down to a foreign power.
charisma.explanation: Rousing identity affirmation that rallies his own side rather than reaching across the House.

charisma.statement: We will welcome you. We will feed you. We will house you. We will connect you. We will educate you. We will care for you. We will hear you. We will love you.
charisma.explanation: Inclusive, welcoming vision extended even to opponents ('you'), invitational rather than combative.

charisma.statement: but our tikanga informs us to rise above hate, rise above division, rise above radical supremacy, and rise above imperialism.
charisma.explanation: Calls for rising above division, but framed against opponents cast as practising 'hate' and 'supremacy', limiting its bridge-building.

charisma.statement: Do not be hateful or angry, whānau mā. Do not be hateful or angry at this new Government's treatment and disrespect. Be inspired. Be motivated to be more ourselves.
charisma.explanation: Urges supporters away from anger toward positive motivation; constructive in tone though still aimed at her own base.

charisma.statement: I urge this Prime Minister to take balanced counsel and immerse himself in communities who are proud of their culture, who have their own solutions, and are not embarrassed about who they are
charisma.explanation: Direct, relatively respectful appeal to the PM to seek broader counsel; reaches toward the other side.

charisma.statement: I came into Parliament in 1999 and never would have thought he would have got up there. But he will be, I think, a very, very good Speaker.
charisma.explanation: Warm, cross-party goodwill that builds collegial rapport.

charisma.statement: National was hugely supportive of the language—hugely supportive of the language—and I don't mind saying that I think there's a lot of good National people.
charisma.explanation: Explicitly credits opponents (National, Key, English) for past support of te reo, seeking common ground.

charisma.statement: That is the job of an Opposition—it is to hold the Government of the day to account, and that is what we will be doing.
charisma.explanation: Confident framing of the opposition role, appealing mainly to her own side.

charisma.statement: that is the prerogative of the Government of the day to reverse decisions of previous Governments. It is what Governments do.
charisma.explanation: Concedes the legitimacy of the opponents' right to govern and reverse policy, a fair-minded, bridge-acknowledging point.

rigor.statement: if they're the Māori voice and they got only 3 percent of the vote most of the time, and yet they say the Māori people are 18 percent of the population, it means that one-sixth of the Māori people might support them and five-sixths don't. How can they call themselves the Māori voice?
rigor.explanation: Uses a numerical argument, but the inference conflates total party vote share with support among Māori specifically (many Māori vote for other parties), a flawed step.

rigor.statement: If we'd not got back, these three parties, we were heading off to be Venezuela or Myanmar.
rigor.explanation: Hyperbolic false analogy with no evidential link between NZ policy and the cited regimes.

rigor.statement: The coalition documents read like a manifesto of white supremacy and cultural genocide.
rigor.explanation: Sweeping label substituted for evidenced argument; loaded terms without demonstrated entailment.

rigor.statement: Repealing section 7AA of the Oranga Tamariki Act will undo all the progress that has been made to try and fix a systemically racist organisation that, over generations, has stolen our kids.
rigor.explanation: Asserts consequences without evidence; 'undo all progress' is an unsupported absolute.

rigor.statement: Scrapping Aotearoa's world-leading smokefree laws will sacrifice Māori lives to fund tax cuts for the wealthy.
rigor.explanation: Causal chain is plausible but stated as certainty with an emotional appeal rather than evidence.

rigor.statement: As Moana Jackson laid out in the Matike Mai kaupapa, we must strive for self-determination, self-sufficiency to be implemented by 2040, on the 200th anniversary of the Treaty of Waitangi.
rigor.explanation: Anchors the goal in a cited body of work, lending some structure, but the pathway is unspecified.

rigor.statement: I look opposite me and I see tobacco lobbyists, I see gun lobbyists, I see Hobson's Pledge lobbyists, I see absolute profiteers, landlords, conspirators, and climate change deniers.
rigor.explanation: Ad hominem characterisation in place of evidenced argument.

rigor.statement: All that the principles talk about is partnership. They talk about good faith. They talk about participation. That's what the principles are about.
rigor.explanation: Gives a substantive account of what the principles entail, though offered as assertion rather than with cited sourcing.

rigor.statement: He knows more than Jim Bolger, he knows more than Jenny Shipley, he knows more than Bill English, he knows more than Jacinda Ardern—he knows more than every Prime Minister who has supported the Treaty principles since 1987!
rigor.explanation: Appeal to authority/incredulity by listing past PMs rather than engaging Seymour's actual argument.

rigor.statement: We will remove the distraction of cellphones in our schools, because we know that the evidence shows that our kids improve their achievement and also their wellbeing.
rigor.explanation: Appeals to 'the evidence' on achievement and wellbeing but cites no specific study; a reasonable but lightly-evidenced claim.

rigor.statement: Labour were a party at the election who stood for nothing.
rigor.explanation: Unsupported absolute ('stood for nothing') functioning as a rhetorical slogan.

rigor.statement: Under Chris Hipkins' watch as Minister of Education... our achievement went backwards... The Programme for International Student Assessment results last night just confirmed that decline.
rigor.explanation: Cites a concrete data source (PISA) to support the decline claim, but the causal link to one minister is asserted rather than demonstrated.

divination.statement: If we'd not got back, these three parties, we were heading off to be Venezuela or Myanmar.
divination.explanation: Counterfactual prediction of national collapse; implausible and unsupported.

divination.statement: Repealing section 7AA of the Oranga Tamariki Act will undo all the progress that has been made to try and fix a systemically racist organisation that, over generations, has stolen our kids.
divination.explanation: Predicts repeal will 'undo all the progress'; directionally arguable but the absolute 'all' is uncertain and unproven.

divination.statement: Scrapping Aotearoa's world-leading smokefree laws will sacrifice Māori lives to fund tax cuts for the wealthy.
divination.explanation: Predicts harm to Māori health from repeal; plausible given higher Māori smoking rates but magnitude uncertain.

divination.statement: We will ensure this Government's reign is short.
divination.explanation: Predicts a one-term government; the coalition in fact governed a full term, and at the time this was an optimistic forecast against incumbency.

divination.statement: I said very clearly about three weeks ago that Māori would revolt in the streets. I said there would be civil disobedience—not my choice. I said you'll get protests worse than the Springbok Tour.
divination.explanation: Predicts street protests exceeding the 1981 Springbok Tour; large hīkoi did follow, but 'worse than the Springbok Tour' overshoots what eventuated.

authenticity.statement: Who settled the central North Island Tribes' 14-iwi settlement? Who settled that? The Māori Wardens—who gave them their start? The Māori Women's Welfare League, Mt Hikurangi—I could be here all day on what we've done for Māori, not like these people: all talk and no action; all talk and no action.
authenticity.explanation: Cites concrete past involvement (CNI settlement, support for Māori Wardens) to back his claim of action for Māori; partially verifiable record consistent with the stance.

authenticity.statement: National was hugely supportive of the language—hugely supportive of the language—and I don't mind saying that I think there's a lot of good National people.
authenticity.explanation: Acknowledges good faith on the other side even while attacking current policy, a consistent and fair-minded stance.

authenticity.statement: banning new offshore exploration was something that I was proud that we delivered in our Government.
authenticity.explanation: Consistent with Labour's stated climate position and an action it took, words matching deeds.

authenticity.statement: We're no longer hearing the Minister of Finance, the Hon Nicola Willis, tell us that it is a fiscally neutral tax package.
authenticity.explanation: Accuses an opponent of inconsistency on fiscal neutrality; an attack on the opponent's consistency rather than a signal about Woods herself.

strength.statement: Who settled the central North Island Tribes' 14-iwi settlement? Who settled that? The Māori Wardens—who gave them their start? The Māori Women's Welfare League, Mt Hikurangi—I could be here all day on what we've done for Māori, not like these people: all talk and no action; all talk and no action.
strength.explanation: Claims credit for delivered outcomes like the CNI settlement, which did occur, but the 'we' is broad and follow-through partly overstated.

strength.statement: We want to end poverty. We want to have a tax policy where we would have 2.2 million people living better.
strength.explanation: Aspirational ('end poverty') from an opposition party with no delivery vehicle.

strength.statement: There are 21,000 new public housing places funded by the previous Governments between 2017 and 2023. We delivered over 13,000 of them in the six years that we were in Government; the most public housing of any Government since Walter Nash
strength.explanation: Claims delivered, verifiable output (13,000+ public homes built) rather than mere announcement.

strength.statement: banning new offshore exploration was something that I was proud that we delivered in our Government.
strength.explanation: Refers to an actually enacted policy (2018 ban on new offshore oil/gas exploration) she was associated with delivering.

strength.statement: I have set a very ambitious target of getting 80 percent of our kids to curriculum by the time they leave intermediate.
strength.explanation: A clear, committed target stated at the outset of the term; delivery is yet to be demonstrated.

strength.statement: We will remove the distraction of cellphones in our schools, because we know that the evidence shows that our kids improve their achievement and also their wellbeing.
strength.explanation: A firm commitment that the government did subsequently implement; here stated as forthcoming.

strength.statement: National will return a curriculum that is knowledge-rich; that lays out the core content knowledge, every year, in order of how it should be taught to ensure that there is consistency across the country.
strength.explanation: A stated policy direction at term's start; follow-through not yet demonstrated.

strength.statement: We will ensure that every single child in this country at primary school will learn to read through structured literacy, and we will ensure that structured mathematics is embedded
strength.explanation: Firm universal commitment; delivery remains to be shown at this point in the term.

strength.statement: In our first 100 days... we are ensuring that every child—no matter where they go to school—has access to an hour a day of reading, writing, and maths.
strength.explanation: Time-bound commitment tied to the 100-day plan; credible delivery vehicle, outcome pending.

civility.statement: When I was standing in Christchurch Central for the first time, he called me an ambulance chaser and I called him deeply offensive. I don’t chase ambulances anymore, and I’m sure he’s not deeply offensive anymore either. So I’m sure we’ll get on fine as well.
civility.explanation: Recalls a past mutual insult with Gerry Brownlee but frames it self-deprecatingly and reconciliatorily, defusing rather than escalating.

civility.statement: here’s one of the things that this Speech from the Throne says: “for the past several years the number of people employed in the public service has grown at a rate that has not been matched by a commensurate increase in the level of services provided to the public.” Does that sound like Christopher Luxon to you? No, that’s the 2008 Speech from the Throne.
civility.explanation: Pointed and mocking in tone but engages the substance of the policy content rather than attacking a person.

civility.statement: that’s a corporate middle manager who himself said today, from that chair, that the Government’s “Under new management”.
civility.explanation: Belittling 'corporate middle manager' label aimed at Luxon's character/competence rather than at a policy.

civility.statement: In fact, a lot of what the Key Government did was more progressive than what that Government’s proposing, so you should be utterly and totally ashamed of yourself.
civility.explanation: 'You should be utterly and totally ashamed of yourself' is a personal admonishment rather than substantive critique.

civility.statement: a new Government department with a Minister of Regulation to cut regulatory costs, ha ha! It is laughable. You know, so you’re going to have an entire machinery to cut costs. That is absolutely ridiculous.
civility.explanation: Mocking ('laughable', 'ridiculous') but directed at the policy/structure, not a person.

civility.statement: It’s a neoliberal straight-jacket and it’s been roundly criticised by anyone who knows anything about it.
civility.explanation: Dismissive labelling but aimed at the legislation rather than a person.

civility.statement: It’s utterly shameful that a party with a number of medical doctors in its ranks will vote to increase smoking.
civility.explanation: 'Utterly shameful' plus a loaded framing imputing bad motive to the opposing party.

civility.statement: The member for Banks Peninsula, Vanessa Weenink, GP, would have had people come into her practice with emphysema caused by smoking addiction. Will she vote for it or will she uphold her Hippocratic Oath that says “Do no harm.”?
civility.explanation: Singles out a named member and pressures her personally, implying she would betray her medical ethics.

civility.statement: This is a harmful piece of piece of legislation. It will cause death. Death by taxes is what we’ve got here.
civility.explanation: Sensationalist phrasing ('It will cause death', 'Death by taxes') counts against civility.

civility.statement: Let’s get people into work in nursing and doctors by helping them pay off their student loans. It might not be a bad idea, because in 2008 John Key said, “We’re going to introduce voluntary bonding schemes based on student loan write-offs.”
civility.explanation: Acknowledges merit in an opponent's policy while still criticising its originality — substance-focused.

charisma.statement: When I was standing in Christchurch Central for the first time, he called me an ambulance chaser and I called him deeply offensive. I don’t chase ambulances anymore, and I’m sure he’s not deeply offensive anymore either. So I’m sure we’ll get on fine as well.
charisma.explanation: Light, warm gesture toward an opponent that seeks to establish a workable relationship across the aisle.

charisma.statement: I have seen nothing new from the National Party in this incoming Government.
charisma.explanation: Purely combative dismissal of the other side, not consensus-building.

charisma.statement: In fact, a lot of what the Key Government did was more progressive than what that Government’s proposing, so you should be utterly and totally ashamed of yourself.
charisma.explanation: Alienating, shaming framing that shuts down dialogue.

charisma.statement: Let’s get people into work in nursing and doctors by helping them pay off their student loans. It might not be a bad idea, because in 2008 John Key said, “We’re going to introduce voluntary bonding schemes based on student loan write-offs.”
charisma.explanation: Concedes a point to the opposing side ('It might not be a bad idea'), a small bridge-building acknowledgement amid the attack.

charisma.statement: So why don’t you have an original idea of your own to face the real problems that are facing New Zealand today: the problems of climate change, the problems of housing, the problems of the health system. Not rewarming, reheating, and retreading policies from 2008.
charisma.explanation: Framed as a combative challenge to opponents rather than an inclusive call to shared solutions.

specificity.statement: I have seen nothing new from the National Party in this incoming Government.
specificity.explanation: Sweeping characterisation with no detail on its own, though he goes on to support it with examples afterwards.

specificity.statement: The member for Banks Peninsula, Vanessa Weenink, GP, would have had people come into her practice with emphysema caused by smoking addiction. Will she vote for it or will she uphold her Hippocratic Oath that says “Do no harm.”?
specificity.explanation: Names a specific member and her profession and a concrete clinical scenario, though it ends in a rhetorical question.

specificity.statement: So why don’t you have an original idea of your own to face the real problems that are facing New Zealand today: the problems of climate change, the problems of housing, the problems of the health system. Not rewarming, reheating, and retreading policies from 2008.
specificity.explanation: Names the policy areas of concern (climate, housing, health) but offers no concrete alternative or mechanism.

rigor.statement: here’s one of the things that this Speech from the Throne says: “for the past several years the number of people employed in the public service has grown at a rate that has not been matched by a commensurate increase in the level of services provided to the public.” Does that sound like Christopher Luxon to you? No, that’s the 2008 Speech from the Throne.
rigor.explanation: Backs the 'recycled policy' claim with direct textual evidence by quoting the matching 2008 speech rather than mere assertion.

rigor.statement: a new Government department with a Minister of Regulation to cut regulatory costs, ha ha! It is laughable. You know, so you’re going to have an entire machinery to cut costs. That is absolutely ridiculous.
rigor.explanation: Points to a genuine irony (creating a department to reduce costs) but rests mostly on ridicule rather than developed evidence.

rigor.statement: As Richard Ekins said in the New Zealand Universities Law Review, it’s “reckless lawmaking”—it’s unconstitutional, it politicises the Public Service, and it threatens the rule of law.
rigor.explanation: Supports the criticism by citing a named academic source in a law review; an appeal to authority, but a legitimate and checkable one.

rigor.statement: It’s a neoliberal straight-jacket and it’s been roundly criticised by anyone who knows anything about it.
rigor.explanation: 'Anyone who knows anything about it' is an unsupported overgeneralisation and appeal to consensus, with no evidence cited here.

rigor.statement: The member for Banks Peninsula, Vanessa Weenink, GP, would have had people come into her practice with emphysema caused by smoking addiction. Will she vote for it or will she uphold her Hippocratic Oath that says “Do no harm.”?
rigor.explanation: Appeal to emotion and to a professional oath rather than evidence about the policy's effects.

veracity.statement: here’s one of the things that this Speech from the Throne says: “for the past several years the number of people employed in the public service has grown at a rate that has not been matched by a commensurate increase in the level of services provided to the public.” Does that sound like Christopher Luxon to you? No, that’s the 2008 Speech from the Throne.
veracity.explanation: Presents a verifiable textual parallel between the 2008 and 2023 throne speeches; plausible and checkable, though the precise wording match is asserted.

veracity.statement: that’s a corporate middle manager who himself said today, from that chair, that the Government’s “Under new management”.
veracity.explanation: Reductive framing of Luxon, who was a corporate CEO rather than a 'middle manager'; misleading characterisation.

veracity.statement: As Richard Ekins said in the New Zealand Universities Law Review, it’s “reckless lawmaking”—it’s unconstitutional, it politicises the Public Service, and it threatens the rule of law.
veracity.explanation: Accurately attributes a specific critique to a named author and publication; verifiable, though the characterisations are contestable.

veracity.statement: It’s utterly shameful that a party with a number of medical doctors in its ranks will vote to increase smoking.
veracity.explanation: 'Vote to increase smoking' is a misleading characterisation of repealing smokefree measures; directionally arguable but framed to overstate.

veracity.statement: This is a harmful piece of piece of legislation. It will cause death. Death by taxes is what we’ve got here.
veracity.explanation: Hyperbolic causal claim presented as fact without supporting evidence here.

veracity.statement: It’s nothing like KiwiBuild. KiwiBuild might not have built enough houses, but it didn’t send people to their graves.
veracity.explanation: 'KiwiBuild might not have built enough houses' is accurate — the scheme badly missed its build targets.

divination.statement: This is a harmful piece of piece of legislation. It will cause death. Death by taxes is what we’ve got here.
divination.explanation: Predicts the repeal will cause deaths; smoking-related harm is directionally plausible but 'death by taxes' is hyperbolic and the magnitude/timeframe is unspecified.

authenticity.statement: It’s nothing like KiwiBuild. KiwiBuild might not have built enough houses, but it didn’t send people to their graves.
authenticity.explanation: Candidly concedes his own party's KiwiBuild shortfall rather than defending it, showing consistency between word and the known record.

charisma.statement: We ran a campaign that inspired hope rather than fear, Mr Winston Peters.
charisma.explanation: Self-praising contrast that rallies her own side while taking a swipe at Peters; not consensus-building.

charisma.statement: the members opposite are not going to get away with their political violence lightly.
charisma.explanation: Combative us-vs-them framing, not consensus-building.

charisma.statement: We refuse to spend all our time talking about the next outrageous thing Mr Seymour or Mr Peters said instead of focusing on what matters to people’s daily lives.
charisma.explanation: Appeals to her own side's frustration more than bridging.

charisma.statement: Change will never come from turning on each other, but by turning towards each other.
charisma.explanation: Inclusive, unifying language inviting cooperation.

charisma.statement: They are not here for students, for single parents, or for people with disabilities. They’re here for people who make money from exploiting workers, renters, and our taiao.
charisma.explanation: Divisive framing that demonises the other side.

charisma.statement: It felt like it was written by an ad agency but, at the end of it, no one had a clue what they were actually selling—platitude after platitude—and that’s why they’re over there.
charisma.explanation: Crowd-pleasing attack, not persuasion of the unconvinced.

charisma.statement: I also want to thank those many people outside Parliament who have made possible what just happened: another peaceful transition of power, a contest of ideas, a battle of words rather than of weapons.
charisma.explanation: Gracious, unifying reflection on democracy that reaches beyond his own side.

charisma.statement: To Rawiri Waititi and Debbie Ngarewa-Packer, congratulations on leading your party back to this place in Parliament.
charisma.explanation: Cross-party graciousness toward opponents.

charisma.statement: some people aren’t what you’d call intellectual. Those people who aren’t so intellectual, they tend to be afraid of debate, and so they will call you racist and they’ll shout you down and they’ll try and block the motorway.
charisma.explanation: Alienating; pre-emptively dismisses critics rather than persuading.

charisma.statement: and also congratulations to Chris Luxon and David Seymour in the formation of this Government, and their political parties
charisma.explanation: Gracious acknowledgement of coalition partners; warm but directed at allies.

charisma.statement: you’re here to represent everybody as one people called New Zealanders, regardless of our DNA, our gender, our background, or our creeds.
charisma.explanation: Unity rhetoric, but deployed within a combative, divisive passage limiting its bridge-building effect.

charisma.statement: certainly not someone who is so decolonised he wears a cowboy hat—so decolonised he wears a cowboy hat.
charisma.explanation: Derisive crowd-pleasing line, not persuasion.

charisma.statement: Whether people agree or not, they’re entitled to hear, as Phil Collins sang, they’re entitled to “hear both sides of the story”. Not one side—both sides of the story.
charisma.explanation: Appeals to a fairness principle most can endorse, though embedded in a grievance against the media.

veracity.statement: a record—record—330,000 people voted Green
veracity.explanation: The Greens won roughly 330,000 party votes in 2023, a record for the party; broadly accurate.

veracity.statement: You are the reason we take our seats here as the third-largest party in Parliament with the biggest caucus we have ever had.
veracity.explanation: Greens were the third-largest party in 2023 with their largest-ever caucus of 15; accurate.

veracity.statement: It is a team that includes, for the first time ever, three Green Party electorate MPs.
veracity.explanation: The Greens won three electorate seats for the first time in 2023; accurate.

veracity.statement: Our mātāwaka caucus of Māori and Pasifika members of Parliament has grown from three members to seven.
veracity.explanation: Specific growth figure consistent with the expanded 2023 caucus.

veracity.statement: I hope Ministers remember these electorates when their Crown limos get stuck in the inevitable traffic jams resulting from his decision to defund the Let’s Get Wellington Moving programme.
veracity.explanation: The incoming government did move to defund/scale back Let's Get Wellington Moving; the factual basis is sound though framed combatively.

veracity.statement: Like raising the price of electric cars by ending the Clean Car Discount—but only after the PM himself had benefited from it.
veracity.explanation: Luxon reportedly benefited from the Clean Car Discount; the hypocrisy framing is roughly grounded though one-sided.

veracity.statement: We have won marriage equality, stopped the harms of conversion therapy, ended the logging of native timber, revitalised te reo through kōhanga reo and kura kaupapa, decriminalised abortion, and built thousands of warm, dry homes.
veracity.explanation: Accurate list of NZ reforms (marriage equality, conversion-therapy ban, abortion decriminalisation, etc.), though credited collectively.

veracity.statement: This Government is actually saying the truly nasty things out loud, like they care more for the ability for unhealthy programmes and rolling back Auahi Kore numbers and targets and aims.
veracity.explanation: The incoming government did move to repeal Smokefree (Auahi Kore) measures; the underlying factual claim is broadly accurate, the framing editorial.

veracity.statement: Per person, after inflation, he increased expenditure by 30 percent.
veracity.explanation: Real per-capita core Crown spending rose substantially 2017–2023; the ~30% figure is broadly defensible but depends on the measure used.

veracity.statement: And yet we had not 2,500 bureaucrats in the Ministry of Education but 4,400. That’s the growth under Labour and our results got worse.
veracity.explanation: Ministry of Education headcount did grow markedly; the specific figures are in the right range though framed to imply causation.

veracity.statement: The Programme for International Student Assessment examinations of 15-year-olds in science, literacy, and mathematics have been tested every three years since the turn of the century and we have just had the worst results ever for New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: NZ's 2022 PISA maths result was its lowest ever, but 'worst results ever' across all domains overstates the picture.

veracity.statement: Cameron Luxton, I think it’s probably true, has built more houses personally than the Government built in the six years that it had!
veracity.explanation: Hyperbole — KiwiBuild and state-build delivered thousands of homes; the claim is plainly false even hedged with 'probably'.

veracity.statement: We’re going to have a split-gas approach to methane and other greenhouse gases because we actually do follow the science, and the science says that methane has different characteristics from carbon dioxide.
veracity.explanation: Methane is a short-lived gas with different warming dynamics from CO2; the scientific distinction is sound, though policy implications are contested.

veracity.statement: the Green Party, who have not elected an MP who has studied science past high school in 12 years. The ACT Party has more scientists than the Green Party has elected, probably, in its history.
veracity.explanation: An unverified, hedged ('probably') claim about MPs' qualifications that is dubious and selectively framed.

veracity.statement: People pulled back from being landlords, and tenants were the ones that suffered, with record increases in rent over the six years that we’ve just seen with this Government.
veracity.explanation: Rents did rise substantially over the period; attributing it solely to Labour policy is misleading.

veracity.statement: the forward forecast for GDP for next year by the IMF has us at 159 in the world—just in front of Equatorial Guinea and doing less than 1 percent in terms of GDP
veracity.explanation: Misleading use of an IMF GDP-growth-rate ranking presented as a measure of economic standing; the framing distorts what the number means.

veracity.statement: as Dame Whina Cooper said, we signed the Treaty so that we could become one people.
veracity.explanation: A contested attribution and interpretation of the Treaty deployed to support a particular political reading.

veracity.statement: So $303,500 charity money to Te Pāti Māori, and what is going on when that can be allowed to survive in this country’s democracy?
veracity.explanation: Cites a specific donation figure tied to a real controversy, but the characterisation was contested and unproven at the time.

veracity.statement: only one party has ever taken all of the Māori seats off Labour, and you’re looking at it.
veracity.explanation: NZ First won all the Māori electorate seats in 1996; the claim is accurate.

veracity.statement: We survived the last campaign having been marginalised, Cinderella-ised, demonised by too many who were in the Public Interest Journalism Fund—paid off in the media.
veracity.explanation: Misleading — the PIJF funded journalism projects but did not 'pay off' journalists to attack NZ First.

veracity.statement: before the 2020 election, New Zealand First was attacked by the Serious Fraud Office (SFO)... when we beat the SFO—not once, but twice: before the election and after it
veracity.explanation: The SFO charged two individuals (not Peters or the party, which were not prosecuted); 'beat the SFO' overstates a case that did not target him personally.

veracity.statement: Because Mr Jackson has been the key voice in the Labour Party these last six years, and he’s sent them to their demise.
veracity.explanation: Overstated single-cause attribution of Labour's loss to one MP.

veracity.statement: We had plenty in Ōtara.
veracity.explanation: A factual rebuttal to Peters' claim the Greens held no public meetings; plausibly accurate but unverifiable from the text.

specificity.statement: Our mātāwaka caucus of Māori and Pasifika members of Parliament has grown from three members to seven.
specificity.explanation: Exact before/after numbers given.

specificity.statement: Change will never come from turning on each other, but by turning towards each other.

specificity.statement: We will be stronger, we will be tougher, and we will be more compassionate. We will be more staunch than we have ever been before

specificity.statement: Per person, after inflation, he increased expenditure by 30 percent.

specificity.statement: And yet we had not 2,500 bureaucrats in the Ministry of Education but 4,400. That’s the growth under Labour and our results got worse.

specificity.statement: I’m proud to be the first Minister for Regulation, with a Ministry for Regulation and a Regulatory Standards Bill setting out the principles of how you make laws that do make sense

specificity.statement: This Government is going to make sure that if you attack someone in a sole-charge workplace or a workplace attached to their dwelling house, then that’s an aggravating factor, or if you’re a member of a gang, you’re going away for longer

specificity.statement: the forward forecast for GDP for next year by the IMF has us at 159 in the world—just in front of Equatorial Guinea and doing less than 1 percent in terms of GDP

civility.statement: I hope Ministers remember these electorates when their Crown limos get stuck in the inevitable traffic jams resulting from his decision to defund the Let’s Get Wellington Moving programme.
civility.explanation: A pointed but fairly light jab tied to a policy decision.

civility.statement: Instead—instead—what we got is a random, visionless, and harmful grab bag of laws that are more about politicians’ pet projects and petty grievances than they are about addressing the challenges we face right now.

civility.statement: Like raising the price of electric cars by ending the Clean Car Discount—but only after the PM himself had benefited from it.

civility.statement: This is a cynical, dishonest policy that speaks to National’s gross incompetence in both climate policy and financial policy.

civility.statement: We refuse to spend all our time talking about the next outrageous thing Mr Seymour or Mr Peters said instead of focusing on what matters to people’s daily lives.
civility.explanation: Contains a jab but advocates focusing on substance over personalities.

civility.statement: They are not here for students, for single parents, or for people with disabilities. They’re here for people who make money from exploiting workers, renters, and our taiao.
civility.explanation: Imputes bad motives to opponents in stark us-vs-them terms.

civility.statement: It felt like it was written by an ad agency but, at the end of it, no one had a clue what they were actually selling—platitude after platitude—and that’s why they’re over there.
civility.explanation: Mocking dismissal of Davidson's speech rather than engaging its content.

civility.statement: I also want to thank those many people outside Parliament who have made possible what just happened: another peaceful transition of power, a contest of ideas, a battle of words rather than of weapons.

civility.statement: To Rawiri Waititi and Debbie Ngarewa-Packer, congratulations on leading your party back to this place in Parliament.

civility.statement: But you wouldn’t ask Rawiri Waititi if you wanted to know about hard work, would you?

civility.statement: So Grant Robertson and Chris Hipkins—thick as thieves; in fact, taxpayers might say that’s exactly what they were—were conniving together to get fewer kids going to school, learning less for more money.
civility.explanation: Calls opponents 'thieves' and ascribes deliberate intent to harm — personal and strawmanning.

civility.statement: Cameron Luxton, I think it’s probably true, has built more houses personally than the Government built in the six years that it had!
civility.explanation: A rhetorical jibe at the previous government's record rather than a personal insult.

civility.statement: the Green Party, who have not elected an MP who has studied science past high school in 12 years. The ACT Party has more scientists than the Green Party has elected, probably, in its history.
civility.explanation: Belittles opponents' credentials as a group.

civility.statement: some people aren’t what you’d call intellectual. Those people who aren’t so intellectual, they tend to be afraid of debate, and so they will call you racist and they’ll shout you down and they’ll try and block the motorway.
civility.explanation: Demeans opponents as unintelligent and afraid of debate — personal and strawmanning.

civility.statement: a health system that treats all New Zealanders equally, based on need, using good data—not lazy and bigoted discrimination based on race
civility.explanation: Characterises opponents' approach as 'lazy and bigoted', charged framing of a policy dispute.

civility.statement: I’ll just say that, if you’re going to go on camera and lie about your interactions with Brooke, you probably won’t be doing it again.
civility.explanation: Publicly accuses a named individual of lying with an implied threat.

civility.statement: and also congratulations to Chris Luxon and David Seymour in the formation of this Government, and their political parties
civility.explanation: Courteous congratulation.

civility.statement: certainly not someone who is so decolonised he wears a cowboy hat—so decolonised he wears a cowboy hat.
civility.explanation: Personal mockery of Rawiri Waititi's appearance and identity.

civility.statement: We survived the last campaign having been marginalised, Cinderella-ised, demonised by too many who were in the Public Interest Journalism Fund—paid off in the media.
civility.explanation: Sweeping insinuation against the media collectively.

civility.statement: This is the high point. It’s going down now... I know a bunch of losers when I see them. Any money you like—you’re going that way
civility.explanation: Calls opponents 'losers' — a personal insult.

civility.statement: Because Mr Jackson has been the key voice in the Labour Party these last six years, and he’s sent them to their demise.
civility.explanation: Blames a named individual for his party's defeat — a personal attack.

rigor.statement: Instead—instead—what we got is a random, visionless, and harmful grab bag of laws that are more about politicians’ pet projects and petty grievances than they are about addressing the challenges we face right now.
rigor.explanation: Sweeping characterisation asserted without supporting evidence.

rigor.statement: This is a cynical, dishonest policy that speaks to National’s gross incompetence in both climate policy and financial policy.
rigor.explanation: Conclusion of incompetence asserted, not evidenced.

rigor.statement: They are not here for students, for single parents, or for people with disabilities. They’re here for people who make money from exploiting workers, renters, and our taiao.
rigor.explanation: Sweeping motive attribution presented without evidence.

rigor.statement: Per person, after inflation, he increased expenditure by 30 percent.
rigor.explanation: Argues from a quantified fiscal figure, though presented selectively.

rigor.statement: And yet we had not 2,500 bureaucrats in the Ministry of Education but 4,400. That’s the growth under Labour and our results got worse.
rigor.explanation: Juxtaposes staffing growth with worse results, implying causation without establishing it.

rigor.statement: So Grant Robertson and Chris Hipkins—thick as thieves; in fact, taxpayers might say that’s exactly what they were—were conniving together to get fewer kids going to school, learning less for more money.
rigor.explanation: Strawman imputing that they intended fewer kids at school; no evidence of intent.

rigor.statement: We’re going to have a split-gas approach to methane and other greenhouse gases because we actually do follow the science, and the science says that methane has different characteristics from carbon dioxide.
rigor.explanation: Appeals to science and states a valid premise, but the policy conclusion is asserted rather than argued.

rigor.statement: the Green Party, who have not elected an MP who has studied science past high school in 12 years. The ACT Party has more scientists than the Green Party has elected, probably, in its history.
rigor.explanation: Credential-based dismissal verging on ad hominem, with no real evidence.

rigor.statement: People pulled back from being landlords, and tenants were the ones that suffered, with record increases in rent over the six years that we’ve just seen with this Government.
rigor.explanation: Asserts a causal chain from tenancy policy to rents; directionally arguable but contested and not evidenced.

rigor.statement: some people aren’t what you’d call intellectual. Those people who aren’t so intellectual, they tend to be afraid of debate, and so they will call you racist and they’ll shout you down and they’ll try and block the motorway.
rigor.explanation: Ad hominem and strawman about how opponents will respond.

rigor.statement: a health system that treats all New Zealanders equally, based on need, using good data—not lazy and bigoted discrimination based on race

rigor.statement: Whether people agree or not, they’re entitled to hear, as Phil Collins sang, they’re entitled to “hear both sides of the story”. Not one side—both sides of the story.
rigor.explanation: Invokes a reasonable principle of balance but supports it by anecdote rather than evidence.

strength.statement: I’m proud to be the first Minister for Regulation, with a Ministry for Regulation and a Regulatory Standards Bill setting out the principles of how you make laws that do make sense
strength.explanation: A new ministry and portfolio were actually established; the bill was still pending, so partial follow-through.

strength.statement: This Government is going to make sure that if you attack someone in a sole-charge workplace or a workplace attached to their dwelling house, then that’s an aggravating factor, or if you’re a member of a gang, you’re going away for longer
strength.explanation: Stated intent/commitment not yet delivered at time of speaking.

veracity.statement: Hamilton East is home to the world famous Hamilton Gardens, a 54-hectare public garden that was once a rubbish dump but now has 23 international gardens, 1.2 million visitors a year, and is in the top 1 percent of Tripadvisor's international travel experiences in the world.
veracity.explanation: A cluster of checkable factual claims about Hamilton Gardens; the themed-garden count, its origin as a former dump and its Tripadvisor standing are broadly accurate, though precise figures (hectares, visitor numbers) are hard to verify exactly.

veracity.statement: Long-term projections forecast this site to remove 65,000 long-haul truck journeys off the road—with an associated 66 percent reduction in carbon emissions for each container movement
veracity.explanation: Presents modelled projections as fact; the numbers are credible for the Ruakura development but are forecasts rather than measured results, with the basis not stated.

veracity.statement: Waters infrastructure and other essentials that address our estimated $200 billion infrastructure deficit will now start to be pragmatically addressed under this National-led coalition Government.
veracity.explanation: The $200 billion infrastructure deficit figure is in the ballpark of Infrastructure Commission estimates, so the headline number is defensible; the claim that it 'will now start to be addressed' is forward-looking assertion.

specificity.statement: Hamilton East is home to the world famous Hamilton Gardens, a 54-hectare public garden that was once a rubbish dump but now has 23 international gardens, 1.2 million visitors a year, and is in the top 1 percent of Tripadvisor's international travel experiences in the world.
specificity.explanation: Concrete and precise: names area, number of gardens, annual visitors and a ranking metric rather than a vague boast.

specificity.statement: Long-term projections forecast this site to remove 65,000 long-haul truck journeys off the road—with an associated 66 percent reduction in carbon emissions for each container movement
specificity.explanation: Quantified prediction with a figure for journeys removed and a percentage emissions reduction per movement.

specificity.statement: Waters infrastructure and other essentials that address our estimated $200 billion infrastructure deficit will now start to be pragmatically addressed under this National-led coalition Government.
specificity.explanation: Cites a dollar figure for the deficit but the action ('pragmatically addressed') has no mechanism, amount, or timeframe.

specificity.statement: We are moving on from the binary rates and development contribution models that have stymied our ability to unlock growth faster, and we will now enable special purpose vehicles, infrastructure funding and financing tools, tolls, overseas investment where appropriate, and value-capture models, which can be appropriately deployed on a case by case basis.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete funding mechanisms (special purpose vehicles, IFF tools, tolls, value-capture) rather than a vague promise to 'fund infrastructure', though without amounts or dates.

specificity.statement: I am so pleased we are proposing a national infrastructure agency that will have a long-term and evidence-based approach to what investments we need to make to take New Zealand forward, to support productivity, livability, and employment, not driven by ideology with unintended consequences and unmanaged financial waste.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific body (national infrastructure agency) and its remit, but offers no detail on scope, funding, or timing.

specificity.statement: I have chaired Te Whare Korowai, Hamilton Christian Nightshelter, and turned a non-existent business with a $2,000 start-up loan from my dad into a million-dollar enterprise.
specificity.explanation: Names organisations and gives a start figure and an end scale, more concrete than a generic 'I've worked hard' claim.

specificity.statement: To all the small-business owners out there, I am one too. I can relate. You are the backbone of the New Zealand economy. Help is coming.
specificity.explanation: 'Help is coming' is a slogan with no policy, mechanism, or timeframe attached.

specificity.statement: If employers are doing well, then employees have the opportunity to thrive also. We can't penalise one and not expect it to impact on the other.
specificity.explanation: A general principle with no concrete policy, figures, or mechanism.

specificity.statement: Hamilton is keen to see a sensible return to law and order, where people are made accountable for stealing and damaging property that is not theirs... not electronic bail with very little accountability or resource to support.
specificity.explanation: Identifies a target (electronic bail) but the alternative is framed as a 'sensible return to law and order' with no concrete measures.

specificity.statement: For those that can't fend for themselves, we absolutely need to provide the resources and supports to help them—assist them for as long as it takes. And we have a sacred duty to look after our most vulnerable and those that fall on hard times.
specificity.explanation: Expresses a value ('a sacred duty', 'as long as it takes') with no concrete resources, programmes, or measures named.

specificity.statement: I believe in less government, personal choice, and responsibility—a Government that sets up the right macro policy settings that enables success, and then gets out of the way.
specificity.explanation: An ideological statement of principle with no policy mechanism, figure, or timeframe.

divination.statement: Long-term projections forecast this site to remove 65,000 long-haul truck journeys off the road—with an associated 66 percent reduction in carbon emissions for each container movement
divination.explanation: A forecast about a long-term future outcome (truck journeys removed, emissions cut) attributed to projections; plausible and directionally supported for an inland port, but long-range and uncertain.

strength.statement: Waters infrastructure and other essentials that address our estimated $200 billion infrastructure deficit will now start to be pragmatically addressed under this National-led coalition Government.
strength.explanation: Stated intent by a brand-new government with nothing yet delivered; 'will now start to be addressed' is announcement rather than demonstrated follow-through.

strength.statement: We are moving on from the binary rates and development contribution models that have stymied our ability to unlock growth faster, and we will now enable special purpose vehicles, infrastructure funding and financing tools, tolls, overseas investment where appropriate, and value-capture models, which can be appropriately deployed on a case by case basis.
strength.explanation: A list of intended tools the government 'will now enable'; stated intent at the start of the term with delivery still to come.

strength.statement: I am so pleased we are proposing a national infrastructure agency that will have a long-term and evidence-based approach to what investments we need to make to take New Zealand forward, to support productivity, livability, and employment, not driven by ideology with unintended consequences and unmanaged financial waste.
strength.explanation: Describes a proposal ('we are proposing'), i.e. an announcement, not a delivered policy; no implementation demonstrated.

strength.statement: I have chaired Te Whare Korowai, Hamilton Christian Nightshelter, and turned a non-existent business with a $2,000 start-up loan from my dad into a million-dollar enterprise.
strength.explanation: Claims concrete personal follow-through — building a business from a small loan to a million-dollar enterprise — i.e. delivered results rather than aspiration, though it is a self-report.

rigor.statement: I am so pleased we are proposing a national infrastructure agency that will have a long-term and evidence-based approach to what investments we need to make to take New Zealand forward, to support productivity, livability, and employment, not driven by ideology with unintended consequences and unmanaged financial waste.
rigor.explanation: Advocates an 'evidence-based approach', but the contrast with the status quo as 'driven by ideology... and unmanaged financial waste' is asserted rather than evidenced.

rigor.statement: If employers are doing well, then employees have the opportunity to thrive also. We can't penalise one and not expect it to impact on the other.
rigor.explanation: A plausible economic intuition stated as a logical entailment, but it is asserted without evidence and leans on a simplified either/or framing of employer vs employee interests.

rigor.statement: I understand the challenges of local government and I have seen how central government has disrespected local government for the last six years with disingenuous engagement and how we must do it differently and work together to achieve good and sustainable outcomes.
rigor.explanation: The charge of 'disingenuous engagement' over six years is asserted from personal observation without specific evidence.

authenticity.statement: To all the small-business owners out there, I am one too. I can relate. You are the backbone of the New Zealand economy. Help is coming.
authenticity.explanation: His claim to relate to small-business owners is consistent with his stated record of having built his own business; words align with his actions.

authenticity.statement: I understand the challenges of local government and I have seen how central government has disrespected local government for the last six years with disingenuous engagement and how we must do it differently and work together to achieve good and sustainable outcomes.
authenticity.explanation: Drawn from his own experience as a Hamilton city councillor, so the perspective is consistent with his actual record.

authenticity.statement: I believe in less government, personal choice, and responsibility—a Government that sets up the right macro policy settings that enables success, and then gets out of the way.

forthrightness.statement: They will know in due course, and I’m sorry to say it, but I doubt that the member will be the first to know.

forthrightness.statement: On what we have agreed as a Government, that we will pursue a Treaty Principles Bill to select committee, and that’s as far as it will go.

forthrightness.statement: We have not committed to a referendum.
