forthrightness.statement: School lunches will continue to be funded; we just want to make sure that the system is more effective and that wastage is removed, and if there's a better way to deliver it at lower cost, we'll look to do that.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to choose the better use of $2.9 billion (landlord tax cuts vs school lunches/fees-free/prescriptions); ignores the comparison and talks only about school-lunch efficiency.

forthrightness.statement: what we are interested in is actually delivering on our climate change goals—that's actually what matters here. The means by which we deliver those goals may differ from the previous administration, but our commitment is incredibly strong to deliver those commitments.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked the specific questions of whether the MBIE just transitions unit was wound down and how many climate jobs are at risk; answers neither, offering only a general statement of commitment.

forthrightness.statement: that's just not true. There has been no reduction in the funding in the disabilities budget compared to what the previous Government funded in the year before, and, further, we have made a commitment to increase funding this year
forthrightness.explanation: Asked on what date he first became aware of the cut to entitlements; gives no date and instead disputes the premise.

forthrightness.statement: As I said, we've been working to the previous Government's budget. There has been an overspend and an overrun. There has been more money put into the ministry for this year, and there will also be more money put into the Budget 2024 process as well.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether Penny Simmonds requested a pre-Budget funding commitment for Whaikaha; does not answer yes or no and reverts to budget talking points.

forthrightness.statement: I have complete confidence in the Minister. By her own admission and that of her ministry, she's apologised for the confusion and the anxiety—that those changes were poorly communicated and poorly consulted on—but we've made changes to the process going forward, and that's a good thing.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked what it says about his confidence that he now requires the Minister to take decisions to Cabinet; directly affirms confidence but reframes the Cabinet requirement as a positive rather than engaging the implied loss of trust.

forthrightness.statement: I do agree: housing has been an abject failure in this country after six years of the previous administration. What we have to do is increase supply of private houses, increase the supply of rental properties available, and increase the supply of social and State housing available as well. We've got plans to deal with all three.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked specifically what steps would increase publicly owned rental housing; partially agrees with the report but answers with a general three-part supply line rather than steps on public housing.

forthrightness.statement: Again, I don't know how to explain this any differently to the member but it's an "and, and, and".
forthrightness.explanation: Asked about reliance on the accommodation supplement by ~350,000 people; repeats the 'and, and, and' supply formula without engaging the concern.

forthrightness.statement: We are committed to making sure that we build more houses in general in this country. That has been an absolute disaster under the previous administration. This Government takes getting houses built seriously.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked why he prioritises tax cuts for landlords over building public housing; does not address the trade-off and pivots to a general building commitment and an attack on the predecessor.

forthrightness.statement: It was a phantom policy, and I tell you a really big difference: this money—this cold, hard cash—goes direct into the bank accounts of parents. There is no middleman or -woman; this is real cost of living relief for New Zealand families.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether her package gives hundreds of millions less than the scrapped previous policy; disputes the comparison as hypothetical rather than conceding or quantifying it.

forthrightness.statement: Yes. This policy has been fully funded, with $723 million provided over the forecast period, and the Budget will reflect that. I think it's really important that members of this House understand this fact: we have costed this policy based on 100 percent uptake, because we want every single family in New Zealand who qualifies for this policy to know that the funding is there for them.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers whether funding has been set aside — yes, with a figure and the costing assumption.

forthrightness.statement: John Key would be very unhappy to hear the member opposite mischaracterise his comments in that way. And I would put to her that we should have honour in this House with comments that we make and how we represent others.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether she agrees with John Key's reported concern about funding cuts; does not address the substance and instead disputes the characterisation.

forthrightness.statement: If the member wishes to ask questions about the disability services portfolio, she should put them on notice to that Minister.
forthrightness.explanation: Declines to engage the substantive question about diabetes-monitor funding, redirecting it to another Minister.

forthrightness.statement: We have previously made clear our commitment to ensure that there is more funding available for front-line services.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether she will meet Treasury's specific $2.8 billion estimate to maintain services; gives a general assurance of 'more funding' without addressing the figure.

forthrightness.statement: I am intending on consulting widely about the Holidays Act changes, and I look forward to the member being part of that consultation.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to guarantee no employee will lose entitlements under her changes; gives no guarantee and pivots to a promise of consultation.

forthrightness.statement: Yes, I do stand by my statement. Diabetes is a serious health condition affecting many New Zealanders, and I'm advised that avenues such as Health New Zealand and Pharmac support New Zealanders to gain access to funding for insulin pumps and monitors. The expectation is that health devices to address health conditions are dealt with under Vote Health.
forthrightness.explanation: Engages the question by affirming her statement and explaining the rationale (devices funded via Vote Health), though it leaves the gap for those previously funded through disability support.

forthrightness.statement: It needs to be very, very clear that there has been no cut in funding. There has been additional funding given to get Whaikaha through to the end of the year... There is no cut in funding.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether she agrees with David Seymour that the cuts have gone too far; ignores the quote and repeats 'no cut in funding'.

forthrightness.statement: I'm not aware of the individual case, but the member has answered the question herself, if she said that it met the guidelines of the funding. Therefore, if it meets the guidelines of the funding, it should be funded.
forthrightness.explanation: Gives a conditional answer (if it meets the guidelines it should be funded) but sidesteps the individual case by saying she is unaware of it.

forthrightness.statement: There are currently about 22 percent of New Zealanders who actually belong to ethnic communities. However, you know, at a time when New Zealand is facing a cost of living crisis, agencies have been asked to identify where they can make savings or make changes in order to deliver savings. Decisions related to staffing numbers at the ministry are operational and Budget sensitive.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to reconcile her growth statement with a 14% staff reduction; deflects by calling staffing 'operational and Budget sensitive' without addressing the contradiction.

forthrightness.statement: I don't have responsibility for Mr Seymour's comments. However, I feel that the Ministry for Ethnic Communities does an amazing job, and I support them 100 percent.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether she agrees with Seymour's disparaging comment and whether the cuts move toward abolishing the ministry; answers neither, only voicing general support.

forthrightness.statement: In, I think, my second answer to the second supplementary, I mentioned all of those groups. So, yes.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether consultation would follow Trade for All principles (consulting Māori, SMEs, women, etc.); gives a direct affirmative, though without elaboration.

forthrightness.statement: There are no changes to the policy apart from the fact that we're funding it an extra half a million dollars a year to make sure that there is equal access to as many women as possible.
forthrightness.explanation: Responds to a rhetorical gotcha about which students menstruate by clarifying the policy is unchanged and adding the funding figure.

civility.statement: we are going to give low and middle income working people tax relief—that's something that the Labour Party and the Green Party used to believe in; they were people that they used to support, but they don't seem to care about it anymore
civility.explanation: Imputes that opponents no longer 'care' about low- and middle-income people — a character jab rather than policy critique.

civility.statement: I do agree: housing has been an abject failure in this country after six years of the previous administration. What we have to do is increase supply of private houses, increase the supply of rental properties available, and increase the supply of social and State housing available as well. We've got plans to deal with all three.
civility.explanation: 'Abject failure' is harsh but aimed at the previous government's policy record, not a personal attack.

civility.statement: Again, I don't know how to explain this any differently to the member but it's an "and, and, and".
civility.explanation: Mildly condescending ('I don't know how to explain this any differently') but not a personal attack.

civility.statement: Does he stand by his statement that tax deductibility changes will reduce rents, or would he like to revise that in light of advice that his Government has received that rents are primarily driven by household income and relative supply and demand for housing?
civility.explanation: Pointed but engages the substance of the policy claim rather than the person.

civility.statement: What is a better use of $2.9 billion: tax cuts for landlords, or retention of food in schools, expanding fees-free tertiary education, and retaining free prescriptions, with money left over?
civility.explanation: Frames the choice tendentiously ('tax cuts for landlords') but stays on policy spending priorities.

civility.statement: Does he stand by the statements from his Minister for Regulation that risks to endangered native dolphins' lives are the equivalent to driving a car, and, if so, are we to expect that this Government will wind back marine protection in line with their war on nature?
civility.explanation: 'War on nature' is sensationalist framing, and the characterisation of Seymour's remark was disputed by him on a point of order.

civility.statement: Is the Prime Minister aware that the advice the member alluded to about the effects of mortgage interest deductibility on rental housing continued on to say that in the long run, reductions in rents could be expected, and would he advise members, as a matter of general practice, to read all the evidence instead of selectively quoting some?
civility.explanation: Contains a dig about selective quoting but is anchored in the substance of the advice.

civility.statement: I've made no such statement. However, some people are unable to understand the point of an analogy about risk, rather than literally suggesting dolphins would drive cars.
civility.explanation: Legitimately corrects the record but adds a belittling aside ('some people are unable to understand').

civility.statement: Will the Government actually allow for the FamilyBoost policy in the costings it does in its Budget, and is that a general policy of the Government—to actually put aside money to fund the things it promises the public—or will this Government simply make it up and hope to lose the election so someone else can inherit the problem?
civility.explanation: Sarcastic framing ('make it up and hope to lose the election') overshadows an otherwise legitimate question about whether the policy is funded.

civility.statement: Has the Prime Minister received any reports about the gulf or gap he's going to have to fill, having inherited a 100,000-homes promise that ended up with 2,000 being built by the administration that the original questioner came from?
civility.explanation: A pointed partisan jab, but built on the predecessor's policy record rather than a personal insult.

civility.statement: We should absolutely acknowledge the atrocity that was the Hamas attack on Israel. We should also acknowledge Israel's right to defend itself, as I did, as our Prime Minister, when that happened. But there are limits to that right to self-defence.
civility.explanation: Measured, respects competing claims, focuses on principle rather than attacking opponents.

civility.statement: Waiting until the conditions for a ceasefire exist before calling for one simply lacks moral courage, and it is not consistent with the long-held principled position that New Zealand has taken.
civility.explanation: 'Lacks moral courage' is sharp but aimed at the Government's policy stance, with an argued basis.

civility.statement: It was a phantom policy, and I tell you a really big difference: this money—this cold, hard cash—goes direct into the bank accounts of parents. There is no middleman or -woman; this is real cost of living relief for New Zealand families.
civility.explanation: 'Phantom policy' dismisses the predecessor's plan, but as a critique of the policy's deliverability rather than a personal attack.

civility.statement: John Key would be very unhappy to hear the member opposite mischaracterise his comments in that way. And I would put to her that we should have honour in this House with comments that we make and how we represent others.
civility.explanation: Impugns the member's 'honour' rather than engaging the quoted comment, a deflection toward character.

civility.statement: Over the last six years, employers would be forgiven for feeling like they have been pitted against workers, but I believe that the frustrations both employers and workers are facing are connected.
civility.explanation: Constructive framing focused on shared frustrations rather than attacking opponents.

civility.statement: Is he aware of the finding of the report that building good quality public housing at scale and pace can save Government spending in the long term through reduced need for landlord subsidies and through savings in health budgets, and, if so, does this suggest that increasing the supply of public housing is consistent with this Government's stated commitment to social investment?
civility.explanation: Substantive, policy-focused question without personal attack.

charisma.statement: we are going to give low and middle income working people tax relief—that's something that the Labour Party and the Green Party used to believe in; they were people that they used to support, but they don't seem to care about it anymore
charisma.explanation: Rallies his own side by contrasting against opponents rather than seeking common ground.

charisma.statement: We should absolutely acknowledge the atrocity that was the Hamas attack on Israel. We should also acknowledge Israel's right to defend itself, as I did, as our Prime Minister, when that happened. But there are limits to that right to self-defence.
charisma.explanation: Acknowledges multiple sides' legitimate concerns before drawing a line — bridging rather than purely combative.

charisma.statement: Over the last six years, employers would be forgiven for feeling like they have been pitted against workers, but I believe that the frustrations both employers and workers are facing are connected.
charisma.explanation: Frames employers and workers as having connected interests, an attempt at a unifying rather than divisive narrative.

veracity.statement: The previous administration loaded costs up on landlords and they got passed through to renters with higher rents—$170 more on average every single week.
veracity.explanation: The '$170 a week' figure is a contested attribution of all rent increases to one policy; rent rises had multiple drivers, so the causal claim is overstated.

veracity.statement: that's just not true. There has been no reduction in the funding in the disabilities budget compared to what the previous Government funded in the year before, and, further, we have made a commitment to increase funding this year
veracity.explanation: Distinguishes top-line funding from the tightening of entitlements that families experienced — partly true but elides the specific changes that prompted the question.

veracity.statement: Has the Prime Minister received any reports about the gulf or gap he's going to have to fill, having inherited a 100,000-homes promise that ended up with 2,000 being built by the administration that the original questioner came from?
veracity.explanation: References the KiwiBuild 100,000-home promise against a far smaller number actually built — directionally accurate, though the exact figure is rounded.

veracity.statement: Three-quarters of Gaza's 2.2 million people are internally displaced; more than a million people are crammed into Rafah, a tiny sliver of land which now has a population five times what it was before the war.
veracity.explanation: Population and displacement figures broadly match UN reporting at the time.

veracity.statement: Labour called for a ceasefire back in November. It was the right thing to do then, and it is absolutely the right thing for us to be doing now.
veracity.explanation: Labour did publicly call for a ceasefire in late 2023; the factual claim about their prior position holds.

veracity.statement: In 2016, under the then Minister of Foreign Affairs Murray McCully, New Zealand sponsored a United Nations Security Council resolution reaffirming that Israeli settlements in the Palestinian territory, occupied by Israel since 1967, constitute a flagrant violation of international law
veracity.explanation: Accurately describes NZ's co-sponsorship of UNSC Resolution 2334 (2016) and its language on settlements.

veracity.statement: Overnight, the United Nations Security Council passed a resolution calling for an immediate ceasefire for the month of Ramadan. Significantly, for the first time, the United States has not exercised its veto.
veracity.explanation: Accurately reports UNSC Resolution 2728 (March 2024) and the US abstention rather than a veto.

veracity.statement: An estimated 21,000 low to middle income families will qualify for the maximum reimbursement of $975 every three months, and, in total, FamilyBoost will help support more than 140,000 children and their families.
veracity.explanation: Presented as estimates; the headline reach figure is broad and uptake projections later proved optimistic.

veracity.statement: According to the OECD, childcare costs in New Zealand are among the highest in the world—at 37 percent of household income.
veracity.explanation: Broadly consistent with OECD net-childcare-cost comparisons for some household types, though the single 37% figure depends on the specific measure used.

veracity.statement: I understand that 90 percent of contractors report that they are satisfied, or very satisfied, with their jobs, and that they would prefer to continue being self-employed, rather than to have a paid job working for someone else.
veracity.explanation: Cites a satisfaction statistic without source; the figure is plausible but unverified and hedged ('I understand').

veracity.statement: The previous Government's Holidays Act Taskforce began work in 2018, but were not able to deliver on changes by the end of their term in Government.
veracity.explanation: Accurate: the Holidays Act Taskforce was established in 2018 and reforms were not legislated under the previous government.

veracity.statement: It needs to be very, very clear that there has been no cut in funding. There has been additional funding given to get Whaikaha through to the end of the year... There is no cut in funding.
veracity.explanation: Top-line funding may not have fallen, but the statement glosses over the tightening of what families could spend funding on — the change that prompted the question.

veracity.statement: On 7 March, the Aged Care Commissioner released her first report, titled Amplifying the voices of older people across Aotearoa New Zealand. The report has drawn on engagement with thousands of people from our important older communities alongside their families, whānau, carers, and service providers.
veracity.explanation: A verifiable, accurate description of an actual published report.

veracity.statement: There are currently about 22 percent of New Zealanders who actually belong to ethnic communities. However, you know, at a time when New Zealand is facing a cost of living crisis, agencies have been asked to identify where they can make savings or make changes in order to deliver savings. Decisions related to staffing numbers at the ministry are operational and Budget sensitive.
veracity.explanation: The ~22% ethnic-communities figure is in the right range, though such proportions depend on definitions and census timing.

veracity.statement: The UAE is a top-20 export market for New Zealand and our largest market in the Middle East, with exports totalling over $1 billion last year.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with trade data: the UAE was NZ's largest Middle East market with exports around the billion-dollar mark.

veracity.statement: 73 percent of New Zealand's trade will be covered by trade agreements once the EU-NZ free-trade agreement (FTA) enters into force on 1 May.
veracity.explanation: Coverage figure broadly aligns with MFAT estimates following the EU FTA.

veracity.statement: A study by the University of Otago estimated that up to 95,000 young women could be missing school because of a lack of access to period products.
veracity.explanation: Cites a real Otago study, but 'up to 95,000' is the upper-bound estimate presented as the headline figure.

veracity.statement: Is he concerned, then, at the ability of the private rental market to provide New Zealanders with affordable housing when almost 350,000 people have to access the accommodation supplement because private rents are too high?
veracity.explanation: The accommodation supplement recipient figure is in the right ballpark for the period.

authenticity.statement: The previous administration loaded costs up on landlords and they got passed through to renters with higher rents—$170 more on average every single week.
authenticity.explanation: Casts the Government as 'on the side of renters' while the policy under question is restoring tax deductibility for landlords — a tension between framing and action.

authenticity.statement: Labour called for a ceasefire back in November. It was the right thing to do then, and it is absolutely the right thing for us to be doing now.
authenticity.explanation: Points to a consistent, pre-existing position (November call for a ceasefire) that matches the current stance.

rigor.statement: According to the OECD, childcare costs in New Zealand are among the highest in the world—at 37 percent of household income.

rigor.explanation: Uses survey-style evidence to justify the policy direction, though the source is unspecified.

rigor.statement: A study by the University of Otago estimated that up to 95,000 young women could be missing school because of a lack of access to period products.

rigor.explanation: Connects report evidence (long-term savings) to the Government's own 'social investment' framing to construct a coherent argument.

divination.explanation: Predicts the EU-NZ FTA entering into force on 1 May — by this point near-certain, the deal having gained Royal assent.

divination.statement: Other countries are progressing trade negotiations with the UAE—including Australia, who are expected to conclude a deal by the end of this year
divination.explanation: Forecasts Australia concluding a UAE deal by year-end 2024 — plausible given negotiations under way, but contingent on the talks landing.

strength.statement: I’ve spoken to scores and scores of my counterparts on this issue on behalf of New Zealand. I’ve spoken to my counterpart in Indonesia, in person, when we visited Indonesia just recently—the biggest Muslim country in the world.
strength.explanation: Describes ongoing diplomatic engagement; activity is real but follow-through/outcome unclear — process rather than delivered result.

specificity.statement: I’ve spoken to scores and scores of my counterparts on this issue on behalf of New Zealand. I’ve spoken to my counterpart in Indonesia, in person, when we visited Indonesia just recently—the biggest Muslim country in the world.
specificity.explanation: Names Indonesia and an in-person visit, but 'scores and scores' of counterparts is vague with no outcomes.

specificity.statement: New Zealand has long—this Government—advocated for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire in Gaza, leading to a lasting, sustainable peace. We welcome the UN Security Council’s resolution, overnight, demanding an immediate ceasefire. We have called on all parties to immediately comply with this resolution.
specificity.explanation: References a concrete resolution and a clear ask, but no detail on what compliance steps NZ will pursue.

specificity.statement: On the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) investigation, well, New Zealand did not suspend its aid. No. What we did was ensure that we funded the World Food Programme, the International Committee of the Red Cross, and the United Nations Children’s Fund, UNICEF, and kept the funding going until the next tranche is due on 1 June.
specificity.explanation: Names three specific agencies and a concrete date (1 June) for the next funding tranche.

specificity.statement: this is the Government that deputed as terrorists Israeli settlers because of their behaviour, not just Hamas but Israeli settlers as well.
specificity.explanation: Points to a concrete category of action but without naming the actual mechanism (travel bans) or scope.

specificity.statement: New Zealand is committed to supporting the critical humanitarian response in Gaza, and to date we have channelled $15 million through the International Committee of the Red Cross, the World Food Programme, and the United Nations Children’s Fund.
specificity.explanation: Gives a precise figure ($15m) and names the three delivery agencies.

specificity.statement: Over 32,000—that’s how many people have been killed in Gaza, with 13,000 of those people being children and around 8,400 being women.
specificity.explanation: Precise breakdown by total, children, and women.

specificity.statement: We also need to urgently create a special visa for Palestinian New Zealanders to bring their families to safety, and to back this up with diplomatic support to get them out of Gaza.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete mechanism (special visa category plus diplomatic support) but no numbers or timeframe.

specificity.statement: On 7 October 2023, Hamas attacked Israel. They killed over 1,200 people. They took hundreds hostage, of which, it is suspected, less than 100 still live in captivity, held in tunnels, held in basements
specificity.explanation: Concrete date, casualty figure, and hostage estimate.

specificity.statement: that is why I am proud the New Zealand coalition Government has declared not only Hamas’ so-called military wing but also its fake political wing to be a terrorist entity.
specificity.explanation: Identifies the specific action (full designation) but no date or detail.

specificity.explanation: Provides specific casualty and injury figures for both sides.

specificity.statement: every person in this world has the right to live in freedom and safety, and we need an urgent, lasting, permanent ceasefire now.
specificity.explanation: A general principle plus a broad call; no mechanism, figure, or concrete step.

specificity.statement: why is it that an Amendment Paper was used to manifest those commitments from the election as a precursor to the Budget with regard to tax deductibility, but not those changes that relate to income tax changes?... an Amendment Paper, particularly one that proposes quite substantive changes, has not been before a select committee process, and this bill largely operates retrospectively
specificity.explanation: Detailed, precise procedural question identifying Part 1 vs Part 2, the Amendment Paper, and the select-committee gap.

specificity.statement: the reality is that we have a very busy programme within the coalition Government, in the large number of actions that we are working our way through... The personal income tax changes that we have signalled very clearly that we are going to make are subject to the Budget process, and hence will be coming through that process. The other aspects from our assessment were appropriate to go through this bill, and we’re comfortable with that.
specificity.explanation: Gives one concrete reason (Budget process) but otherwise vague ('busy programme', 'from our assessment').

specificity.statement: the high-wealth individuals research project, because that revealed a startling disparity between the effective tax rates by the super-wealthy compared with other New Zealanders... most New Zealanders paying an average tax rate of something like around 22 percent versus around 8 percent for those who are super-rich.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific report and gives concrete comparative effective-rate figures.
