rigor.statement: Does the Minister, then, disagree with the consistent advice from the Treasury that we would have a more productive economy with the implementation of a capital gains tax, fixing the incentives which currently see far too much money flowing into bidding up house prices?
rigor.explanation: Appeals to Treasury/IMF advice and identifies a specific mechanism (capital misallocation into housing) to support the CGT case.

rigor.statement: Why did she decide to increase the level of cuts required of Whaikaha to 7.5 percent rather than the 6.5 percent she campaigned on, and is requiring of other agencies, given she received a briefing from the Minister of disabilities in late 2023?
rigor.explanation: Builds a factual case (campaign figure, differential treatment, prior briefing) to press an apparent inconsistency.

strength.statement: These include delivering tax reductions to provide cost of living relief to New Zealanders who have seen no change in personal income tax rates and thresholds for 14 years. Can I reinforce to members that those tax reductions will be funded by reprioritisations, savings, and new revenue measures. This package of measures will not add to debt.
strength.explanation: A concrete commitment to tax reductions that was in train but not yet enacted as of this date — stated intent with delivery pending.

strength.statement: Since 7 October, we've received 71 applications from Palestinian nationals around the world. Of these, we believe 15 applications are from people who, to the best of our knowledge, may have been in Gaza at the time of their application or shortly before lodging. We've issued seven visas to people who are immediate family members of New Zealand citizens or permanent residents... The New Zealand Government has also provided a total of $15 million in humanitarian assistance, including through the World Food Programme, UNICEF, and the International Committee of the Red Cross.
strength.explanation: Points to delivered action — visas issued and $15m in aid disbursed through named agencies — though modest relative to the demand.

strength.statement: This legislation is being passed in a record time of seven weeks so that New Zealand businesses can realise benefits as soon as possible. In particular, this early entry into force date means our kiwifruit industry will see $43 million worth of tariff savings this year. We also estimate that 35,000 tonnes of onions will be exported to the EU after 1 May, saving our onion exporters $3 million per season.
strength.explanation: Describes actually completing the legislative process to bring the EU FTA into force — a concrete delivered/near-delivered outcome, not just an announcement.

strength.statement: Today, I'm pleased to announce a new mental health and addiction peer support service in hospital emergency departments (EDs). The service will see peer support workers embedded within EDs to provide additional support for those with mental health needs and their families in a time of need.
strength.explanation: An announcement of a new service rather than demonstrated delivery — intent stated, implementation yet to be shown.

strength.statement: Today, I also announced a $1 million workforce fund over two years that's been set up to provide a level 4 New Zealand certificate in health and wellbeing peer support training and specific training for working in EDs.
strength.explanation: A funded commitment that has been 'set up' but whose delivery (trained workforce) is still prospective.

strength.statement: I recently announced the introduction of the Courts (Remote Participation) Amendment Bill to Parliament, contributing to the Government's 100-day commitment to enable more virtual participation in court proceedings. This bill enables the use of audiovisual link technology, which proved invaluable during the COVID-19 pandemic to support access to justice and a safer option to attend court for victims.
strength.explanation: Reports introducing the bill against a stated 100-day commitment — a delivered legislative step, though enactment is pending.

strength.statement: It is the Government's position that education and every other utility should be used to combat racism in our society, and we're going to go to the ends of the earth to ensure that that happens.
strength.explanation: Sweeping aspiration to combat racism with no specific policy action attached.

strength.statement: These changes include restoring interest deductibility for residential investment properties and reducing the brightline test from 10 years to two. ... Changes to the brightline test will come into force from 1 July 2024 alongside the gambling duty changes. Interest deductibility will be restored in stages, with 80 percent of a deduction allowed from 1 April 2024 and 100 percent from 1 April 2025.
strength.explanation: Concrete legislative changes enacting coalition commitments via an Amendment Paper, with delivery scheduled and largely under way.

strength.statement: Yes, the Government is ruthlessly focused on rebuilding the economy and reducing the cost of living. That is why we are axing the Auckland regional fuel tax (RFT) on 30 June this year, and why the transport Minister is in Auckland today outlining the coalition Government's plan to get Auckland moving again.
strength.explanation: Points to a scheduled, concrete repeal of the RFT — committed with a firm date, delivery pending the date.

charisma.statement: When the economy is going well, they say tax reduction must not happen because it will be inflationary; when the economy is not going well, they say tax reduction must not happen because we can't afford it. The truth is that members opposite believe the Government can spend money better than New Zealanders can on their own families; well, I disagree.
charisma.explanation: Rallies her own side with an us-vs-them framing of 'members opposite'; no attempt to persuade the unconvinced.

charisma.statement: I'd like to recognise the work done by the Foreign Affairs, Defence and Trade Committee and members from all parties, who worked collaboratively to speed up the process while still hearing the views from all submitted. I'd also like to recognise the considerable efforts of the Hon Damien O'Connor and all parties in this House for agreeing to progress the ratification of the EU FTA legislation so quickly.
charisma.explanation: Generous cross-party acknowledgement, crediting all parties and a Labour opponent by name — consensus-building and inclusive.

charisma.statement: It's no wonder that member is no longer the Minister responsible. But what I would like to do is thank him for his hard work on an agreement that will help deliver for all New Zealanders, and recognise how hard it must be to be a Minister for Trade in a Labour Government.
charisma.explanation: Mixes a courteous thanks with point-scoring at the questioner's expense, undercutting any bridge-building.

charisma.statement: Trade Ministers Tim Groser, Todd McClay, David Parker, Damien O'Connor, and now Todd McClay again have all had input into the formation and delivery of this agreement... I recognise the work of Damien O'Connor and I thank him for that. And whilst not all parts of this agreement have met the level of aspiration that everybody in New Zealand has, this House and Damien O'Connor can go away after this enters into force, knowing that we have helped New Zealanders.
charisma.explanation: Explicitly credits trade ministers across both major parties over a decade and singles out a Labour opponent for thanks — strongly consensus-building and magnanimous.

charisma.statement: Can I ask the Minister of Finance as to whether she has received, apart from the 100,000 ways of spending the taxpayers' money, one idea from over there on how to make the taxpayers' money?
charisma.explanation: Plays to his own benches with an us-vs-them framing of 'over there'.

divination.statement: Yes, I do, and the Minister has a very important job to do, fixing a system that is, frankly, not fit for purpose which she inherited from that member's previous Government, and I am confident she's going to do exactly that.
divination.explanation: Predicts the Minister will fix the system — plausible but unverifiable forecast about future performance.

divination.statement: I can tell members that there will be personal income tax relief in the Budget. This tax relief—and Mr Parker will be pleased to hear this—will be funded from within the operating allowance, and the operating allowance will be less than the $3.5 billion allowance indicated in the half-year update. This means the Government will not be borrowing extra to pay for tax relief, and it means tax relief will not be adding to inflationary pressures.
divination.explanation: Predicts the tax relief will not add to inflationary pressures — plausible but contestable and unverified.

divination.statement: The legacy we inherited of elevated, lazy spending will take several Budgets to fix, but the first steps will be taken in Budget 2024.
divination.explanation: Predicts it will take several Budgets to fix — directional and plausible but vague.

divination.statement: What is his response to the fact that this effective cut to the minimum wage will increase child poverty rates, given that 64 percent of families in poverty are in work?
divination.explanation: Predicts the wage decision will increase child poverty — directionally supported, magnitude uncertain.

divination.statement: We expect that around 4,500 extra New Zealanders will benefit from this boost.
divination.explanation: Forecasts ~4,500 additional beneficiaries — a quantified but uncertain projection.

divination.statement: State Highway 1 across the Brynderwyns will open tonight until 2 April, for the Easter weekend, with work currently under way to ensure the resilience of this critical route being paused to allow holidaymakers to travel north.
divination.explanation: Near-term, falsifiable prediction that the road will open tonight until 2 April.

divination.statement: Already, 113,000 cubic metres of dirt has been moved of the 145,000 cubic metres which need to be moved, and there is more work to be done. It will be open over Easter and completed in May.
divination.explanation: Predicts completion in May — concrete and checkable but subject to slippage.

divination.statement: There is a great opportunity for New Zealand to capture an even larger share of a sector projected to reach—and wait for this—US$1 trillion by 2040.
divination.explanation: Cites a forecast of US$1 trillion by 2040 — a long-range projection with wide uncertainty.

civility.statement: Yes, I do, and the Minister has a very important job to do, fixing a system that is, frankly, not fit for purpose which she inherited from that member's previous Government, and I am confident she's going to do exactly that.
civility.explanation: Defends a colleague while pinning blame on the previous Government; pointed but not a personal attack.

civility.statement: As we have said, she didn't bring it to Cabinet, and as a result there was no Cabinet discussion. That is something the Minister has apologised for, and she will do going forward.
civility.explanation: Acknowledges a mistake plainly without attacking anyone.

civility.statement: I disagree completely. All we're saying is that all Ministers, on their portfolios, need to bring forward to Cabinet conversations around any changes to front-line services that are major and significant and that will impact New Zealanders. That didn't happen in this case. The Minister has admitted that up front, has learnt from that experience, and we're moving forward.
civility.explanation: Policy/process focused, no personal attack.

civility.statement: Yes. What I support, though, is actually growing our economy and making sure that we do everything we can to end the wasteful spending so we can protect front-line services, doing everything we can to give tax relief to low and middle income working families, and to make sure that we have growth in our economy. That's what we're focused on.
civility.explanation: Engages on policy substance without personal attack.

civility.statement: Could I ask the Prime Minister as to whether his Government is going to be guided by what may be described as the Roosevelt principle: that we'll try our hardest but we may not always get it right, but we'll keep on trying, rather than saying that we're perfect, never apologise, and say that we're the podium of truth?
civility.explanation: Gentle, principle-based question without personal attack.

civility.statement: Spending on front-line services will be reprioritised, despite some people practically fainting at the thought that the Government could do things differently and more effectively, and the Budget will deliver on Government policy commitments, including many of those in the coalition agreements.
civility.explanation: Mild mockery ('practically fainting') of opponents, but framed around policy.

civility.statement: The legacy we inherited of elevated, lazy spending will take several Budgets to fix, but the first steps will be taken in Budget 2024.
civility.explanation: 'Lazy spending' is a loaded characterisation of the prior Government, though aimed at policy.

civility.statement: Does she stand by her statement that Whaikaha will "get vast orders of magnitude more in additional funding for front-line services"; if so, why was the additional funding allocated not enough to reverse the significant eligibility changes that her Government made without any warning or consultation?
civility.explanation: Pointed but engages the Minister's own words and policy.

civility.statement: the answer to every single question by the Labour Party is: more tax.
civility.explanation: Mocking misrepresentation rather than engagement with substance.

civility.statement: There's a magic money tree; just appropriate it!
civility.explanation: Mocking caricature of the Opposition's fiscal approach.

civility.statement: How will the Minister ensure that the rights of children at Gloriavale will be upheld and protected, given the disestablishment of the Gloriavale - West Coast Stakeholder Group?
civility.explanation: Respectful, substantive question focused on policy consequences.

civility.statement: I can confirm I did describe the behaviour of some of the pixie-like hapū in Taranaki as not reflective of true tikanga Māori.
civility.explanation: 'Pixie-like hapū' is a belittling, derogatory characterisation of a group rather than engagement with substance.

civility.statement: Well, obviously, that meeting involved me listening to that minerals sector. The minerals extractive sector has a rich, legitimate, and profoundly important place to play as we derive responses to climate change, rather than hysteria and alarmism.
civility.explanation: Dismisses opposing views as 'hysteria and alarmism.'

civility.statement: I thank the member from Taranaki for that question. She would know there's endless amounts of wind from that part of the country.
civility.explanation: A jibe at the questioner's region rather than a personal insult.

civility.statement: I don't want to hear from the galah over there
civility.explanation: Direct name-calling ('galah') of another member.

civility.statement: How does it contribute to the Taranaki region to allow an Australian mining company to suck 50 million tonnes of seabed each year for 35 years in a way that harms local fisheries and, in the mining company's own words, "totally destroys the seabed"?
civility.explanation: Loaded language but the attack is on the project, not a person.

civility.statement: a wise woman once said the problem with socialism is you run out of other people's money. And along came the New Zealand Labour Party and they proved her correct for only $100 billion.
civility.explanation: Mocking framing of the opposing party, though aimed at fiscal record.

civility.statement: Even Chris Hipkins is now telling New Zealanders that the country is in an awful state. Well, we know that, Chris Hipkins, we watched you do it.
civility.explanation: Direct personal needling of a named member ('we watched you do it').

civility.statement: Our disability communities deserve better. They deserve better than a Minister for Disability Issues who knew that Whaikaha had funding issues on 15 December, did absolutely nothing, did not alert that to her finance Minister or Prime Minister, didn't ask for more money for Whaikaha, but, instead, on 14 March signed out a briefing approving changes that were announced and implemented with immediate effect on 18 March—changes that left our disability communities blindsided and, in their own words, "devastated".
civility.explanation: Harsh but largely focused on the Minister's conduct and decisions, not her character.

civility.statement: Instead of taking responsibility, what the Minister does is to denigrate the work of carers, the same carers, the very carers, that she wrote about so compassionately two years ago.
civility.explanation: Accuses the Minister of denigrating carers; pointed but tied to her statements rather than personal abuse.

forthrightness.statement: That is not what's happened. All that we have said is that we expect major changes to front-line services across a range of portfolios that impact New Zealanders to be brought to Cabinet for a good discussion.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked for a specific date Simmonds informed his office; gives no date and reframes to a general principle.

forthrightness.statement: As we have said, she didn't bring it to Cabinet, and as a result there was no Cabinet discussion. That is something the Minister has apologised for, and she will do going forward.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly confirms the decision wasn't taken to Cabinet and that an apology was made.

forthrightness.statement: I disagree completely. All we're saying is that all Ministers, on their portfolios, need to bring forward to Cabinet conversations around any changes to front-line services that are major and significant and that will impact New Zealanders. That didn't happen in this case. The Minister has admitted that up front, has learnt from that experience, and we're moving forward.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked why the public should have confidence given delegations were removed; restates process rather than addressing confidence directly.

forthrightness.statement: Yes. What I support, though, is actually growing our economy and making sure that we do everything we can to end the wasteful spending so we can protect front-line services, doing everything we can to give tax relief to low and middle income working families, and to make sure that we have growth in our economy. That's what we're focused on.
forthrightness.explanation: Says 'Yes' to standing by the decision but immediately pivots to talking points rather than the real-terms-cut framing.

forthrightness.statement: Well, what they need is a Government that's going to have responsible financial management, rather than an 84 percent increase in Government spending, which drove up domestic inflation, which drove up interest rates, which put the economy into shrinking, into recession, and creates a rising risk of unemployment.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked how workers keep up with rising costs amid a real wage cut; pivots entirely to attacking past spending.

forthrightness.statement: We are deeply committed on delivering our net carbon zero 2050 goals, and one of the ways we're going to do that is doubling the amount of renewable electricity in this country.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked how he'll deliver climate goals after axing the just transitions unit; ignores the axing and offers a general aim.

forthrightness.statement: I want to make sure that there are more jobs for people in the New Zealand economy, and what we're doing is wanting to grow our economy. One of the ways we do that is by introducing fast-track consenting.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked how many climate change jobs he's comfortable axing; gives no number and changes the subject to jobs generally.

forthrightness.statement: What I can guarantee is that this is a Government that is working incredibly hard to deliver on our climate change commitments. That is what we're doing. We're also a Government that's determined to grow our economy and deliver on our climate change commitments. We can do both those things at the same time.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to guarantee no funding cuts to the Climate Change Commission; substitutes a different, vaguer guarantee.

forthrightness.statement: I have repeatedly confirmed in this House and elsewhere that in our Budget, more funding to provide front-line support to people with disabilities will be a priority, and that member is now asking me to comment on issues that are a matter for the Minister for Disability Issues and that are matters that that member should put on notice.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked the specific pre-committed amount; deflects to 'a priority' and refers the question to another Minister.

forthrightness.statement: I had a paper that was given to me by Whaikaha in February which noted, from providers, that the fund had been used for such expenses. I didn't make any insinuation that those would be inappropriate; that was just stating what the fund had been used for at that time.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly identifies her evidence source and clarifies what she did and didn't claim.

forthrightness.statement: First of all, I will confirm that my decisions weren't based on hearsay; they were based on a paper that was given to me by Whaikaha. Secondly, I won't resign, because I have inherited a situation where Whaikaha have a budget set by the previous Government that was insufficient for the settings that were in place, and so additional funding has had to be given to ensure they can get through the end of this year. A review will be undertaken to put in place the systems, the processes, the settings that should have been put in place by that Government when they set the ministry up.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked directly if she'll resign; answers 'I won't resign' and gives reasons.

forthrightness.statement: I believe I've addressed the question—that I don't believe that added bureaucracy is necessary to ensure the safety of children within Gloriavale. There are specific areas of law where every one of my Cabinet colleagues who has an area of specific interest for Gloriavale and the rights of children will be working to uphold that within their own agencies.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked how she will ensure children's rights after disestablishing the group; restates her view on bureaucracy and defers to colleagues rather than detailing assurance.

forthrightness.statement: Well, obviously, that meeting involved me listening to that minerals sector. The minerals extractive sector has a rich, legitimate, and profoundly important place to play as we derive responses to climate change, rather than hysteria and alarmism.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked whether he raised environmental/iwi/fishing concerns in the meeting; never says, and reframes to praise the sector.

forthrightness.statement: I thank the member from Taranaki for that question. She would know there's endless amounts of wind from that part of the country.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to choose between offshore wind and seabed mining off Taranaki; deflects entirely with a joke.

forthrightness.statement: On behalf of the Minister, no, I do not accept that observation. The household economic survey is being retained, whereas it would otherwise have come to an end in 2024. That's a more robust, better-quality survey to provide the information that the Government needs on which to base policy decisions in relation to child poverty reduction and other Government aims, and also to monitor the effectiveness of those policies going forward.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers 'no' and gives a specific reason (retention of an alternative survey).

veracity.statement: this is a Minister that is actually making sure there is more money going in this year than there was last year under that previous Government, and—importantly—in Budget 2024, there'll be even more money in place for people who need the disabled support and resource they need.
veracity.explanation: Claim of increased funding is broadly plausible but unsubstantiated in the text and contested by the Opposition.

veracity.statement: Well, what they need is a Government that's going to have responsible financial management, rather than an 84 percent increase in Government spending, which drove up domestic inflation, which drove up interest rates, which put the economy into shrinking, into recession, and creates a rising risk of unemployment.
veracity.explanation: The '84 percent increase in Government spending' figure is contestable and presented without context.

veracity.statement: The Cabinet Manual does not require Ministers to consult Cabinet on every decision that they make. In fact, the Prime Minister determines which decisions they want the Cabinet to be consulted on or not, so that is absolutely a legitimate question.
veracity.explanation: Accurate characterisation of how the Cabinet Manual and PM's discretion actually operate.

veracity.statement: Does he stand by the Government's decision to only increase the minimum wage by 2 percent when inflation is at 4.7 percent, which is a cut to the minimum wage in real terms?
veracity.explanation: The 2% rise versus 4.7% inflation implying a real-terms cut is arithmetically sound on the figures cited.

veracity.statement: What is his response to the fact that this effective cut to the minimum wage will increase child poverty rates, given that 64 percent of families in poverty are in work?
veracity.explanation: The '64 percent of families in poverty are in work' figure is plausible but unverified in the text.

veracity.statement: Yesterday, the coalition Government announced an $18 million boost for New Zealanders that have to travel for health treatment. These changes are long overdue for the national travel assistance (NTA) scheme, with its last increase to mileage and accommodation rates back in 2009.
veracity.explanation: Concrete, checkable claims about the boost and the last rate increase; presented as official announcement.

veracity.statement: There is a great opportunity for New Zealand to capture an even larger share of a sector projected to reach—and wait for this—US$1 trillion by 2040.
veracity.explanation: The figure echoes common industry projections but the range across analysts is broad.

veracity.statement: GNS Science have provided information that the value of so-said seabed is one-half a trillion—$500 billion—including phosphate in the Chathams and manganese nodules in the Kermadecs.
veracity.explanation: A specific valuation attributed to GNS Science; the headline 'value' of in-ground resources is easily overstated and lacks context.

veracity.statement: How does it contribute to the Taranaki region to allow an Australian mining company to suck 50 million tonnes of seabed each year for 35 years in a way that harms local fisheries and, in the mining company's own words, "totally destroys the seabed"?
veracity.explanation: The tonnage/duration figures and quoted phrase are checkable; presented as fact without sourcing here.

veracity.statement: On behalf of the Minister, no, I do not accept that observation. The household economic survey is being retained, whereas it would otherwise have come to an end in 2024. That's a more robust, better-quality survey to provide the information that the Government needs on which to base policy decisions in relation to child poverty reduction and other Government aims, and also to monitor the effectiveness of those policies going forward.
veracity.explanation: Factual claims about survey retention are plausible but contested and unverified here.

veracity.statement: a wise woman once said the problem with socialism is you run out of other people's money. And along came the New Zealand Labour Party and they proved her correct for only $100 billion.
veracity.explanation: The '$100 billion' debt figure is overstated/under-contextualised as a measure of waste.

veracity.statement: Our disability communities deserve better. They deserve better than a Minister for Disability Issues who knew that Whaikaha had funding issues on 15 December, did absolutely nothing, did not alert that to her finance Minister or Prime Minister, didn't ask for more money for Whaikaha, but, instead, on 14 March signed out a briefing approving changes that were announced and implemented with immediate effect on 18 March—changes that left our disability communities blindsided and, in their own words, "devastated".
veracity.explanation: Specific, checkable claims about dates and actions, presented as fact and contested by the Minister.

strength.statement: this is a Minister that is actually making sure there is more money going in this year than there was last year under that previous Government, and—importantly—in Budget 2024, there'll be even more money in place for people who need the disabled support and resource they need.
strength.explanation: Mix of a claimed current increase and a future Budget promise; delivery on the latter not yet demonstrated.

strength.statement: Just this week, the Government announced significant new money—hundreds of millions of dollars—to ensure that low and middle income families with young children get more money in their bank accounts with our FamilyBoost childcare policy.
strength.explanation: Claims a concrete announcement/commitment; delivery to bank accounts is prospective.

strength.statement: First of all, I will confirm that my decisions weren't based on hearsay; they were based on a paper that was given to me by Whaikaha. Secondly, I won't resign, because I have inherited a situation where Whaikaha have a budget set by the previous Government that was insufficient for the settings that were in place, and so additional funding has had to be given to ensure they can get through the end of this year. A review will be undertaken to put in place the systems, the processes, the settings that should have been put in place by that Government when they set the ministry up.
strength.explanation: Promises a future review and cites additional funding; delivery is in progress at best.

strength.statement: Yesterday, the coalition Government announced an $18 million boost for New Zealanders that have to travel for health treatment. These changes are long overdue for the national travel assistance (NTA) scheme, with its last increase to mileage and accommodation rates back in 2009.
strength.explanation: A funded, announced policy change; implementation is still being rolled out.

strength.statement: Already, 113,000 cubic metres of dirt has been moved of the 145,000 cubic metres which need to be moved, and there is more work to be done. It will be open over Easter and completed in May.
strength.explanation: Reports concrete delivery progress on a stated work programme.

strength.statement: On 31 January, I welcomed an agreement with Australia that will benefit New Zealand researchers to participate in collaborative research projects through Australia's SmartSat Cooperative Research Centre; on 5 March, together with the climate change Minister, the Hon Simon Watts, I welcomed the successful launch of MethaneSAT, a state-of-the-art satellite designed to accurately detect methane emissions and contribute to global efforts to combat climate change; and just last week, we announced New Zealand's research being sent to the International Space Station.
strength.explanation: Recounts a series of delivered announcements, though several are agreements/launches rather than her own delivery.

specificity.statement: this is a Minister that is actually making sure there is more money going in this year than there was last year under that previous Government, and—importantly—in Budget 2024, there'll be even more money in place for people who need the disabled support and resource they need.
specificity.explanation: References more money and Budget 2024 but gives no figures or mechanisms.

specificity.statement: We are deeply committed on delivering our net carbon zero 2050 goals, and one of the ways we're going to do that is doubling the amount of renewable electricity in this country.
specificity.explanation: Names a 2050 target and 'doubling renewable electricity' but no timeline, figures, or mechanism.

specificity.statement: I can tell members that there will be personal income tax relief in the Budget. This tax relief—and Mr Parker will be pleased to hear this—will be funded from within the operating allowance, and the operating allowance will be less than the $3.5 billion allowance indicated in the half-year update. This means the Government will not be borrowing extra to pay for tax relief, and it means tax relief will not be adding to inflationary pressures.
specificity.explanation: Names the policy, funding source, and the $3.5 billion benchmark.

specificity.statement: Spending on front-line services will be reprioritised, despite some people practically fainting at the thought that the Government could do things differently and more effectively, and the Budget will deliver on Government policy commitments, including many of those in the coalition agreements.
specificity.explanation: States reprioritisation and coalition commitments without detail on what or how much.

specificity.statement: Just this week, the Government announced significant new money—hundreds of millions of dollars—to ensure that low and middle income families with young children get more money in their bank accounts with our FamilyBoost childcare policy.
specificity.explanation: Names FamilyBoost and an order of magnitude ('hundreds of millions') but no precise figure or per-family amount.

specificity.statement: Does she stand by her statement that Whaikaha will "get vast orders of magnitude more in additional funding for front-line services"; if so, why was the additional funding allocated not enough to reverse the significant eligibility changes that her Government made without any warning or consultation?
specificity.explanation: Quotes the Minister's exact phrasing and ties it to a concrete consequence.

specificity.statement: First of all, I will confirm that my decisions weren't based on hearsay; they were based on a paper that was given to me by Whaikaha. Secondly, I won't resign, because I have inherited a situation where Whaikaha have a budget set by the previous Government that was insufficient for the settings that were in place, and so additional funding has had to be given to ensure they can get through the end of this year. A review will be undertaken to put in place the systems, the processes, the settings that should have been put in place by that Government when they set the ministry up.
specificity.explanation: References a paper, inherited budget shortfall and a planned review, but no figures.

specificity.statement: Yesterday, the coalition Government announced an $18 million boost for New Zealanders that have to travel for health treatment. These changes are long overdue for the national travel assistance (NTA) scheme, with its last increase to mileage and accommodation rates back in 2009.
specificity.explanation: Names the scheme, the $18 million figure, and the 2009 reference point.

specificity.statement: This boost will see the mileage rates rise from 28c to 34c a kilometre, and the nightly accommodation rate change from $100 to $140 a night.
specificity.explanation: Exact before-and-after figures for mileage and accommodation rates.

specificity.statement: We expect that around 4,500 extra New Zealanders will benefit from this boost.
specificity.explanation: Gives a concrete number of expected beneficiaries.

specificity.statement: State Highway 1 across the Brynderwyns will open tonight until 2 April, for the Easter weekend, with work currently under way to ensure the resilience of this critical route being paused to allow holidaymakers to travel north.
specificity.explanation: Precise reopening window and dates.

specificity.statement: Already, 113,000 cubic metres of dirt has been moved of the 145,000 cubic metres which need to be moved, and there is more work to be done. It will be open over Easter and completed in May.
specificity.explanation: Exact volumes moved and remaining, plus a completion month.

specificity.statement: you can't tax yourself to prosperity—you can't tax your way to prosperity. You need a plan for growth. You need a plan to grow the economy.
specificity.explanation: Repeated calls for 'a plan' with no actual plan detail.

specificity.statement: Does he stand by his answer to me at question time yesterday that "what we are interested in is actually delivering on our climate … goals", and, if so, how does he intend to do that when his Government has axed the just transitions unit and emissions reductions jobs at the Ministry for Primary Industries?
specificity.explanation: Names the just transitions unit and MPI emissions roles as concrete evidence.

specificity.statement: Yes, I do stand by my statements. I especially stand by the statements I recently made in my speech to the Auckland Business Chamber outlining my priorities in the workplace relations and safety portfolio. My priorities to simplify and improve the Holidays Act, increase certainty for those in contracting relationships, reform health and safety, and put in place measures for the performance of front-line services will help increase labour market flexibility and improve business confidence, and I believe that these moves will be positive steps for both businesses and workers.
specificity.explanation: Lists named policy areas (Holidays Act, contracting, health and safety) but no mechanisms or timeframes.

rigor.explanation: Counters the 'soft on crime' framing with a budget figure, though rhetorically rather than with full evidence.

rigor.statement: at what stage does someone who wants to ram-raid that pharmacy know that they’re not one of the pharmacies that are stocking pseudoephedrine? Is it just something you find out after the damage is done?
rigor.explanation: Raises a coherent practical objection — opt-in stocking does not protect pharmacies from offenders who only learn which stock it after attacking — though posed rhetorically.

rigor.statement: the real-time register that we know that is used in Queensland—not a perfect system from what I understand, but it is something that could have been a starting point. No need for us to reinvent the wheel.
rigor.explanation: Argues from an existing precedent and acknowledges its imperfections, a measured evidence-based suggestion.

rigor.statement: I think what we need to do is make clear that we are introducing a regime of regulating cough medicine similar to the four other countries that we most often compare ourselves with ... you can have paralysis by analysis.
rigor.explanation: Leans on the 'paralysis by analysis' cliché to justify not gathering more evidence rather than engaging the substance of the consultation gap.

rigor.statement: I listen to the likes of Know Your Stuff NZ, who know a lot about drugs; they have been pretty clear about the fact they don’t believe it’s viable to manufacture methamphetamine.
rigor.explanation: Grounds his position in cited expert/submitter evidence on the non-viability of home manufacture rather than assertion alone.

rigor.statement: it is actually not currently a requirement to keep pseudoephedrine medications in safes in pharmacists. So the notion that this legislation is taking away that requirement is untrue, and not only is it untrue, it couldn’t be true, if somebody knew that basic fact.
rigor.explanation: Corrects a false premise underpinning the opposing amendment, a substantively relevant logical point.

rigor.statement: it would be wrong for the Parliament or the Government to tell them exactly what to do, because we just don’t direct the police in this country.
rigor.explanation: Invokes the constitutional principle of police operational independence as a coherent reason not to legislate a precursor-monitoring directive.

rigor.statement: The assumed need for it suggests that this legislation will increase the availability of methamphetamine, when all the evidence and most of the submissions that came into the select committee told us that the opposite is true.
rigor.explanation: Argues from the weight of submissions/evidence that the bill will not increase meth availability, though asserts 'all the evidence' somewhat sweepingly.

rigor.statement: if you are to introduce a new substance for classification, and therefore to bring along with it new criminal penalties, you only need to pass an Order in Council, which is typically rubber-stamped and waved through Parliament within a few minutes. However, if you are to declassify or to down-classify a substance, you need an entire amendment bill
rigor.explanation: Uses the procedural asymmetry as evidence for her conclusion that the Act is structurally biased, a well-reasoned point.

rigor.statement: we have seen it reflected in the Law Commission’s work from 2011; from He Ara Oranga, the mental health and addiction inquiry; and Turuki! Turuki!, the Safe and Effective Justice Advisory Group review—all of which, effectively, said we just need a straight-up repeal and replacement
rigor.explanation: Marshals three named reviews to support the call for repeal-and-replace of the Act, evidence-based argumentation.

rigor.statement: the difference with methamphetamine from every other drug, virtually, that we deal with ... is that this starts life, as does every ingredient which goes into it: every precursor is legal when it starts life, and it’s only when they are put together that you have an illegal substance.
rigor.explanation: Sound factual premise framing his subsequent concern about precursor monitoring.

rigor.statement: When I was a younger police officer, we had a major heroin epidemic in New Zealand ... that was cured overnight, because the Mr Asia syndicate ... had been bringing basically all the heroin into New Zealand ... The next lot of heroin arrived because the very resourceful criminals ... actually started to make heroin, what we called homebake heroin, using codeine-based products
rigor.explanation: Reasoning by historical analogy to warn of substitution effects; suggestive but the analogy's force depends on contested parallels.

rigor.statement: Has the Minister considered the importance of ensuring that there is a monitoring regime so that by, for example, working out how much red phosphorus is being sold ... if the amount of them being sold, stolen, or otherwise acquired starts to rise, is there anything that the member has considered?
rigor.explanation: Proposes a concrete, testable monitoring mechanism (tracking precursor sales like red phosphorus) tied to his substitution argument.

charisma.statement: I’d like to thank the Minister, the Hon David Seymour, for his considerable contribution just before the break ... I thank him for responding in a very sincere and genuine way to the questions that we put.
charisma.explanation: Builds goodwill and a cooperative tone before asking him to adopt her amendment — bridge-building.

charisma.statement: while I was listening to Greg O’Connor, Hello Sailor’s “Blue Lady” was ringing in my ears. Greg O’Connor has got to be one of the best recounters.
charisma.explanation: Light cross-bench rapport that disarms before responding to the argument.

charisma.statement: entirely consistent with the approach that we have taken on cigarettes, on alcohol, on cannabis, and on all other substances, including pseudoephedrine, let’s take an evidence-based, harm minimisation approach, but let’s apply that to substances across the board.
charisma.explanation: Appeals across the House to a shared evidence-based logic the Minister himself is using, seeking common ground.

charisma.statement: I want to start by, first and foremost, thanking all of those who took time to make submissions on the bill. I’d also like to thank all of the other members of the committee for their consideration of this bill
charisma.explanation: Inclusive, appreciative tone that brings stakeholders and members along.

charisma.statement: when the first reading did occur, almost a year ago, the then Opposition members were quite scathing of this bill and didn’t seem to think that it did much at all. I’m sure they understand now, when they’re on the other side, that sometimes there are pieces of legislation that do make the legislation better.
charisma.explanation: Makes a partisan point about the other side's inconsistency rather than seeking common ground, though gently.

divination.statement: as pseudoephedrine becomes more readily available, the group of frequent drug users in New Zealand will use this drug and, potentially, use it to manufacture methamphetamine.
divination.explanation: Prediction of domestic meth manufacture resuming after reclassification; runs against the select-committee evidence that home manufacture is no longer viable given cheap imported meth, so uncertain/leaning unlikely.

divination.statement: the coordinated shoppers—the aunties that get together and who might be tools for supply of meth could come back into our community and then start cooking in their kāinga
divination.explanation: Forecasts a revival of home meth cooking by coordinated purchasers; speculative and contrary to the evidence presented that home manufacture is no longer viable.

divination.statement: I think, sadly, it is unlikely that anything we’re doing right now is going to stop that supply. It seems to be a strong supply.
divination.explanation: Prediction that the meth supply will persist; consistent with strong observed import volumes.

strength.statement: we also are very supportive and have a history of being very supportive of our local community pharmacies. And we demonstrated that, certainly, with our minor ailments bills and removing prescription charges so that people weren’t dissuaded by those $5 prescription charges
strength.explanation: Points to a policy actually delivered (scrapping prescription charges) as evidence of follow-through, not just aspiration.

forthrightness.statement: I did use Five Eyes as shorthand for the five countries—Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States—that, along with New Zealand, make up the Five Eyes networks. Those other four countries all have near identical, if not identical, approaches to pseudoephedrine cough medicine, as New Zealand has, or will have very soon if this law passes.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers Leary's question about why Five Eyes was invoked — explains it was shorthand for comparable-jurisdiction alignment, no evasion.

forthrightness.statement: I think what we need to do is make clear that we are introducing a regime of regulating cough medicine similar to the four other countries that we most often compare ourselves with ... you can have paralysis by analysis.
forthrightness.explanation: Responds to the question about why he did not seek further advice from affected communities by reframing rather than addressing the lack of consultation head-on.

forthrightness.statement: in terms of how I could monitor sales, or anyone could, Medsafe have to let the stuff be imported. So we’ll have a pretty good idea of how much is coming into the country if you wanted to monitor sales.
forthrightness.explanation: Eventually answers the monitoring question after noting it is out of scope, but offers import volumes rather than the point-of-sale monitoring the members asked about.

forthrightness.statement: I think, sadly, it is unlikely that anything we’re doing right now is going to stop that supply. It seems to be a strong supply.
forthrightness.explanation: Candid concession in answering O'Connor that current measures are unlikely to halt the meth supply rather than overclaiming.

strength.statement: I described to them that, in the health workforce area, we have placed more GP registrars actually out with practice than many of us can recall for many years.
strength.explanation: Claims credit for concrete workforce action (GP registrars in practice), but the delivery is described vaguely without firm numbers, so follow-through is only partly demonstrated.

strength.statement: There have been 50 new medical school places filled this year; I believe the split is 30 to Auckland, 20 to Otago.
strength.explanation: Specific delivery claim (places filled this year) with this Minister responsible, though a modest measure.

strength.statement: a few weeks ago, the Prime Minister and I announced the five health targets, which will set a key direction for health.
strength.explanation: An announcement of targets, not delivery — targets set a direction but no outcome has yet been achieved.

strength.statement: today, we announced an $18 million a year increase to the national transport allowance.
strength.explanation: A funded announcement attributable to the Government, but announced today so delivery is not yet demonstrated.

strength.statement: Pharmac has decided to retain the 8.1B exemption for children; this means that children with cancer will be able to receive their medications from Pharmac and have it administered in a hospital. The previous Government put that under review.
strength.explanation: Claims a concrete decision to retain children's cancer drug access, an actual call made rather than mere aspiration.

strength.statement: To tackle this issue head on, the coalition Government has committed $500 million to fixing those damn potholes.
strength.explanation: A funding commitment recently made — intent and money allocated, but delivery not yet demonstrated.

specificity.statement: I described to them that, in the health workforce area, we have placed more GP registrars actually out with practice than many of us can recall for many years.
specificity.explanation: Gestures at a quantity ('more...than many can recall') without a figure, mechanism, or timeframe.

specificity.statement: There have been 50 new medical school places filled this year; I believe the split is 30 to Auckland, 20 to Otago.
specificity.explanation: Concrete figures and a breakdown by institution for the current year.

specificity.statement: a few weeks ago, the Prime Minister and I announced the five health targets, which will set a key direction for health.
specificity.explanation: References a named package ('five health targets') but this sentence itself gives only the headline, not the measures.

specificity.statement: faster cancer treatment, 90 percent of patients to receive cancer management within 31 days of the decision to treat; improved immunisation for children, 95 percent of children to be fully immunised at 24 months of age
specificity.explanation: Precise percentage thresholds and timeframes for named clinical targets.

specificity.statement: today, we announced an $18 million a year increase to the national transport allowance.
specificity.explanation: Names a precise annual dollar figure and the named scheme.

specificity.statement: In 1995, the very founder was convicted of three charges of indecent assault against a 19-year-old. The overseeing shepherd, Howard Temple, is currently facing 27 charges of sexual offending. In 2023, Jonathon Benjamin was convicted of 26 charges of sexual offending.
specificity.explanation: Names individuals, charge counts, and years with precision.

specificity.statement: When it comes into force, it will increase our exports via the EU by $1.8 billion annually—a substantial amount from a Government that is focused on trade and trading with the world.
specificity.explanation: Names a precise annual export-gain figure.

specificity.statement: It notes that we will have 91 percent of duties removed when it comes into force, and 97 percent after seven years.
specificity.explanation: Precise percentages tied to defined timeframes.

specificity.statement: The EU is our fourth-largest trading partner, with around $20 billion in two-way goods and services traded on an annual basis—very significant amounts. We’re noting tariff savings of $100 million per year on New Zealand exports.
specificity.explanation: Ranking, dollar volumes, and a per-year saving figure.

specificity.statement: we’re looking at around $43 million in tariff savings for kiwifruit growers, which accounts to, on average, an annual saving of $16,000 per grower.
specificity.explanation: Aggregate and per-grower figures stated precisely.

specificity.statement: his own ministry reports that over just a six-year period, our country’s area of indigenous vegetation cover decreased by over 12,000 hectares, and we currently have the highest proportion of threatened species per capita in the world.
specificity.explanation: Hectare figure, timeframe, and a comparative ranking.

specificity.statement: The Parliamentary Commissioner for the Environment points out that only 2 percent of Government expenditure goes toward nature.
specificity.explanation: A precise percentage attributed to a named source.

specificity.statement: It could bring hundreds of millions of dollars into the industry—hundreds of millions of dollars—but they won’t support it because they’re in the pocket of the lobbyists.
specificity.explanation: Names a real bill but the benefit is a round, unsourced range.

specificity.statement: Most OECD countries pay about 14 percent—14—of average income. However, the highest costs are observed in New Zealand where net childcare costs for working families can reach as high as 38 percent of average earnings.
specificity.explanation: Comparative percentages and a clear measure (share of average earnings).

specificity.statement: Ordinary Kiwi parents will be getting direct financial assistance with the reimbursement of up to 25 percent of early childhood education (ECE) fees that they’ve paid for. That is up to $75 a week for working families with young children
specificity.explanation: Names the mechanism (reimbursement of ECE fees), the rate (25%), and the weekly cap ($75).

specificity.statement: So the higher the income, the less support they will get, so that we can target the low- and middle-income families.
specificity.explanation: Describes a targeting/abatement mechanism in direction but without the income thresholds or abatement rate.

specificity.statement: Even just this morning, a tax bill passed in this House that had two brand new taxes—two brand new taxes. What we saw was that fuel taxes are going to go up by twice as much

specificity.statement: we’ve seen a $50 tax on every car up and down New Zealand with National’s drivers’ tax, with the Prime Minister speculating there could be more
specificity.explanation: Names a dollar figure and the policy.

specificity.statement: For the first time in my public service history, there is no clear indication of what the operating allowance is for the Budget. They said that it’s going to be less than $3.5 billion.
specificity.explanation: Cites a concrete figure ('less than $3.5 billion') and a specific document.

specificity.statement: At one minute past midnight tonight, State Highway 1 over the Brynderwyns reopens for Easter.

specificity.statement: To tackle this issue head on, the coalition Government has committed $500 million to fixing those damn potholes.
specificity.explanation: Names a dollar commitment and purpose, though no timeframe or distribution.

specificity.statement: A recent NZIER report indicated that the economic benefits of just building the Dome Valley extension to Te Hana was approximately $500 million per year.
specificity.explanation: Names the source, the project segment, and an annual benefit figure.

specificity.statement: In Queenstown, for example, they dropped the bus fares to $2 for a flat fare, made the transfer free, made the buses run every 15 minutes, and what happened? They raised more revenue than when the bus fares were higher.
specificity.explanation: Names the place, fare level, frequency, and the revenue outcome.

specificity.statement: we now have the highest car ownership rate in the entire world. And our entire dairy exports—$19 billion—do not pay for our annual imports of vehicles and fuel to run them, which is now at $22 billion.
specificity.explanation: Concrete dollar figures for dairy exports and vehicle/fuel imports.

specificity.statement: the Minister... was forced to admit that putting speed limits up to 50 from 30 kilometres an hour around schools only saves 15 seconds—that’s 1 percent of the average car journey... if a pedestrian or vulnerable road user is struck by a car, they have a 300 percent increased chance of fatality.
specificity.explanation: Quantifies the time saving, its share of a journey, and the fatality-risk change.

specificity.statement: did he consult extensively with the vehicle industry before proposing the rates that are proposed in the bill, in particular for electric vehicles (EVs)?
specificity.explanation: A precise, answerable question naming the bill, the rates, and the relevant industry.

specificity.statement: the Government has agreed that there should be a lower plug-in hybrid rate. That is why we sent it to select committee, to test that issue, and Cabinet agreed that the rate should be $38.
specificity.explanation: Names the concrete rate ($38) and the decision pathway.

specificity.statement: the purpose of this bill is about ensuring that vehicles which use our roads are contributing towards maintaining them. That includes electric vehicles, which up until 1 April have received an exemption.
specificity.explanation: Clearly states the bill's purpose, the affected vehicles, and the exemption end date.

specificity.statement: a heavy vehicle is 625 times greater impact on the road than a light vehicle—625.
specificity.explanation: A precise quantitative claim, repeated for emphasis.

specificity.statement: the $785 million paid in RUC by heavy vehicles, compared to the $1.8 billion paid by light vehicles, isn’t completely out of sync with their impact on the road
specificity.explanation: Cites concrete RUC revenue figures for heavy versus light vehicles.

specificity.statement: On Monday, I heard an interesting article on Radio New Zealand—actually, it was the CEO of the Motor Trade Association... pointing to the reality that with the changes in this piece of legislation, there is no incentive for people to move from combustion engines into e-vehicles, because at an average of 14,000 kilometres, it will be about $1,064 paid in road-user charges (RUC), which would be equivalent to diesel on the same road.
specificity.explanation: Cites the source, an average distance, and a dollar RUC figure.

specificity.statement: road-user charges are here to fund the roads and that we’ve had the electric vehicles (EVs) not paying them for a while, and that was to incentivise the uptake of those electric vehicles.
specificity.explanation: Clear policy explanation but at a general level.

veracity.explanation: Plausible directional claim about registrar placements but unquantified and hard to verify as stated.

veracity.explanation: Specific, checkable figure that aligns with the announced expansion of medical places; hedged with 'I believe'.

veracity.explanation: Cites an official projection figure, though stated as certainty when it is a forecast.

veracity.explanation: Unsubstantiated corruption claim presented as commonly known fact.

veracity.statement: Most OECD countries pay about 14 percent—14—of average income. However, the highest costs are observed in New Zealand where net childcare costs for working families can reach as high as 38 percent of average earnings.
veracity.explanation: Cites OECD childcare-cost comparisons broadly consistent with published figures, though the framing selects the high end for NZ.

veracity.explanation: Accurately describes the FamilyBoost policy parameters as announced.

veracity.statement: Even just this morning, a tax bill passed in this House that had two brand new taxes—two brand new taxes. What we saw was that fuel taxes are going to go up by twice as much
veracity.explanation: References a real bill passed that morning and fuel-tax changes; the 'two brand new taxes' characterisation is a contestable political framing presented as fact.

veracity.statement: we’ve seen a $50 tax on every car up and down New Zealand with National’s drivers’ tax, with the Prime Minister speculating there could be more
veracity.explanation: References the $50 motor-vehicle registration/levy change; the '$50 tax on every car' label is a partisan characterisation of a fee increase.

veracity.statement: For the first time in my public service history, there is no clear indication of what the operating allowance is for the Budget. They said that it’s going to be less than $3.5 billion.
veracity.explanation: Specific institutional claim about the Budget Policy Statement's operating allowance; plausible from her experience but a contestable characterisation of the document.

veracity.statement: At one minute past midnight tonight, State Highway 1 over the Brynderwyns reopens for Easter.
veracity.explanation: A specific, verifiable claim about a scheduled road reopening.

veracity.statement: In 2017, they cancelled the Roads of National Significance, which included the four-lane highway to Northland.
veracity.explanation: Broadly accurate that the 2017 Labour-led Government deprioritised Roads of National Significance, though 'cancelled' simplifies a more graduated reprioritisation.

veracity.statement: A recent NZIER report indicated that the economic benefits of just building the Dome Valley extension to Te Hana was approximately $500 million per year.
veracity.explanation: Attributes a specific figure to a named NZIER report; sourced but unverifiable from the text and dependent on the report's assumptions.

veracity.explanation: Consistent with road-safety research that impact survivability falls sharply between 30 and 50 km/h; the precise '300 percent' and '15 seconds' are presented confidently.

veracity.explanation: A specific historical claim about 2012 weight and funding changes, presented as fact but unverifiable here and a contestable characterisation.

authenticity.statement: we have never ever reached that level of immunisation

civility.statement: I want to start this discourse by thanking our hard-working health professionals, both clinical and non-clinical, for their continued support and commitment to serving New Zealanders and maintaining our health system.
civility.explanation: Respectful, gracious opening acknowledging the workforce; constructive in tone.

civility.statement: Gloriavale is not some quaint, outdated community. It’s an oppressive, backward, harmful, and evil institution, run by a small group of controlling men.
civility.explanation: Strongly worded but directed at a community credibly associated with documented abuse, not at a political opponent's character.

civility.statement: It’s a sign of an incompetent Government—a Government that doesn’t care, and a Government that’s too obsessed with its own chaos to look after people.
civility.explanation: Sweeping characterisation of the Government as not caring and chaotic; rhetoric rather than engagement with the policy rationale.

civility.statement: Basic human rights are not a priority for this Government. Children are not a priority for this Government.
civility.explanation: Accusatory framing of motives rather than critique of the specific decision.

civility.statement: And I do, of course, have to acknowledge the other side for their work, but I will congratulate Mr McClay for his work and making sure that we got it into force quickly and efficiently.
civility.explanation: Gracious, gives credit across the aisle.

civility.statement: We aren’t going to get wealthy growing mega Government bureaucracies and shuffling paper back and forth.
civility.explanation: A dismissive jab at 'bureaucracies' but aimed at policy approach rather than a person.

civility.statement: this Government has been breathtakingly reckless in prioritising short-term profits over the long-term health and wellbeing of our environment and communities.
civility.explanation: Charged language ('breathtakingly reckless') imputing bad priorities, though aimed at the policy direction.

civility.statement: If the Government bulldozes on with this short-sighted, reckless approach to nature, we will ultimately face dire consequences, and Aotearoa deserves much better.
civility.explanation: Critical of approach rather than persons, but emotive and conditional-threat framing.

civility.statement: We’re seeing a Minister completely out of her depth.
