specificity.statement: I’m reminded of Leon Smith, who lost his life in action in Afghanistan, a month after earning his New Zealand Gallantry Decoration. He was trying to save the life of his SAS comrade Dougie Grant while under fire.
specificity.explanation: Named individual, decoration, circumstances, and comrade.

specificity.statement: They are the heroes who sacrifice for our country, and they are the heroes who deserve the respect and the acknowledgment of every single citizen in this country. New Zealand wouldn’t be the beautiful country on planet Earth without their sacrifice.
specificity.explanation: General platitudes of gratitude with no concrete mechanism, figure, or detail.

specificity.statement: the bill we have before us today incorporates and retains that strategic partnership in the statute to address that concern that was raised by the Waitangi Tribunal and that was raised by submitters.
specificity.explanation: Points to a concrete legislative change and its stated rationale.

specificity.statement: Oranga Tamariki prepares and releases a range of regular reports including: (1) an annual report, which measures their performance against standards agreed as part of their annual appropriations; (2) a quarterly report ... (3) safety of children in care annual report ... and (4) under section 44(8)(b) of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989, the Minister for Children is required to report to Parliament every three years
specificity.explanation: Enumerates named reports, statutory sections, and reporting frequencies in detail.

specificity.statement: hence, this bill was introduced into the House last year—in May 2024—so we’ve had about a year of this process.
specificity.explanation: Gives a specific month and year.

specificity.statement: In August of 1840, just seven months after the signing of Te Tiriti o Waitangi, our very first tupuna was removed as a baby by colonial hands.
specificity.explanation: Anchored to a specific date and event relative to the Treaty signing.

specificity.statement: In 1986, we even had Pūao-te-Āta-tū, which was a ministerial advisory group led by the great John Rangihau
specificity.explanation: Names the report, the year, and the chair.

rigor.statement: Those wars saw around 336 Māori die in the First World War and 649 die in the Second World War. But it is estimated that, in the New Zealand Wars, around 2,154 Māori died, and 745 British or colonialist or kūpapa soldiers died. This is a significant number. Those wars—from 1845 to 1872—ran for 27 years.
rigor.explanation: Uses quantified evidence to support the conclusion that the New Zealand Wars deserve recognition; conclusion follows from the premises.

rigor.statement: I believe that the proposed wording for the new amendment, which says “commemoration of the contribution of all those who have served New Zealand … in time of war and in warlike conflicts”, would capture those in the New Zealand Wars.
rigor.explanation: Reasoned textual interpretation of the amendment's wording applied to a specific case; a defensible inference, though the drafters' intent is unconfirmed.

rigor.statement: I have to say there was a little bit of disappointing politicking from the Opposition, who voted against retaining that at select committee. They have an opportunity to support the bill now but I don’t anticipate that they’re going to do so, given the things they’ve been saying, which, unfortunately, haven’t been based on fact.
rigor.explanation: Cites a specific committee vote to support the charge, but the 'not based on fact' claim is asserted rather than evidenced.

rigor.statement: Oranga Tamariki prepares and releases a range of regular reports including: (1) an annual report, which measures their performance against standards agreed as part of their annual appropriations; (2) a quarterly report ... (3) safety of children in care annual report ... and (4) under section 44(8)(b) of the Oranga Tamariki Act 1989, the Minister for Children is required to report to Parliament every three years
rigor.explanation: Marshals a concrete list of existing accountability mechanisms to rebut the claim that reporting oversight is being lost.

rigor.statement: I challenge every Māori in this Whare and every non-Māori—and part-Māori ... that is responsible to and for mokopuna tamariki Māori, to check your privilege, to check your fragility, to check your white tears, to check your racism, and to check your sexism and misogyny and get some counselling and education and free your mind.
rigor.explanation: Relies on ad hominem and emotive appeal rather than evidence or logical entailment.

rigor.statement: It’s really, really telling that we’re seeing a level of outrage here that is not manifested when we are seeing tamariki Māori sleeping on the streets—
rigor.explanation: A whataboutery/relative-priorities appeal rather than an evidenced argument about the bill itself.

rigor.statement: the cultural considerations which are the focus of section 7AA, the methodology for maintaining the respect for cultural considerations in 7AA, have been retained in the Act. The bill does not prevent Oranga Tamariki from continuing and developing these relationships that they have already had and want to have with iwi, hapū, and Māori organisations.
rigor.explanation: Reasoned, measured rebuttal grounded in what the amended Act does and does not do.

strength.statement: I set out to tell the stories of those places and to recognise those streets, with a poppy sign and a little bit of the story behind those.
strength.explanation: Describes a concrete, self-initiated project he actually delivered as a Wellington city councillor (WWI commemorative street signage), though modest in scale.

charisma.statement: I would like to thank the Green Party and the Labour Party for recognising and acknowledging our tūpuna who have fought in the New Zealand Land Wars, Te Pūtake o Te Riri
charisma.explanation: Warm acknowledgement of other parties' support, building goodwill, though limited to the opposition bloc.

charisma.statement: So I am very encouraged by that, and I think it’s a fitting time as well, when we think of not just those who have been before but indeed those who continue to serve in a time of increasing uncertainty around the globe.
charisma.explanation: In the same speech he welcomes 'the collaborative comments from the Opposition'; the tone is inclusive and cross-party consensus-building on a shared cause.

charisma.statement: That was an excellent speech by Tim Costley. I just want to acknowledge what a great contribution that was to this debate.
charisma.explanation: Generous cross-party praise (Labour MP commending a National MP), building goodwill across the aisle.

charisma.statement: I also want to say I support colleagues both from Labour, the Greens, and Te Pāti Māori in their call for the New Zealand Wars to be considered properly as well.
charisma.explanation: Explicitly aligns across multiple parties on a shared cause, building common ground.

charisma.statement: I stand to address the “Oranga Tamariki (Repeal of Culture, Repeal of Custom, Repeal of Safety, and Repeal of Protections and Prosperity) Bill”, soon to be lorded over all mokopuna and their whānau by a Government and their spokesperson who knows nothing about Māori culture.
charisma.explanation: Sharply us-vs-them framing that alienates rather than persuades the other side.

charisma.statement: I want to say to the Minister over there—Karen Chhour—I respect what happened to her, in terms of her upbringing. She brings her experiences to the table. I do respect that, Minister, in terms of what you have revealed. I’m not here to mock you today, but I am here to ask you to listen to what te ao Māori have been saying.
charisma.explanation: Seeks to bring the Minister along rather than demonise her, appealing to shared concern for children.

civility.statement: That was an excellent speech by Tim Costley. I just want to acknowledge what a great contribution that was to this debate.
civility.explanation: Respectful, gracious acknowledgement of a political opponent.

civility.statement: I have to say there was a little bit of disappointing politicking from the Opposition, who voted against retaining that at select committee. They have an opportunity to support the bill now but I don’t anticipate that they’re going to do so, given the things they’ve been saying, which, unfortunately, haven’t been based on fact.
civility.explanation: Criticises the Opposition's conduct and accuracy rather than attacking them personally, but 'politicking' and 'not based on fact' are pointed jabs.

civility.statement: I stand to address the “Oranga Tamariki (Repeal of Culture, Repeal of Custom, Repeal of Safety, and Repeal of Protections and Prosperity) Bill”, soon to be lorded over all mokopuna and their whānau by a Government and their spokesperson who knows nothing about Māori culture.
civility.explanation: Personal attack on the Minister ('knows nothing about Māori culture') plus a mocking renaming of the bill; character-focused rather than substance-focused.

civility.statement: Clearly, the apology and crocodile tears from the Minister to the survivors of abuse in care ... was more fake news
civility.explanation: Impugns the Minister's sincerity with 'crocodile tears' and 'fake news' — a direct personal attack on honesty, which the Speaker was asked to rule on.

civility.statement: I challenge every Māori in this Whare and every non-Māori—and part-Māori ... that is responsible to and for mokopuna tamariki Māori, to check your privilege, to check your fragility, to check your white tears, to check your racism, and to check your sexism and misogyny and get some counselling and education and free your mind.
civility.explanation: Broadly accusatory personal challenge (racism, sexism, 'get some counselling') aimed at colleagues rather than their arguments.

civility.statement: It’s really, really telling that we’re seeing a level of outrage here that is not manifested when we are seeing tamariki Māori sleeping on the streets—
civility.explanation: Accuses opponents of misplaced priorities/hypocrisy rather than engaging their argument, though it stays on political conduct rather than personal insult.

civility.statement: the cultural considerations which are the focus of section 7AA, the methodology for maintaining the respect for cultural considerations in 7AA, have been retained in the Act. The bill does not prevent Oranga Tamariki from continuing and developing these relationships that they have already had and want to have with iwi, hapū, and Māori organisations.
civility.explanation: Engages the substance calmly and respectfully, without personal attack, even acknowledging the children are 'victims themselves'.

civility.statement: I want to say to the Minister over there—Karen Chhour—I respect what happened to her, in terms of her upbringing. She brings her experiences to the table. I do respect that, Minister, in terms of what you have revealed. I’m not here to mock you today, but I am here to ask you to listen to what te ao Māori have been saying.
civility.explanation: Explicitly respectful toward a political opponent's personal story while still disagreeing on policy — models constructive dialogue.

authenticity.statement: All of my political life, I’ve been a critic of the many imperialist wars and foreign adventures that this country and others have taken part in. ... But I’m not a pacifist. Hitler had to be stopped in World War II. Putin should be stopped in Ukraine. I supported the New Zealand Defence Forces being deployed in Timor-Leste and in the Solomon Islands, in Bougainville, in the Pacific.
authenticity.explanation: A consistent, nuanced position held over his career — opposing wars he sees as unjust (Iraq, Vietnam) while backing deployments he supported — matching his known record as a long-standing Labour anti-war voice who is not a pacifist.

authenticity.statement: 25 years ago, I was probably of the same view as the Minister that first and foremost we had to make these babies safe. That is still my view—absolutely. There are a number of us who had not seen the research ... When we saw that, we all came in behind.
authenticity.explanation: Openly acknowledges his own past position and a principled, evidence-driven change of mind rather than claiming lifelong consistency — a candid, credible account.

veracity.statement: Without this decision, the smelter would have automatically received over $150 million a year. This compares with the $37 million as a result of this Government's decision. This reflects savings of over $100 million per year to the Crown.
veracity.explanation: The figures may be accurate, but framing a reduced free allocation as '$100 million of savings' is arguable — the $150m was a notional automatic entitlement, not spending avoided.

veracity.statement: our aluminium plant produces the most pure aluminium in the world
veracity.explanation: A superlative claim asserted without evidence; likely marketing hyperbole rather than a verified fact.

veracity.statement: The latest results show that 72.1 percent of patients were admitted or discharged within six hours, a significant improvement from 67.5 percent in the previous quarter and an improvement from 69.7 percent in the same quarter of the previous year.
veracity.explanation: Precise figures attributed to just-released Health NZ quarterly data; internally consistent and checkable.

veracity.statement: Access to faster cancer care continues to improve, with 85.9 percent of patients receiving treatment within 31 days—just 0.1 percent away from the yearly milestone—and 77 percent of two-year-olds were immunised in the second quarter of this year, up from 75.7 percent in the previous quarter.
veracity.explanation: Specific published target figures; candidly notes these are only stable/near-milestone.

veracity.statement: increasing the number of front-line nurses at Health New Zealand by over 2,000 since we came into Government
veracity.explanation: Specific, checkable staffing claim presented as fact.

veracity.statement: as a former Dargaville boy, I'm very concerned about that as well, and I'm going to be talking to my colleague Simeon Brown about what we might do in the future. But there's been a massive decline, over the last six decades, in medical services in the North.
veracity.explanation: The long-run decline in Northland services is broadly supportable, if imprecise.

veracity.statement: We are definitely going to stop the scaremongering about the rainbow community—and they're writing to me right now in their thousands about the way they've been miscast by members of the Green Party... And we know why they're resigning in massive numbers from the Green Party right now
veracity.explanation: 'In their thousands' and 'massive numbers' resigning are unquantified, unsubstantiated claims.

veracity.statement: While section 7AA was well intended, it has created uncertainty for social workers when making decisions about the best interests and wellbeing of a child, as it puts a child's ethnicity first and their wellbeing second.
veracity.explanation: The characterisation of 7AA subordinating wellbeing to ethnicity is disputed by its drafters.

veracity.statement: The repeal of section 7AA does remove the requirement for the chief executive of Oranga Tamariki to report to the public at least once a year on the impact of measures on improving outcomes for Māori.
veracity.explanation: Candid, accurate statement of what the repeal removes rather than spinning it away.

veracity.statement: 38.3 percent of respondents said they were not concerned about their safety, and 26.9 percent said they felt safer. The fact that 65 percent of New Zealanders feel safe or safer than they did 12 months ago is a reflection of the hard work of our police officers.
veracity.explanation: Adds 'not concerned' to 'felt safer' to assert 65 percent 'feel safe or safer' — conflating two different response categories to inflate the headline.

veracity.statement: We've implemented a gang patch ban we were told would never work; we've stopped gangs taking over towns; delivered a new 24/7 station in the Auckland CBD; got police back out on the beat, with 40 percent more foot patrols; and seen violent crime drop by 2 percent.
veracity.explanation: Several claims are checkable and plausible; the causal framing of 'stopped gangs taking over towns' is looser.

veracity.statement: The 27th Ipsos Issues Monitor, released last month, showed that law and order continues to drop as a concern for New Zealanders. After peaking as the second most important issue to Kiwis in May 2023, it is now the fifth most important issue in the monitor to voters.
veracity.explanation: Cites a specific named survey with a datable trend that is checkable.

veracity.statement: New Zealand now has the most permissive regime for enabling extractive sector developments in the Western world.
veracity.explanation: A sweeping superlative asserted without evidence or comparative benchmark.

veracity.statement: Development West Coast says that for every mining job in the region, two others are created elsewhere; 100 new jobs at a mine. But it's not only in the West Coast; in Coromandel, the Wharekirauponga Underground Mine is likely to sustain over 1,000 jobs.
veracity.explanation: Attributes a multiplier to Development West Coast; the specific job figures are optimistic and unverified.

veracity.statement: Some 10 percent of the GDP of our economy and 11 percent of the workforce is in the construction sector.
veracity.explanation: Broadly in the right range for construction's economic footprint, though figures vary by definition.

veracity.statement: The Anzac Day Act 1966 currently restricts recognition and commemoration to those who served in six specified conflicts, ending with the war in South Vietnam. By being limited to the specific named conflicts, the Act is currently too narrow.
veracity.explanation: Accurate description of the existing Act's scope as the basis for the amendment.

specificity.statement: Without this decision, the smelter would have automatically received over $150 million a year. This compares with the $37 million as a result of this Government's decision. This reflects savings of over $100 million per year to the Crown.
specificity.explanation: Concrete dollar figures and a clear comparison.

specificity.statement: Does he think it's fair to give Rio Tinto an extra $37 million a year power bill subsidy, via free carbon credits, in the same week that households across the country are set to get a double-digit rise to their power bills?
specificity.explanation: Names the figure, the mechanism (free carbon credits) and a concrete contrast.

specificity.statement: Does he agree with the Climate Change Commission that free allocation of carbon credits weakens price incentives for emissions reduction and that the current approach to allocation is not aligned with our climate change targets?
specificity.explanation: Cites a specific institutional finding about price incentives and target alignment.

specificity.statement: The latest results show that 72.1 percent of patients were admitted or discharged within six hours, a significant improvement from 67.5 percent in the previous quarter and an improvement from 69.7 percent in the same quarter of the previous year.
specificity.explanation: Exact percentages with quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year comparisons.

specificity.statement: Access to faster cancer care continues to improve, with 85.9 percent of patients receiving treatment within 31 days—just 0.1 percent away from the yearly milestone—and 77 percent of two-year-olds were immunised in the second quarter of this year, up from 75.7 percent in the previous quarter.
specificity.explanation: Named targets with exact percentages and timeframes.

specificity.statement: This initiative will deliver 10,579 additional procedures by mid-2025. Patients are already seeing the benefits of this announcement, with 2,000 elective procedures already completed, including cataracts, and hip and knee replacements.
specificity.explanation: Exact target number, deadline, and named procedure types.

specificity.statement: the Government is taking action to strengthen primary care and grow the workforce, by creating 100 clinical placements for overseas-trained doctors in primary care, providing incentives to recruit up to 400 graduate nurses per year into primary care, and investing an additional $285 million over three years to support GP clinics
specificity.explanation: Named figures, mechanisms and timeframes for each measure.

specificity.statement: I'm advised that Health New Zealand is actively recruiting for those positions to have that service restored within 12 months.
specificity.explanation: Gives a 12-month restoration horizon, though no detail on how.

specificity.statement: increasing the number of front-line nurses at Health New Zealand by over 2,000 since we came into Government
specificity.explanation: Concrete figure and reference point.

specificity.statement: We agree entirely with the Prime Minister's comments about looking after our seniors—after all, we invented the phrase “Looking after our seniors”, and that's why we've done so much in the past.
specificity.explanation: Slogan and self-congratulation with no concrete detail.

specificity.statement: as a former Dargaville boy, I'm very concerned about that as well, and I'm going to be talking to my colleague Simeon Brown about what we might do in the future. But there's been a massive decline, over the last six decades, in medical services in the North.
specificity.explanation: Names historic examples (Te Kōpuru maternity, Dargaville) but nothing concrete about future action.

specificity.statement: While section 7AA was well intended, it has created uncertainty for social workers when making decisions about the best interests and wellbeing of a child, as it puts a child's ethnicity first and their wellbeing second.
specificity.explanation: References the specific provision and its claimed effect on decision-making.

specificity.statement: I have consistently said that nothing about this repeal will stop Oranga Tamariki's existing strategic partnerships with iwi and Māori organisations or prevent them from entering into new ones. During the select committee process, it was recommended that the part of section 7AA relating to the strategic partnerships should be retained in legislation. We considered this recommendation and agreed with the committee.
specificity.explanation: Points to the specific retained provision and the select committee process.

specificity.statement: The repeal of section 7AA does remove the requirement for the chief executive of Oranga Tamariki to report to the public at least once a year on the impact of measures on improving outcomes for Māori.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific reporting obligation and the alternative reports that remain.

specificity.statement: some of these members that are part of the military-style academy pilot programme have committed some pretty serious crimes. They must have committed at least two crimes of 10 years or more, if sentenced. We need to make sure that they are safe from each other and that the staff are safe, and this is the middle ground that will make sure that they are all safe.
specificity.explanation: Names the eligibility threshold (two crimes of 10 years or more).

specificity.statement: Why has she spent so much time on the repeal of section 7AA while, under her watch, reports of concern have increased by a massive 35 percent?
specificity.explanation: Cites a concrete 35 percent figure.

specificity.statement: Does he take responsibility for the higher doctors fees and the reduced access to general, urgent, and mental care because this Government continues to underfund community GP care, and, if so, does he commit to increasing funding for community care?
specificity.explanation: Names the specific harms (fees, access to general/urgent/mental care) but not figures.

specificity.statement: 38.3 percent of respondents said they were not concerned about their safety, and 26.9 percent said they felt safer. The fact that 65 percent of New Zealanders feel safe or safer than they did 12 months ago is a reflection of the hard work of our police officers.
specificity.explanation: Precise percentages from a named poll.

specificity.statement: We've implemented a gang patch ban we were told would never work; we've stopped gangs taking over towns; delivered a new 24/7 station in the Auckland CBD; got police back out on the beat, with 40 percent more foot patrols; and seen violent crime drop by 2 percent.
specificity.explanation: Named initiatives with figures (40 percent more patrols, 2 percent crime drop).

specificity.statement: The 27th Ipsos Issues Monitor, released last month, showed that law and order continues to drop as a concern for New Zealanders. After peaking as the second most important issue to Kiwis in May 2023, it is now the fifth most important issue in the monitor to voters.
specificity.explanation: Named source, rankings, and dates.

specificity.statement: Does he stand by his commitment to resign one year into the job if New Zealanders didn't feel more safe and we didn't have control back of our streets, given that 31 percent of New Zealanders feel less safe, there are more gang members peddling more methamphetamine on our streets, and he has failed to deliver the 500 police he promised New Zealand in two years?
specificity.explanation: Names the resignation pledge, the 31 percent figure, and the 500-police target.

specificity.statement: Why, when all of Whakatāne's obstetric and gynaecology specialists departed in January, were birthing women offered financial support for travel, but support was not offered for women seeking abortion?
specificity.explanation: Concrete comparison of travel support offered for birthing vs abortion, tied to a datable event.

specificity.statement: Does he agree with Christopher Luxon that “We've got to look after our seniors”; if so, why did he cut the number of beds for older patients by 50 percent in the downgraded new Dunedin Hospital?
specificity.explanation: Quotes the PM and cites a concrete 50 percent bed reduction at the new Dunedin Hospital.

specificity.statement: New Zealand now has the most permissive regime for enabling extractive sector developments in the Western world.
specificity.explanation: A definite claim about regime standing, but no metric behind 'most permissive'.

specificity.statement: Development West Coast says that for every mining job in the region, two others are created elsewhere; 100 new jobs at a mine. But it's not only in the West Coast; in Coromandel, the Wharekirauponga Underground Mine is likely to sustain over 1,000 jobs.
specificity.explanation: Named projects, a job multiplier, and figures.

specificity.statement: We in this Government have invested $225 million to fund recruitment and equipping and training our police officers, and we are on target to deliver our 500 additional police.
specificity.explanation: Names the investment figure and the 500-officer target.

specificity.statement: I expect and welcome an increase in tertiary enrolments this year. An increase would be positive, as we know higher education contributes to higher earnings and employment rates, contributing to economic growth.
specificity.explanation: General expectation with no figures or targets.

specificity.statement: Legislation passed just last night with the unanimous support of the House—I'm pleased and grateful to acknowledge—will see up to 250,000 new products available to flow into New Zealand this year alone. This means that our designers, builders, and DIY Kiwis will have far more choice for the products they use. More choice means more competition, greater resilience in terms of supply chain, greater innovation, and downward pressure on prices.
specificity.explanation: Cites 'up to 250,000 new products' this year and named beneficiaries.

specificity.statement: Some 10 percent of the GDP of our economy and 11 percent of the workforce is in the construction sector.
specificity.explanation: Concrete GDP and workforce percentages.

specificity.statement: we're strengthening the disciplinary process, including greater transparency, publishing the fact of builders having been disciplined or suspended, and establishing a new waterproofing licence pass for licensed building practitioners.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete mechanisms — publication of discipline and a new waterproofing licence class.

specificity.statement: The Anzac Day Act 1966 currently restricts recognition and commemoration to those who served in six specified conflicts, ending with the war in South Vietnam. By being limited to the specific named conflicts, the Act is currently too narrow.
specificity.explanation: Names the Act, the number of conflicts, and the cut-off (South Vietnam).

specificity.statement: the commitment made by the Prime Minister at the RSA's annual conference last year is being honoured by the introduction of this legislation, and we've committed to having it passed before Anzac Day of 2026.
specificity.explanation: Names the commitment source and a firm deadline (before Anzac Day 2026).

specificity.statement: Does she think provisions in the Oranga Tamariki (Responding to Serious Youth Offending) Amendment Bill allowing the use of physical force against children in State care breach the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child to be protected from all forms of physical violence?
specificity.explanation: Names the specific bill and the specific UNCROC protection at issue.

strength.statement: Without this decision, the smelter would have automatically received over $150 million a year. This compares with the $37 million as a result of this Government's decision. This reflects savings of over $100 million per year to the Crown.
strength.explanation: Describes a delivered Cabinet decision on allocation rate, though the 'savings' are contested.

strength.statement: The latest results show that 72.1 percent of patients were admitted or discharged within six hours, a significant improvement from 67.5 percent in the previous quarter and an improvement from 69.7 percent in the same quarter of the previous year.
strength.explanation: Points to a measurable improvement on a target, though attribution to the Minister's actions is partial.

strength.statement: This initiative will deliver 10,579 additional procedures by mid-2025. Patients are already seeing the benefits of this announcement, with 2,000 elective procedures already completed, including cataracts, and hip and knee replacements.
strength.explanation: Partial delivery claimed (2,000 done) against a concrete target still in progress.

strength.statement: the Government is taking action to strengthen primary care and grow the workforce, by creating 100 clinical placements for overseas-trained doctors in primary care, providing incentives to recruit up to 400 graduate nurses per year into primary care, and investing an additional $285 million over three years to support GP clinics
strength.explanation: Announced/committed initiatives; delivery is stated but largely prospective.

strength.statement: increasing the number of front-line nurses at Health New Zealand by over 2,000 since we came into Government
strength.explanation: Claims a delivered workforce increase under his Government.

strength.statement: We've implemented a gang patch ban we were told would never work; we've stopped gangs taking over towns; delivered a new 24/7 station in the Auckland CBD; got police back out on the beat, with 40 percent more foot patrols; and seen violent crime drop by 2 percent.
strength.explanation: Lists concrete delivered actions (patch ban, CBD station, foot patrols) rather than mere aspiration.

strength.statement: We in this Government have invested $225 million to fund recruitment and equipping and training our police officers, and we are on target to deliver our 500 additional police.
strength.explanation: 'On target to deliver' is in-progress rather than delivered follow-through.

strength.statement: Legislation passed just last night with the unanimous support of the House—I'm pleased and grateful to acknowledge—will see up to 250,000 new products available to flow into New Zealand this year alone. This means that our designers, builders, and DIY Kiwis will have far more choice for the products they use. More choice means more competition, greater resilience in terms of supply chain, greater innovation, and downward pressure on prices.
strength.explanation: References legislation actually passed the previous night, a delivered step, not just a promise.

strength.statement: we're strengthening the disciplinary process, including greater transparency, publishing the fact of builders having been disciplined or suspended, and establishing a new waterproofing licence pass for licensed building practitioners.
strength.explanation: Stated actions on cowboy builders, presented as underway rather than fully delivered.

strength.statement: the commitment made by the Prime Minister at the RSA's annual conference last year is being honoured by the introduction of this legislation, and we've committed to having it passed before Anzac Day of 2026.
strength.explanation: Commitment being acted on via actual legislation, with follow-through still pending passage.

forthrightness.statement: Well, it is fair to say that decisions such as this are highly complex, with no right answers. They depend on a number of assumptions and judgments about the broader economy, but also, importantly, how the electricity sector will develop over the next 20 years. Cabinet considered options from different experts and made a decision.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked specifically what advice supported the chosen rate given MfE, Treasury and a reviewer all favoured a lower allocation, he retreats to 'it's complex' and never identifies the supporting advice.

forthrightness.statement: Well, there you go again: the degrowth Greens would be happy to see jobs go offshore and aluminium produced in coal boilers overseas. This side of the House backs jobs and growth in our regions.
forthrightness.explanation: Dodges the fairness question about a subsidy amid rising household power bills.

forthrightness.statement: I reject the premise of the question. Oh, how rich it is for the Greens—the degrowth Greens—to talk about the components around being de-competitive or anti-competitive.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to commit to reviewing the scheme, he declines to engage and pivots to attacking the questioner.

forthrightness.statement: If the member had listened to my answers, he would have heard that we are increasing funding for primary care. He's trying to find a conspiracy here. The degrowth Greens are trying to find a conspiracy here.
forthrightness.explanation: Partly answers on funding but dodges the specific accountability for higher fees and reduced access.

forthrightness.statement: I'm advised that Health New Zealand is actively recruiting for those positions to have that service restored within 12 months.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers whether the Whakatāne vacancies and service will be addressed, with a timeframe.

forthrightness.statement: I have personal views, but that is an issue that I will raise with Health New Zealand.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked directly whether he agrees too many abortions occur, he declines to state his view and defers.

forthrightness.statement: Those issues have been delegated to the Hon Casey Costello, and I encourage her to put those directly to her.
forthrightness.explanation: Repeatedly deflects the substantive abortion-services questions to a delegated Minister rather than answering as portfolio holder.

forthrightness.statement: We agree entirely with the Prime Minister's comments about looking after our seniors—after all, we invented the phrase “Looking after our seniors”, and that's why we've done so much in the past.
forthrightness.explanation: Ignores the specific question about a 50 percent cut in older-patient beds at the new Dunedin Hospital.

forthrightness.statement: I'd tell that senior citizen to write to Winston Peters and Simeon Brown on this matter because they're more likely to do something about it than the Labour Party, who just manufacture complaints.
forthrightness.explanation: Deflects a constituent's concern into a partisan jab rather than saying what action will be taken.

forthrightness.statement: as a former Dargaville boy, I'm very concerned about that as well, and I'm going to be talking to my colleague Simeon Brown about what we might do in the future. But there's been a massive decline, over the last six decades, in medical services in the North.
forthrightness.explanation: Acknowledges concern and a next step, but offers no concrete commitment on Dargaville Hospital.

forthrightness.statement: We are definitely going to stop the scaremongering about the rainbow community—and they're writing to me right now in their thousands about the way they've been miscast by members of the Green Party... And we know why they're resigning in massive numbers from the Green Party right now
forthrightness.explanation: Turns a question about health urgency into a counter-attack on the Greens.

forthrightness.statement: To question one, no. To question two, no. To question three, I've already done that.
forthrightness.explanation: Direct yes/no responses to a multi-part question, though extremely terse with no elaboration.

forthrightness.statement: I have consistently said that nothing about this repeal will stop Oranga Tamariki's existing strategic partnerships with iwi and Māori organisations or prevent them from entering into new ones. During the select committee process, it was recommended that the part of section 7AA relating to the strategic partnerships should be retained in legislation. We considered this recommendation and agreed with the committee.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers the effect on partnerships and describes the concrete change made.

forthrightness.statement: The repeal of section 7AA does remove the requirement for the chief executive of Oranga Tamariki to report to the public at least once a year on the impact of measures on improving outcomes for Māori.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly confirms the reporting requirement is removed, then explains the alternative mechanisms.

forthrightness.statement: I'm actually grateful that reports of concern have increased—that means that people trust that Oranga Tamariki are going to do something when children are at risk. I have spent much of my time on 7AA because I believe safety and wellbeing should always come first.
forthrightness.explanation: Reframes the 35 percent rise positively and defends her focus, but doesn't directly grapple with the criticism of prioritising 7AA.

forthrightness.statement: instead of inciting fear, a member who themselves stated that they were the “smartest and most experienced”, as they declared themselves the other day, would understand the difference between reasonable force and physical violence.
forthrightness.explanation: Deflects into criticism of the questioner rather than giving the assurance asked for.

forthrightness.statement: some of these members that are part of the military-style academy pilot programme have committed some pretty serious crimes. They must have committed at least two crimes of 10 years or more, if sentenced. We need to make sure that they are safe from each other and that the staff are safe, and this is the middle ground that will make sure that they are all safe.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers what crimes the cohort is involved in with a concrete threshold.

forthrightness.statement: I consider that a survey that shows that 38.3 percent of the respondents said they were not concerned about their safety, and 26.9 percent said that they felt safer, a sign of success.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked about the failure to deliver 500 police and the 31 percent feeling less safe, he pivots entirely to favourable poll numbers.

forthrightness.statement: yes, I did stand by that commitment, because I watched, for six years under a previous Government, a raft of police Ministers coming through who took no responsibility. I wanted to take responsibility. I said that if people didn't feel safer after 12 months, then I would resign. But the good news is that 38.3 percent of respondents who filled out a recent survey said that they're not concerned about their safety, and 26.9 percent said that they felt safer.
forthrightness.explanation: Confirms he stood by the pledge but avoids reconciling it with the failure to deliver 500 police.

forthrightness.statement: We in this Government have invested $225 million to fund recruitment and equipping and training our police officers, and we are on target to deliver our 500 additional police.
forthrightness.explanation: Pivots from the question about police attending suicide events to recruitment talking points.

forthrightness.statement: All those questions regarding the Tertiary Education Commission should be directed to the Minister.
forthrightness.explanation: Deflects a specific funding concern to another Minister rather than addressing it on behalf of Universities.

civility.statement: Well, there you go again: the degrowth Greens would be happy to see jobs go offshore and aluminium produced in coal boilers overseas. This side of the House backs jobs and growth in our regions.
civility.explanation: 'Degrowth Greens' label and imputing they want jobs offshore is a strawman attack.

civility.statement: I reject the premise of the question. Oh, how rich it is for the Greens—the degrowth Greens—to talk about the components around being de-competitive or anti-competitive.
civility.explanation: Mocking 'how rich' and the 'degrowth' label rather than the substance.

civility.statement: Does he think it's fair to give Rio Tinto an extra $37 million a year power bill subsidy, via free carbon credits, in the same week that households across the country are set to get a double-digit rise to their power bills?
civility.explanation: Harsh but focused on the policy and its equity, not the person.

civility.statement: Does he agree with the Climate Change Commission that free allocation of carbon credits weakens price incentives for emissions reduction and that the current approach to allocation is not aligned with our climate change targets?
civility.explanation: Substantive, policy-focused question.

civility.statement: If the member had listened to my answers, he would have heard that we are increasing funding for primary care. He's trying to find a conspiracy here. The degrowth Greens are trying to find a conspiracy here.
civility.explanation: 'Trying to find a conspiracy' and the 'degrowth Greens' label misrepresent the question.

civility.statement: I'd tell that senior citizen to write to Winston Peters and Simeon Brown on this matter because they're more likely to do something about it than the Labour Party, who just manufacture complaints.
civility.explanation: 'Manufacture complaints' impugns the opposition's motives.

civility.statement: We are definitely going to stop the scaremongering about the rainbow community—and they're writing to me right now in their thousands about the way they've been miscast by members of the Green Party... And we know why they're resigning in massive numbers from the Green Party right now
civility.explanation: Attacks the Green Party by attributing motives and casting blame.

civility.statement: instead of inciting fear, a member who themselves stated that they were the “smartest and most experienced”, as they declared themselves the other day, would understand the difference between reasonable force and physical violence.
civility.explanation: Personal dig quoting the member's earlier self-description to belittle them.

civility.statement: Why has she spent so much time on the repeal of section 7AA while, under her watch, reports of concern have increased by a massive 35 percent?
civility.explanation: 'Under her watch' juxtaposition is pointed but stops short of a personal insult.

civility.statement: Does he take responsibility for the higher doctors fees and the reduced access to general, urgent, and mental care because this Government continues to underfund community GP care, and, if so, does he commit to increasing funding for community care?
civility.explanation: Accusatory ('continues to underfund') but directed at policy and funding, not the person.

civility.statement: Does he stand by his commitment to resign one year into the job if New Zealanders didn't feel more safe and we didn't have control back of our streets, given that 31 percent of New Zealanders feel less safe, there are more gang members peddling more methamphetamine on our streets, and he has failed to deliver the 500 police he promised New Zealand in two years?
civility.explanation: Aggressive but anchored in the Minister's own commitment and record.

civility.statement: What's more likely to make progress against methamphetamine's baleful impact on our community: either toughening up gang laws so that the police have more tools to deal with gangs, or giving money to Sonny Tau to do rehabilitation programmes in the Hawke's Bay?
civility.explanation: A leading, loaded framing (later corrected for naming the wrong person) that belittles rehabilitation funding.

civility.statement: Why, when all of Whakatāne's obstetric and gynaecology specialists departed in January, were birthing women offered financial support for travel, but support was not offered for women seeking abortion?
civility.explanation: Probing and adversarial but focused on the service and policy.

civility.statement: Does he agree with Christopher Luxon that “We've got to look after our seniors”; if so, why did he cut the number of beds for older patients by 50 percent in the downgraded new Dunedin Hospital?
civility.explanation: Sharp but grounded in a factual policy claim rather than personal attack.

civility.statement: I omitted to mention that apparently the green groups are concerned about underground mining because it interferes with the reproductive patterns of frogs.
civility.explanation: Mocking, reductive caricature of opponents' environmental concerns.

civility.statement: Anzac Day must be much more inclusive. Its focus must be not solely on the past but also recognising already the comments that are quite rightly made around the country on 25 April that it represents to the future as well as the present. We have a duty to honour those who serve us.
civility.explanation: Respectful, elevated tone acknowledging shared national values.

civility.statement: We support this bill. What I say to those who are proposed to come under the remit of this particular bill, in changing the Anzac Day legislation, is that I want them to continue to remember the specific days that are important to them.
civility.explanation: Respectful and cooperative on a shared-values matter.

civility.statement: We want to say to the Minister and to this Government that, in a true bipartisan approach, we would be more than happy to make sure a door is open so that we can have those discussions to honour these people in the way that they deserve. We leave that door open to the Minister, and we look forward to ongoing conversation on this bill and the matter that I've just raised.
civility.explanation: Warm, respectful, and consensus-building across party lines.

civility.statement: Does she think provisions in the Oranga Tamariki (Responding to Serious Youth Offending) Amendment Bill allowing the use of physical force against children in State care breach the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child to be protected from all forms of physical violence?
civility.explanation: Confrontational framing but directed at the bill's provisions.

civility.statement: So that gives them a reason to get a hiding, girl, like my lawns?
civility.explanation: Interjection using 'girl' dismissively and a flippant 'hiding' analogy that trivialises the debate and belittles the Minister.

rigor.statement: Well, there you go again: the degrowth Greens would be happy to see jobs go offshore and aluminium produced in coal boilers overseas. This side of the House backs jobs and growth in our regions.
rigor.explanation: Strawman — attributes an extreme position to opponents rather than engaging the argument.

rigor.statement: Does he think it's fair to give Rio Tinto an extra $37 million a year power bill subsidy, via free carbon credits, in the same week that households across the country are set to get a double-digit rise to their power bills?
rigor.explanation: Pointed juxtaposition of corporate subsidy and household bills, but the two are rhetorically linked rather than causally argued.

rigor.statement: Does he agree with the Climate Change Commission that free allocation of carbon credits weakens price incentives for emissions reduction and that the current approach to allocation is not aligned with our climate change targets?
rigor.explanation: Grounds the challenge in the Climate Change Commission's stated position rather than assertion.

rigor.statement: We are definitely going to stop the scaremongering about the rainbow community—and they're writing to me right now in their thousands about the way they've been miscast by members of the Green Party... And we know why they're resigning in massive numbers from the Green Party right now
rigor.explanation: Relies on vague appeals to unnamed correspondence rather than evidence.

rigor.statement: While section 7AA was well intended, it has created uncertainty for social workers when making decisions about the best interests and wellbeing of a child, as it puts a child's ethnicity first and their wellbeing second.
rigor.explanation: Offers a stated mechanism (legislative conflict) but the 'ethnicity first, wellbeing second' framing is a contested characterisation asserted as fact.

rigor.statement: I'm actually grateful that reports of concern have increased—that means that people trust that Oranga Tamariki are going to do something when children are at risk. I have spent much of my time on 7AA because I believe safety and wellbeing should always come first.
rigor.explanation: Interprets rising reports of concern as evidence of trust without support for that causal reading.

rigor.statement: instead of inciting fear, a member who themselves stated that they were the “smartest and most experienced”, as they declared themselves the other day, would understand the difference between reasonable force and physical violence.
rigor.explanation: Relies on 'inciting fear' framing rather than addressing the substance.

rigor.statement: some of these members that are part of the military-style academy pilot programme have committed some pretty serious crimes. They must have committed at least two crimes of 10 years or more, if sentenced. We need to make sure that they are safe from each other and that the staff are safe, and this is the middle ground that will make sure that they are all safe.
rigor.explanation: Grounds the safety rationale in the seriousness of the offending, though the safety-outcome link is asserted.

rigor.statement: Why has she spent so much time on the repeal of section 7AA while, under her watch, reports of concern have increased by a massive 35 percent?
rigor.explanation: Implies a link between her focus on 7AA and rising reports of concern without establishing causation.

rigor.statement: Does he take responsibility for the higher doctors fees and the reduced access to general, urgent, and mental care because this Government continues to underfund community GP care, and, if so, does he commit to increasing funding for community care?
rigor.explanation: Asserts underfunding as the cause of higher fees and reduced access without laying out the evidence.

rigor.statement: 38.3 percent of respondents said they were not concerned about their safety, and 26.9 percent said they felt safer. The fact that 65 percent of New Zealanders feel safe or safer than they did 12 months ago is a reflection of the hard work of our police officers.
rigor.explanation: The 65 percent aggregate is constructed by combining non-equivalent poll categories.

rigor.statement: Does he stand by his commitment to resign one year into the job if New Zealanders didn't feel more safe and we didn't have control back of our streets, given that 31 percent of New Zealanders feel less safe, there are more gang members peddling more methamphetamine on our streets, and he has failed to deliver the 500 police he promised New Zealand in two years?
rigor.explanation: Marshals specific data points, though it bundles several claims into one accusation.

rigor.statement: What's more likely to make progress against methamphetamine's baleful impact on our community: either toughening up gang laws so that the police have more tools to deal with gangs, or giving money to Sonny Tau to do rehabilitation programmes in the Hawke's Bay?
rigor.explanation: False dichotomy — poses enforcement and rehabilitation as mutually exclusive options.

rigor.statement: Why, when all of Whakatāne's obstetric and gynaecology specialists departed in January, were birthing women offered financial support for travel, but support was not offered for women seeking abortion?
rigor.explanation: Draws a pointed inconsistency from specific facts, though it implies motive.

rigor.statement: Does he agree with Christopher Luxon that “We've got to look after our seniors”; if so, why did he cut the number of beds for older patients by 50 percent in the downgraded new Dunedin Hospital?
rigor.explanation: Sets a stated value against a specific decision to expose an inconsistency.

rigor.statement: I omitted to mention that apparently the green groups are concerned about underground mining because it interferes with the reproductive patterns of frogs.
rigor.explanation: Dismisses a stated concern by ridicule rather than engaging its substance.

rigor.statement: I expect and welcome an increase in tertiary enrolments this year. An increase would be positive, as we know higher education contributes to higher earnings and employment rates, contributing to economic growth.
rigor.explanation: Links education to earnings/employment, a broadly evidenced claim, though asserted rather than sourced.

rigor.statement: Legislation passed just last night with the unanimous support of the House—I'm pleased and grateful to acknowledge—will see up to 250,000 new products available to flow into New Zealand this year alone. This means that our designers, builders, and DIY Kiwis will have far more choice for the products they use. More choice means more competition, greater resilience in terms of supply chain, greater innovation, and downward pressure on prices.
rigor.explanation: Chains choice → competition → prices reasonably, but the downstream effects are asserted.

rigor.statement: Does she think provisions in the Oranga Tamariki (Responding to Serious Youth Offending) Amendment Bill allowing the use of physical force against children in State care breach the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child to be protected from all forms of physical violence?
rigor.explanation: Grounds the challenge in a named international instrument, though 'physical force' is framed as 'violence'.

rigor.statement: So that gives them a reason to get a hiding, girl, like my lawns?
rigor.explanation: A rhetorical jibe, not an argument.

charisma.statement: Well, there you go again: the degrowth Greens would be happy to see jobs go offshore and aluminium produced in coal boilers overseas. This side of the House backs jobs and growth in our regions.
charisma.explanation: Us-vs-them framing that rallies his own side.

charisma.statement: I reject the premise of the question. Oh, how rich it is for the Greens—the degrowth Greens—to talk about the components around being de-competitive or anti-competitive.
charisma.explanation: Combative, appeals only to his own side.

charisma.statement: If the member had listened to my answers, he would have heard that we are increasing funding for primary care. He's trying to find a conspiracy here. The degrowth Greens are trying to find a conspiracy here.
charisma.explanation: Dismissive and partisan rather than persuasive.

charisma.statement: I'd tell that senior citizen to write to Winston Peters and Simeon Brown on this matter because they're more likely to do something about it than the Labour Party, who just manufacture complaints.
charisma.explanation: Combative, dismissive of the questioner's side.

charisma.statement: Anzac Day must be much more inclusive. Its focus must be not solely on the past but also recognising already the comments that are quite rightly made around the country on 25 April that it represents to the future as well as the present. We have a duty to honour those who serve us.
charisma.explanation: Inclusive, unifying framing seeking broad common ground on commemoration.

charisma.statement: We support this bill. What I say to those who are proposed to come under the remit of this particular bill, in changing the Anzac Day legislation, is that I want them to continue to remember the specific days that are important to them.
charisma.explanation: Constructive cross-party support with an inclusive appeal to those affected.

charisma.statement: We want to say to the Minister and to this Government that, in a true bipartisan approach, we would be more than happy to make sure a door is open so that we can have those discussions to honour these people in the way that they deserve. We leave that door open to the Minister, and we look forward to ongoing conversation on this bill and the matter that I've just raised.
charisma.explanation: Explicitly bipartisan, invites the Government into ongoing collaboration.

divination.statement: This initiative will deliver 10,579 additional procedures by mid-2025. Patients are already seeing the benefits of this announcement, with 2,000 elective procedures already completed, including cataracts, and hip and knee replacements.
divination.explanation: Predicts 10,579 procedures by mid-2025; plausible given early progress but not yet realised.

divination.statement: I'm advised that Health New Zealand is actively recruiting for those positions to have that service restored within 12 months.
divination.explanation: Predicts service restored within 12 months; contingent on recruitment succeeding.

divination.statement: Development West Coast says that for every mining job in the region, two others are created elsewhere; 100 new jobs at a mine. But it's not only in the West Coast; in Coromandel, the Wharekirauponga Underground Mine is likely to sustain over 1,000 jobs.
divination.explanation: Predicts the Wharekirauponga mine will sustain over 1,000 jobs — plausible but speculative and project-dependent.

divination.statement: We in this Government have invested $225 million to fund recruitment and equipping and training our police officers, and we are on target to deliver our 500 additional police.
divination.explanation: Predicts the 500 additional police will be delivered; contested elsewhere in the same session.

divination.statement: I expect and welcome an increase in tertiary enrolments this year. An increase would be positive, as we know higher education contributes to higher earnings and employment rates, contributing to economic growth.
divination.explanation: Predicts rising enrolments this year; plausible in a higher-unemployment context but not yet confirmed.

divination.statement: Legislation passed just last night with the unanimous support of the House—I'm pleased and grateful to acknowledge—will see up to 250,000 new products available to flow into New Zealand this year alone. This means that our designers, builders, and DIY Kiwis will have far more choice for the products they use. More choice means more competition, greater resilience in terms of supply chain, greater innovation, and downward pressure on prices.
divination.explanation: Predicts downward pressure on prices and greater resilience; directionally plausible but unquantified.

authenticity.statement: We agree entirely with the Prime Minister's comments about looking after our seniors—after all, we invented the phrase “Looking after our seniors”, and that's why we've done so much in the past.
authenticity.explanation: Asserts a long record of caring for seniors but offers no action to counter the specific bed-cut charge.

authenticity.statement: I have consistently said that nothing about this repeal will stop Oranga Tamariki's existing strategic partnerships with iwi and Māori organisations or prevent them from entering into new ones. During the select committee process, it was recommended that the part of section 7AA relating to the strategic partnerships should be retained in legislation. We considered this recommendation and agreed with the committee.
authenticity.explanation: Claims a consistent position and shows it was matched by accepting the committee's recommendation to retain the partnerships provision.

authenticity.statement: I'm actually grateful that reports of concern have increased—that means that people trust that Oranga Tamariki are going to do something when children are at risk. I have spent much of my time on 7AA because I believe safety and wellbeing should always come first.
authenticity.explanation: Ties her time-allocation to a stated consistent value of safety first.

authenticity.statement: yes, I did stand by that commitment, because I watched, for six years under a previous Government, a raft of police Ministers coming through who took no responsibility. I wanted to take responsibility. I said that if people didn't feel safer after 12 months, then I would resign. But the good news is that 38.3 percent of respondents who filled out a recent survey said that they're not concerned about their safety, and 26.9 percent said that they felt safer.
authenticity.explanation: Made a specific resignation pledge tied to people feeling safer; with 31 percent feeling less safe he does not resign but reinterprets the metric to declare success.

authenticity.statement: the commitment made by the Prime Minister at the RSA's annual conference last year is being honoured by the introduction of this legislation, and we've committed to having it passed before Anzac Day of 2026.
authenticity.explanation: Ties the bill to a prior public commitment and presents its introduction as delivery on that word.

authenticity.statement: But, actually, I stand by that. I think that the way that lawyers have become so necessary to so many people is a real problem.
authenticity.explanation: A trained lawyer maintaining, even when challenged in the House, that lawyers are too costly and should be cut out where possible — she holds a position against her own professional interest, a consistency signal rather than self-serving positioning.

authenticity.statement: They could have been bills that started under us and this Government has finished off, or that this Government has introduced, building on work that the previous Government had done. There has been broad support. Here comes another one.
authenticity.explanation: Consistent with his own supportive stance on the bill; frames Labour as a constructive backer, matching the party's stated support in the debate.

rigor.statement: I also think that, by lowering the fee, there may be a real advantage in that people would come to the court or to the disputes tribunal more readily and not take an option up of going to the District Court. So it probably would pay for itself very quickly to have a lower fee.
rigor.explanation: A plausible behavioural/cost argument (lower fee → higher uptake → self-funding) but no data offered; reasoning is directional and hedged ('may be', 'probably').

rigor.statement: One thing that we could look at is: actually recording these processes, because we now have a real technological advance and we could look at something where we recorded those, and we’d have a high-level supervision of the decisions that are being made at this level.
rigor.explanation: Reasoned response to the identified problem (no appeal right) — recording as an alternative accountability layer; logic follows but rests on an undeveloped 'technological advance' premise.

rigor.statement: if we don’t look after them, actually what we find is that they are angry, they end up with mental health issues, they end up with their children in dire situations because the whole system breaks down.
rigor.explanation: An escalating chain from unmet claims to anger to mental health to family breakdown to 'the whole system breaks down' — appeal to emotion / slippery-slope with no evidence linking the steps.

rigor.statement: The New Zealand courts’ Rules Committee recommended that the cap be upped. Why wouldn’t we listen to them? They know what they’re talking about.
rigor.explanation: Leans on an appeal to authority ('they know what they're talking about') rather than the substance of the recommendation, though the authority is a relevant expert body.

rigor.statement: I mean, you only have to look over there to see that many people make lots of mistakes!
rigor.explanation: Uses opponents' supposed fallibility as a rhetorical aside — an ad hominem flourish with no bearing on the argument about appeal rights.

rigor.statement: if a mistake is made in a tribunal like this, they have to start all over again. And they only go to the same level—it’s not like in the courts, where you can appeal to a higher level of court and look at it from a different angle. It’s the same tribunal looking at the same issue if a mistake is made.
rigor.explanation: Sound structural argument: without an appeal right, error correction is limited to the same-level tribunal, correctly contrasted with the tiered court system; conclusion follows from the premise.

rigor.statement: We recognise that the fee—$468—reflects the costs that are incurred to run the disputes tribunal, but we also must recognise that $468 is actually quite a lot for many working people, especially people on very low incomes, like the minimum wage, or lower if they’re part-time, of course. When you consider that the filing fee for the District Court is $260—almost half—surely there could be some wriggle room there, some flexibility.
rigor.explanation: Concedes the fee reflects real costs, then uses a concrete comparator (District Court $260 vs $468) to argue there is room to lower it — evidence-based and balanced.

divination.statement: I also think that, by lowering the fee, there may be a real advantage in that people would come to the court or to the disputes tribunal more readily and not take an option up of going to the District Court. So it probably would pay for itself very quickly to have a lower fee.
divination.explanation: Prediction that a lower fee would 'pay for itself very quickly' — plausible but unquantified and untested, no timeframe beyond 'quickly'.

divination.statement: if we don’t look after them, actually what we find is that they are angry, they end up with mental health issues, they end up with their children in dire situations because the whole system breaks down.
divination.explanation: Predicts social/psychological harms if the vulnerable aren't protected; directionally plausible but vague and unfalsifiable in magnitude.

veracity.statement: They told me that, presently, to get a mediation in the Employment Relations Authority, it’s taking 10 weeks.
veracity.explanation: A specific factual claim about ERA mediation delays, attributed to union members (hearsay) but consistent with widely reported tribunal backlogs; plausible though unverified in the text.

veracity.statement: The average salary in this country is under $70,000 and we are all on salaries that are about, I think, $170,000.
veracity.explanation: Backbench MP base salary of ~$168k is accurate ('about $170,000'); 'average salary under $70,000' is roughly right depending on the measure used — broadly accurate, slightly loose.

veracity.statement: The change in the level at which you will be able to apply to the disputes tribunal will mean that a Master’s degree student who was paid just $9,000 for a full year’s worth of work, who had to cut her losses and abandon the claim for the $41,000 she was owed, would be able to actually take that claim under this new law.
veracity.explanation: A specific real-world example whose particulars can't be verified from the text, but the mechanism (a claim above the old $30k cap now eligible under $60k) is accurate.

veracity.statement: The New Zealand courts’ Rules Committee recommended that the cap be upped. Why wouldn’t we listen to them? They know what they’re talking about.
veracity.explanation: Accurate that the courts' Rules Committee recommended lifting the cap — the stated basis for the bill.

veracity.statement: Think about the minimum wage. It only went up 35c a couple of days ago.
veracity.explanation: The 1 April 2025 minimum wage rise was $23.15 to $23.50 — a 35c increase — matching the claim and its 'couple of days ago' timing for this 3 April debate.

veracity.statement: if a mistake is made in a tribunal like this, they have to start all over again. And they only go to the same level—it’s not like in the courts, where you can appeal to a higher level of court and look at it from a different angle. It’s the same tribunal looking at the same issue if a mistake is made.
veracity.explanation: Accurate characterisation of the disputes tribunal lacking a higher appeal avenue relative to the courts.

veracity.statement: We recognise that the fee—$468—reflects the costs that are incurred to run the disputes tribunal, but we also must recognise that $468 is actually quite a lot for many working people, especially people on very low incomes, like the minimum wage, or lower if they’re part-time, of course. When you consider that the filing fee for the District Court is $260—almost half—surely there could be some wriggle room there, some flexibility.
veracity.explanation: Figures cited ($468 tribunal fee, $260 District Court fee) are in the right range; '$260—almost half' of $468 is roughly accurate (~55%).

veracity.statement: Many countries, including Australia and the United Kingdom, already require notification where information is collected indirectly.
veracity.explanation: Broadly accurate: comparable jurisdictions including Australia and the UK impose transparency/notification obligations around indirect collection of personal information.

veracity.statement: Since 2012, New Zealand has held European Union “adequacy” status—one of only 15 jurisdictions to do so.
veracity.explanation: New Zealand was granted EU adequacy in 2012, and the count of adequacy jurisdictions is around this figure — accurate on the substance.

veracity.statement: The committee received 55 submissions on the bill, including a significant contribution from galleries, libraries, archives, and the museum sector.
veracity.explanation: A concrete procedural fact about the select committee process, of the kind on the parliamentary record and reliable at face value.

specificity.statement: They told me that, presently, to get a mediation in the Employment Relations Authority, it’s taking 10 weeks.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete forum (ERA), a concrete metric (mediation wait) and a figure (10 weeks).

specificity.statement: One thing that we could look at is: actually recording these processes, because we now have a real technological advance and we could look at something where we recorded those, and we’d have a high-level supervision of the decisions that are being made at this level.
specificity.explanation: Proposes a concrete mechanism (recording hearings for high-level supervision) as a check-and-balance, though the how/who/cost are left open.

specificity.statement: The average salary in this country is under $70,000 and we are all on salaries that are about, I think, $170,000.
specificity.explanation: Concrete figures for both average income and MP salary to make her affordability point.

specificity.statement: We’re a community and we need to support everyone in it. It is a very, very big part of the Labour Party that we believe there is our community: they are our children, they are our friends, they are our whānau, and we need to make sure that our system works for everyone in New Zealand, whether people are earning a minimum wage or less or they are earning a lot more. specificity.explanation: Value-laden appeal with no mechanism, figure or measure — a statement of belief rather than a concrete commitment.

specificity.statement: The change in the level at which you will be able to apply to the disputes tribunal will mean that a Master’s degree student who was paid just $9,000 for a full year’s worth of work, who had to cut her losses and abandon the claim for the $41,000 she was owed, would be able to actually take that claim under this new law.
specificity.explanation: Concrete illustrative case with precise figures ($9,000 paid, $41,000 owed) tied directly to the bill's raised cap.

specificity.statement: Think about the minimum wage. It only went up 35c a couple of days ago.
specificity.explanation: Precise figure and timeframe used to underline how large $60,000 is for low earners.

specificity.statement: Why wouldn’t the Government want to consider the prospect of having a right of appeal, not to dispute matters of fact but maybe just matters of law, so that people can have confidence in the process.
specificity.explanation: Proposes a defined, limited remedy — an appeal on matters of law only, not fact — rather than a vague call for 'more safeguards'.

specificity.statement: Many countries, including Australia and the United Kingdom, already require notification where information is collected indirectly.
specificity.explanation: Names specific comparator countries and the specific obligation (notification on indirect collection).

specificity.statement: Since 2012, New Zealand has held European Union “adequacy” status—one of only 15 jurisdictions to do so.
specificity.explanation: Precise date (2012) and count (one of only 15 jurisdictions).

specificity.statement: The committee received 55 submissions on the bill, including a significant contribution from galleries, libraries, archives, and the museum sector.
specificity.explanation: Exact submission count (55) and named the key contributing sector (GLAM).

specificity.statement: At second reading, Government shared with the House its intention to submit an Amendment Paper to maintain a six-month implementation period for the new information privacy principle to help agencies prepare to comply. It has since been decided to extend this period to a full year.
specificity.explanation: Concrete mechanism and figures — an Amendment Paper moving the implementation period from six months to a full 12 months.

charisma.statement: We’re a community and we need to support everyone in it. It is a very, very big part of the Labour Party that we believe there is our community: they are our children, they are our friends, they are our whānau, and we need to make sure that our system works for everyone in New Zealand, whether people are earning a minimum wage or less or they are earning a lot more. We are part of the same whānau.
