divination.explanation: Implicit prediction that a bill by year-end will unlock company access/investment — plausible but contingent.

charisma.statement: The chair of the Electoral Commission is a very important role, as the Hon Dr Duncan Webb outlined, and it does need someone who has some experience—obviously, a legal background is excellent—but is calm, level-headed, and can work through issues and ensure this important organisation for our democracy is led well
charisma.explanation: Cross-party, consensual tone on a non-partisan appointment, explicitly endorsing a colleague's (Webb's) framing.

charisma.statement: This bill is another example of the Government's focus on law and order, and it is a reminder that our focus on reducing crime is about reducing harm—in this instance, preventing harm to children.
charisma.explanation: Confident partisan framing that appeals to the Government's own side rather than seeking common ground.

charisma.statement: we don't need to be claiming it for one side or the other when we're actually just working together to protect particularly vulnerable young people
charisma.explanation: Explicitly seeks cross-party common ground and de-emphasises partisan credit-claiming.

charisma.statement: the key messages here, guys, is that this Government is actually focused on putting the victims first and keeping our community safe.
charisma.explanation: Rallying line aimed at the Government's own side rather than persuading opponents.

charisma.statement: I know in cases like this and in bills like this that the committee can work very collegially and very constructively together.
charisma.explanation: Invokes cross-party constructive cooperation on the committee.

charisma.statement: It is in this institution and some of us here today, who turn a blind eye to our own, but, on an international scale, strive to maintain what can only be described as a façade—a façade that, underneath, advocates for others and not our own.
charisma.explanation: Condemnatory framing that divides rather than builds consensus across the House.

charisma.statement: This bill is another example of this Government's laser-like focus on law and order.
charisma.explanation: Partisan applause line aimed at its own side.

charisma.statement: What we saw from Ministers was a pitting of Dunedin against other regions for the health dollar, and that is abhorrent.
charisma.explanation: Us-vs-Ministers framing that rallies Dunedin rather than seeking cross-party resolution.

charisma.statement: I can see that members on the other side of the House are geometrically challenged—sorry to hear that
charisma.explanation: Belittling opponents undercuts consensus-building despite the strong underlying case.

charisma.statement: I want to commend Rachel Brooking for bringing it up. It's an absolute guts-ache what these people have been through
charisma.explanation: Reaches across party lines to credit a Labour MP on a shared regional concern.

specificity.statement: The chair of the Electoral Commission is a very important role, as the Hon Dr Duncan Webb outlined, and it does need someone who has some experience—obviously, a legal background is excellent—but is calm, level-headed, and can work through issues and ensure this important organisation for our democracy is led well
specificity.explanation: Names desirable qualities (legal background, level-headedness) but no concrete criteria or measures.

specificity.statement: Most importantly, it requires offenders to report if a child is going to be living at the same address as them 48 hours before this occurs, rather than 72 hours after, making it easier for registry staff to contact the principal caregiver
specificity.explanation: Concrete mechanism and precise timeframes (48 hours before vs 72 hours after).

specificity.statement: the bill adds seven additional qualifying offences to the Act... The seven additional offences are four Prostitution Reform Act 2003 offences which were unintended omissions from the original Act, two Crimes Act offences, and one Customs and Excise Act 2018 offence
specificity.explanation: Precise count and named statutes for each added offence.

specificity.statement: This bill is another example of the Government's focus on law and order, and it is a reminder that our focus on reducing crime is about reducing harm—in this instance, preventing harm to children.
specificity.explanation: Slogan-level framing ('focus on law and order') with no measure or mechanism attached.

specificity.statement: Given that it was actually a piece of work that had its first regulatory impact statement in 2022, it indicates that, of course, the underlying policy is something we agree with.
specificity.explanation: Anchors the claim to a dated document, though without further detail.

specificity.statement: Statistics show us that less than 10 percent of all sex offending is reported, and that less than half of that results in conviction.
specificity.explanation: Cites specific proportions to ground the argument.

specificity.statement: there are several New Zealand Bill of Rights Act inconsistencies attached to the existence of the register which have been deemed unjustifiable by the Office of the Attorney-General
specificity.explanation: Names the rights (lesser penalty, double jeopardy) and their source, though without citation detail.

specificity.statement: require offenders travelling out of the country to report this information at least seven days in advance rather than the current 48 hours in advance; require offenders to report their return to New Zealand no more than 72 hours after re-entering
specificity.explanation: Precise timeframes for travel-reporting changes.

specificity.statement: like banning gang insignia, giving police the power to issue dispersal notices, the new legislation introducing powers for courts to issue non-consorting orders to stop specified gang offenders from associating or communicating with one another for up to three years
specificity.explanation: Names concrete measures and a duration ('up to three years').

specificity.statement: the key messages here, guys, is that this Government is actually focused on putting the victims first and keeping our community safe.
specificity.explanation: Slogan-level summary with no measure or mechanism.

specificity.statement: By my count this is the 22nd bill the Justice Committee may well consider this term, and it is welcomed because this is obviously a needed change.
specificity.explanation: Gives a concrete figure (22nd bill) though self-qualified as 'by my count'.

specificity.statement: When our tamariki Māori are 70 percent of children in State care and are also 80 percent of those currently experiencing abuse within that very system, how much louder do we need to be?
specificity.explanation: Uses concrete proportions to anchor the point.

specificity.statement: This bill is another example of this Government's laser-like focus on law and order.
specificity.explanation: Pure slogan ('laser-like focus') with no detail or measure.

specificity.statement: Earlier this year in the House, I asked questions about the proposal of Oranga Tamariki to cut their International Child Protection Unit. We understand that there are cuts to the teams at the Department of Internal Affairs and Customs which work with the exploitation material around young children.
specificity.explanation: Names specific agencies and units affected.

specificity.statement: I want to acknowledge that Labour had done some work on these provisions that are in this proposed legislation to add a clarified list of personal information that will be reported, and amendments to the requirements around reporting travel plans, and also adding seven additional new qualifying offences.
specificity.explanation: Points to specific provisions attributed to that earlier work.

specificity.statement: The child protection amendment bill is part of a raft of legislation that the Government is enabling, including the gangs legislation which has passed, which will be enacted by mid-November.
specificity.explanation: Gives a concrete milestone (gangs legislation passed, enacted by mid-November).

specificity.statement: Last year alone, on an average day, this road got 34,000 vehicles. At its peak in the morning, 2,000 vehicles travel down this road.
specificity.explanation: Precise traffic figures (34,000 daily average, 2,000 peak).

specificity.statement: The first is no parking 24/7... The second is redeveloping the top of Onewa Road to make the traffic flow much better. The third is allowing freight trucks and trucks to use the T3 lane... The fourth area is around dynamic signage for the T3 lane.
specificity.explanation: Enumerated, concrete proposed solutions drawn from a corridor study.

specificity.statement: It was an amazing, beautiful, and sunny Saturday on which 35,000 people gathered outside the dental school... Now, 35,000 people is a quarter of Dunedin's population.
specificity.explanation: Gives an exact figure and contextualises it as a share of the city's population.

specificity.statement: In Wellington's morning peak, buses represent only 3 percent of the vehicles on Thorndon Quay. Guess how many of the people they carry? That 3 percent of vehicles carries 60 percent—six, zero—of the people. On Adelaide Road, buses are 1 percent of the vehicles but carry 40 percent of the people.
specificity.explanation: Named streets with precise vehicle-share and people-share percentages.

specificity.statement: If you look at the census data, vehicle use in Wellington has continued to decline, with driving dropping below 50 percent for the first time, and working from home has increased, but so have public transport patronage and walking and cycling
specificity.explanation: Cites a concrete threshold (driving below 50%) and a data source.

specificity.statement: when it comes to the tunnel, what's been talked about is potentially a four-kilometre underground tunnel; $6 billion would be a conservative estimate for a tunnel like this
specificity.explanation: Gives concrete dimensions and a costed figure for the proposed tunnel.

specificity.statement: For $6 billion, we could have light rail from Island Bay, Miramar, and the airport to the city; added bus routes with all electric buses, new bendy buses; a new ferry, electric ferries; and port infrastructure for the eastern suburbs—with money left over to work on our regional rail network
specificity.explanation: Lists named routes and concrete alternative investments an equivalent budget could fund.

specificity.statement: Gore got over 200 millimetres—anecdotal evidence I'm sure some have offered. Manapōuri was certainly 260 or more.
specificity.explanation: Names locations and millimetre totals.

specificity.statement: One chap said to me, "I spent $90,000—$90,000 more than I had, just to be criticised by all the people that I wasn't doing enough; all the officials, all the local council—$90,000 I didn't have."
specificity.explanation: Concrete dollar figure, but as an individual illustrative story rather than aggregate data.

specificity.statement: They've had nine major storms since June 2021—nine major storms since June 2021—of course including Gabrielle. They said that they had had 3,000 roading faults, eight bridges lost, 53 more scoured out, 73 affected by slash, and 250 major dropouts.
specificity.explanation: Precise counts across storms, roading faults, bridges and dropouts.

specificity.statement: they have gone from a business formed in 2014 with nothing—no employees, no infrastructure—to now having a processing factory; a marine farm, and looking to up to about nine more marine farms; three vessels; and 180 staff all learning new skills.
specificity.explanation: Dates, headcount, vessel and farm counts.

veracity.statement: Most importantly, it requires offenders to report if a child is going to be living at the same address as them 48 hours before this occurs, rather than 72 hours after, making it easier for registry staff to contact the principal caregiver
veracity.explanation: Accurate description of the bill's reporting change; verifiable against the text of the amendment.

veracity.statement: the bill adds seven additional qualifying offences to the Act... The seven additional offences are four Prostitution Reform Act 2003 offences which were unintended omissions from the original Act, two Crimes Act offences, and one Customs and Excise Act 2018 offence
veracity.explanation: Detailed, checkable factual claim about the bill's contents; consistent with other speakers' accounts.

veracity.statement: Given that it was actually a piece of work that had its first regulatory impact statement in 2022, it indicates that, of course, the underlying policy is something we agree with.
veracity.explanation: Specific, checkable factual claim about the policy's origin (2022 regulatory impact statement).

veracity.statement: Statistics show us that less than 10 percent of all sex offending is reported, and that less than half of that results in conviction.
veracity.explanation: Broadly consistent with known low reporting/conviction rates for sexual offending, though exact figures vary by source.

veracity.statement: They also show us that most child sex offending is perpetuated by people known to the child and who have no prior relevant conviction.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with research that most child sexual abuse is by known persons often without prior convictions.

veracity.statement: Much of the evidence about registers suggests they do not have harm prevention effects—although we note that much of the research comes from different jurisdictions which have varying levels of difference to the New Zealand context and register.
veracity.explanation: Directionally supported by international literature but genuinely contested; hedged appropriately.

veracity.statement: there are several New Zealand Bill of Rights Act inconsistencies attached to the existence of the register which have been deemed unjustifiable by the Office of the Attorney-General
veracity.explanation: Refers to an identifiable source (Attorney-General's BORA assessment); plausible but stated broadly.

veracity.statement: require offenders travelling out of the country to report this information at least seven days in advance rather than the current 48 hours in advance; require offenders to report their return to New Zealand no more than 72 hours after re-entering
veracity.explanation: Accurate account of the bill's reporting amendments.

veracity.statement: By my count this is the 22nd bill the Justice Committee may well consider this term, and it is welcomed because this is obviously a needed change.
veracity.explanation: Self-reported tally, plausible but unverifiable from the text.

veracity.statement: When our tamariki Māori are 70 percent of children in State care and are also 80 percent of those currently experiencing abuse within that very system, how much louder do we need to be?
veracity.explanation: Cites high over-representation figures for tamariki Māori in care; broadly consistent with known data, though precise percentages are contestable.

veracity.statement: Earlier this year in the House, I asked questions about the proposal of Oranga Tamariki to cut their International Child Protection Unit. We understand that there are cuts to the teams at the Department of Internal Affairs and Customs which work with the exploitation material around young children.
veracity.explanation: Specific, checkable claims about proposed cuts; plausible and referenced to her own prior questions, though details unverified here.

veracity.statement: The child protection amendment bill is part of a raft of legislation that the Government is enabling, including the gangs legislation which has passed, which will be enacted by mid-November.
veracity.explanation: Checkable claim about the gangs legislation's passage and commencement timing.

veracity.statement: Last year alone, on an average day, this road got 34,000 vehicles. At its peak in the morning, 2,000 vehicles travel down this road.
veracity.explanation: Concrete, verifiable-sounding data drawn from an Auckland Transport corridor study.

veracity.statement: It was an amazing, beautiful, and sunny Saturday on which 35,000 people gathered outside the dental school... Now, 35,000 people is a quarter of Dunedin's population.
veracity.explanation: Attendance and population-share figures are concrete and broadly consistent with reported Dunedin hospital protests, though crowd counts are estimates.

veracity.statement: I was there when we were told by the National Party—by the leader, by the spokesperson for health, and by the candidates standing in Dunedin and the Otago areas—that they would do exactly what the business case said.
veracity.explanation: First-hand claim about National's pre-election commitments; plausible but self-reported and contested.

veracity.statement: We also heard exaggerated claims of $3 billion for things that have never been part of this in-patient build, and that is a disgrace as well.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the $3 billion figure is inflated and misattributed; a genuinely contested claim presented as settled fact.

veracity.statement: In Wellington's morning peak, buses represent only 3 percent of the vehicles on Thorndon Quay. Guess how many of the people they carry? That 3 percent of vehicles carries 60 percent—six, zero—of the people. On Adelaide Road, buses are 1 percent of the vehicles but carry 40 percent of the people.
veracity.explanation: Specific corridor mode-share statistics consistent with Wellington transport data.

veracity.statement: If you look at the census data, vehicle use in Wellington has continued to decline, with driving dropping below 50 percent for the first time, and working from home has increased, but so have public transport patronage and walking and cycling
veracity.explanation: Attributes trend to census data; broadly consistent with Wellington commuting patterns, though exact thresholds are checkable.

veracity.statement: Gore got over 200 millimetres—anecdotal evidence I'm sure some have offered. Manapōuri was certainly 260 or more.
veracity.explanation: Specific rainfall figures, self-qualified as anecdotal; plausible for the described flooding but not sourced.

veracity.statement: They've had nine major storms since June 2021—nine major storms since June 2021—of course including Gabrielle. They said that they had had 3,000 roading faults, eight bridges lost, 53 more scoured out, 73 affected by slash, and 250 major dropouts.
veracity.explanation: Detailed damage figures attributed to the local emergency management centre; specific and plausible for the East Cape.

veracity.statement: they have gone from a business formed in 2014 with nothing—no employees, no infrastructure—to now having a processing factory; a marine farm, and looking to up to about nine more marine farms; three vessels; and 180 staff all learning new skills.
veracity.explanation: Concrete growth figures for Whakatōhea Mussels; specific and checkable-sounding.

civility.statement: we don't need to be claiming it for one side or the other when we're actually just working together to protect particularly vulnerable young people
civility.explanation: Mild rebuke of the Minister but focused on the substance of shared work, not personal attack.

civility.statement: I know in cases like this and in bills like this that the committee can work very collegially and very constructively together.
civility.explanation: Respectful, collaborative framing of the process.

civility.statement: It is in this institution and some of us here today, who turn a blind eye to our own, but, on an international scale, strive to maintain what can only be described as a façade—a façade that, underneath, advocates for others and not our own.
civility.explanation: Accuses colleagues of hypocrisy ('turn a blind eye', 'façade')—pointed and personal rather than policy-focused.

civility.statement: Earlier this year in the House, I asked questions about the proposal of Oranga Tamariki to cut their International Child Protection Unit. We understand that there are cuts to the teams at the Department of Internal Affairs and Customs which work with the exploitation material around young children.
civility.explanation: Substantive policy criticism of the Government's wider record, not a personal attack.

civility.statement: whilst some of them seem very administrative... there always is the potential for things to have unintended consequences, so it does require a good close look.
civility.explanation: Measured, process-focused engagement building on a colleague's point.

civility.statement: I was there when we were told by the National Party—by the leader, by the spokesperson for health, and by the candidates standing in Dunedin and the Otago areas—that they would do exactly what the business case said.
civility.explanation: Sharp accusation of a broken promise but tied to a specific, substantive commitment rather than personal insult.

civility.statement: We also heard exaggerated claims of $3 billion for things that have never been part of this in-patient build, and that is a disgrace as well.
civility.explanation: 'Disgrace' and 'abhorrent' language escalates tone, though aimed at Ministers' claims rather than character.

civility.statement: What we saw from Ministers was a pitting of Dunedin against other regions for the health dollar, and that is abhorrent.
civility.explanation: Charges Ministers with a bad-faith tactic in heightened language ('abhorrent'), edging toward attack over substance.

civility.statement: I can see that members on the other side of the House are geometrically challenged—sorry to hear that
civility.explanation: Mocking personal jab at opponents' competence rather than engaging their argument.

civility.statement: the reason they care is because they fly into Wellington Airport and come to the Beehive, and they want to spend money from people right around New Zealand just so they think they can save a few minutes on some peak-hour travel
civility.explanation: Attributes bad motives to opponents instead of engaging the policy case.

civility.statement: I want to commend Rachel Brooking for bringing it up. It's an absolute guts-ache what these people have been through
civility.explanation: Warm, respectful acknowledgement of an opponent.

rigor.statement: these are people who don't have access to Wi-Fi... it's really important that we don't just have something that is administratively convenient for the police to manage but also something that actually works so that the offenders know what their obligations are and are equipped to meet them
rigor.explanation: Reasoned point about efficacy: notes a practical gap (serving notice by email to homeless/offline offenders) that undercuts the stated protective purpose.

rigor.statement: Statistics show us that less than 10 percent of all sex offending is reported, and that less than half of that results in conviction.
rigor.explanation: Uses data to build an evidence-led case questioning the register's likely reach.

rigor.statement: They also show us that most child sex offending is perpetuated by people known to the child and who have no prior relevant conviction.
rigor.explanation: Logical entailment: if most offenders have no prior conviction, a register of convicted offenders addresses a minority of risk.

rigor.statement: Much of the evidence about registers suggests they do not have harm prevention effects—although we note that much of the research comes from different jurisdictions which have varying levels of difference to the New Zealand context and register.
rigor.explanation: Evidence-based claim that also acknowledges its own limitation (jurisdictional transferability), a mark of disciplined reasoning.

rigor.statement: They are limits on the freedoms of those individuals, but they are justified, I think, in order to meet the policy objective, which is to keep our children safe.
rigor.explanation: Explicit proportionality reasoning: acknowledges rights limits and weighs them against a stated objective rather than dismissing them.

rigor.statement: When our tamariki Māori are 70 percent of children in State care and are also 80 percent of those currently experiencing abuse within that very system, how much louder do we need to be?
rigor.explanation: Data-supported contrast between domestic failures and overseas focus, though framed rhetorically.

rigor.statement: where was the protection for the thousands of children that endured abuse in State and faith-based care? Who protected them then and who protects them now?
rigor.explanation: Rhetorical questions carrying a real argument—that the bill's protective claims ring hollow against domestic care failures—but leaning on emotive framing.

rigor.statement: whilst some of them seem very administrative... there always is the potential for things to have unintended consequences, so it does require a good close look.
rigor.explanation: Reasoned caution: flags that ostensibly technical amendments can carry unintended consequences warranting scrutiny.

rigor.statement: In Wellington's morning peak, buses represent only 3 percent of the vehicles on Thorndon Quay. Guess how many of the people they carry? That 3 percent of vehicles carries 60 percent—six, zero—of the people. On Adelaide Road, buses are 1 percent of the vehicles but carry 40 percent of the people.
rigor.explanation: Marshals data to support the conclusion that buses move people far more efficiently than the vehicle counts suggest.

rigor.statement: For $6 billion, we could have light rail from Island Bay, Miramar, and the airport to the city; added bus routes with all electric buses, new bendy buses; a new ferry, electric ferries; and port infrastructure for the eastern suburbs—with money left over to work on our regional rail network
rigor.explanation: Opportunity-cost argument, though the comparative costings are asserted rather than evidenced.

rigor.statement: the reason they care is because they fly into Wellington Airport and come to the Beehive, and they want to spend money from people right around New Zealand just so they think they can save a few minutes on some peak-hour travel
rigor.explanation: Imputes self-interested motives to opponents (ad hominem) rather than rebutting their reasoning.

rigor.statement: One chap said to me, "I spent $90,000—$90,000 more than I had, just to be criticised by all the people that I wasn't doing enough; all the officials, all the local council—$90,000 I didn't have."
rigor.explanation: Argument rests on a single second-hand anecdote (appeal to anecdote) rather than representative evidence.

rigor.statement: if a young person leaves a programme part-way through to get into a job, the Ministry of Education says, "That's a fail. That's a fail because you didn't complete the course." I think that that is wrong. To me, that's a fantastic success that should be celebrated and not penalised.
rigor.explanation: Coherent critique that a completion-based metric misclassifies a good outcome (employment) as failure; reasoning follows, though the claim about MoE's stance is asserted.

strength.statement: like banning gang insignia, giving police the power to issue dispersal notices, the new legislation introducing powers for courts to issue non-consorting orders to stop specified gang offenders from associating or communicating with one another for up to three years
strength.explanation: Claims a slate of law-and-order measures the Government has advanced; some are enacted/in train, so partial demonstrated delivery.

strength.statement: The child protection amendment bill is part of a raft of legislation that the Government is enabling, including the gangs legislation which has passed, which will be enacted by mid-November.
strength.explanation: Points to legislation actually passed with a commencement date—demonstrated delivery rather than mere aspiration.

strength.statement: The first is no parking 24/7... The second is redeveloping the top of Onewa Road to make the traffic flow much better. The third is allowing freight trucks and trucks to use the T3 lane... The fourth area is around dynamic signage for the T3 lane.
strength.explanation: Concrete proposals he is advancing, but these are intentions/study outputs not yet delivered.

authenticity.statement: I want to acknowledge that Labour had done some work on these provisions that are in this proposed legislation to add a clarified list of personal information that will be reported, and amendments to the requirements around reporting travel plans, and also adding seven additional new qualifying offences.
authenticity.explanation: Claims her party's prior authorship of the provisions; consistent with other cross-party acknowledgements in the debate that the work began under the last Government.

divination.statement: under the leadership of Birkenhead local Dean Kimpton, and under the leadership and possible changes that are coming our way under Minister Simeon Brown, I'm really confident that AT—Auckland Transport—will be focused on actually delivering and listening to our communities in the future.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that Auckland Transport will improve delivery/responsiveness under new leadership—plausible but unproven, and outcome-dependent.

divination.statement: when it comes to the tunnel, what's been talked about is potentially a four-kilometre underground tunnel; $6 billion would be a conservative estimate for a tunnel like this
divination.explanation: Predicts the project's cost ('$6 billion, conservative'); plausible for large tunnels but an unbuilt-project estimate with wide uncertainty.

rigor.statement: I said a brief pause between each announcement, so that an appropriate point of order could be raised at the right time, would be proper, otherwise one has no opportunity to follow the Standing Orders and make a point of order at the right time.
rigor.explanation: Clear, logically structured procedural argument: a pause is needed because without it there is no opportunity to raise a timely point of order. Conclusion follows from the premise.

rigor.statement: was there an addendum to their communication with you, thanking the party and the mover of the changed law in 2018 to revive the “waka hopping bill”, in gratitude for that interposition back then, that assisted them to be the first ones ever to use it?
rigor.explanation: Highlights a genuine inconsistency (a party benefiting from waka-jumping law it opposed) but delivered as rhetorical point-scoring rather than reasoned argument.

rigor.statement: let’s also remember we also need to back our creativity, our innovation, right across our country, right across our economic performance as well, because if we don’t do that, we’re never going to lift the productivity that we need to lift.
rigor.explanation: Reasonable analogy from sport to economic innovation and productivity, but the causal link is asserted rather than evidenced.

rigor.statement: How does he justify the 133 percent increase in benefit sanctions over the last year when unemployment is the highest it has been in three years as a direct result of this Government cutting 7,000 public sector jobs?
rigor.explanation: Marshals data but asserts a direct causal link between two trends without establishing it.

rigor.statement: I’m actually proud that we’re actually enforcing rights and responsibilities in this country. What we’re making sure is that there will be sanctions on benefits for people who do not uphold their basic obligations to this country and to each other.
rigor.explanation: A coherent obligations-based rationale, but rests on a values appeal rather than addressing the evidence in the question.

rigor.statement: Are the Government’s choices to under-fund critical infrastructure like our hospitals, our schools, and our ferries essentially just setting them up to fail to pave the way for an eventual sell-off of these crucial assets that we all own?
rigor.explanation: A loaded question imputing hidden motive (deliberate underfunding to enable sell-offs) without establishing the causal chain — an insinuation rather than an evidenced argument.

rigor.statement: Has the Prime Minister seen any evidence of conspiracy theories being spread in New Zealand, and, if so, what is the Government doing to dispel them?
rigor.explanation: Rhetorical framing designed to ridicule an opponent rather than advance evidence-based reasoning.

rigor.statement: Could I ask the Prime Minister as to whether he thinks it’d be in any way principled to sell a ferry that you haven’t bought yet?
rigor.explanation: Makes a fair logical observation (you cannot sell an asset not yet acquired) but deployed as a gotcha.

rigor.statement: If you follow that question very carefully, it’s loaded with innuendo and it’s also confusing, because when he finished the question, you weren’t certain whether it was the first event he was talking about or the second one. A bit of straight common sense and logic would be very helpful for those of us trying to follow the question.
rigor.explanation: Points to genuine ambiguity but leans on an appeal to 'straight common sense' rather than a precise analysis.

rigor.statement: in 2023-24, core Crown expenses were $139 billion. That is a big number. It means core Crown expenses are 73 percent higher than they were just six years earlier. This increase in expenses is far greater than the increase in revenue over the same period. The financial statements show core Crown revenue of $133 billion in 2023-24, an increase of 54 percent.
rigor.explanation: Builds a clear evidenced argument that expense growth has outpaced revenue growth; the numbers support the conclusion.

rigor.statement: As the member knows, State-owned enterprises make operational decisions independent of the Government. The Government’s decision was to not provide additional funding for the Project iReX. Operational decisions thereafter are the responsibility of the State-owned enterprise.
rigor.explanation: Draws a defensible distinction between a funding decision and downstream operational decisions, though it sidesteps accountability for the flow-on effect.

rigor.statement: It is, I think, a stretch for me to take responsibility for six years of a Labour Government that cranked up Government spending to irresponsible levels, driving up inflation, causing the Reserve Bank to have to crank up interest rates to levels which have had a very damaging effect on the economy. We’re here now; we’re cleaning up the mess. Our plan is working.
rigor.explanation: Offers a causal chain (spending → inflation → rate rises → damage) that is plausible but presented one-sidedly without acknowledging global inflation drivers.

rigor.statement: Well, the Hawke’s Bay Expressway carries 29,000 vehicles a day and links freight to one of New Zealand largest ports. The region’s growing population and economy means that the central section of this road is reaching capacity at peak times
rigor.explanation: Reasonable evidence-to-conclusion chain: high volume plus growth means the road is nearing capacity, justifying four-laning.

rigor.statement: Fewer prison sentences have been imposed in recent years, and at the same time the prevalence of serious violent crime and sexual crimes has increased—which is why we are progressing a range of initiatives, including reforming the sentencing regime
rigor.explanation: Juxtaposes two trends (fewer sentences, more serious crime) to justify policy, implying causation from correlation without establishing the link.

rigor.statement: It is clear that a very small number of prolific offenders create many, many victims. Three strikes will stop them—for longer—from adding more victims to their list.
rigor.explanation: Asserts the policy will work from the premise that a few offenders cause many victims, without evidence that longer sentences net-reduce victimisation.

rigor.statement: Why does the Minister blame the massive increase in exploitation claims on visa settings incentivising offshore agents to offer fake jobs, when her own Cabinet paper acknowledges that would only be 150 people compared to the 3,925 migrant exploitation claims?
rigor.explanation: Evidence-based challenge exposing a proportionality gap between the cited cause and the total scale of complaints.

rigor.statement: Did she talk to any exploited migrants, unions, workers’ rights advocates to substantiate those comments, or is she making those statements based off vibes and without information from the ground?
rigor.explanation: Raises a fair evidentiary question but frames it as a rhetorical false dichotomy (consulted advocates vs 'vibes').

civility.statement: I said a brief pause between each announcement, so that an appropriate point of order could be raised at the right time, would be proper, otherwise one has no opportunity to follow the Standing Orders and make a point of order at the right time.
civility.explanation: Respectful, procedure-focused point directed at process rather than any person.

civility.statement: was there an addendum to their communication with you, thanking the party and the mover of the changed law in 2018 to revive the “waka hopping bill”, in gratitude for that interposition back then, that assisted them to be the first ones ever to use it?
civility.explanation: A sarcastic dig at the Greens (over Darleen Tana), framed as an inquiry; needling rather than substantive engagement, though it points to a real irony.

civility.statement: The Prime Minister might want to take some lessons after his failure to achieve a free-trade agreement with India.
civility.explanation: A partisan jab inserted into an otherwise unifying speech; personal dig at the PM's competence rather than engagement with the substance.

civility.statement: Why does a Minister in his Government calling somebody a “loser” for working late and telling him to “Take some wine and [eff] off” not warrant any formal sanction from him as Prime Minister?
civility.explanation: Pointed accountability question that quotes the conduct at issue; harsh but legitimate scrutiny of a minister's behaviour rather than a gratuitous personal attack.

civility.statement: Is he confident that Andrew Bayly had not consumed any alcohol when he berated an export worker for the very fact that he was working, and, if not, will he commit to removing Mr Bayly’s ministerial warrant if it’s proven that he indeed was under the influence of alcohol when he behaved inappropriately?
civility.explanation: Sharp but focused on a minister's conduct and accountability rather than pure character assassination.

civility.statement: Well, as I’ve said publicly, I was disappointed in the Minister’s conduct. It didn’t meet my standards; it didn’t meet the standards of what we expect from Ministers. But he has subsequently genuinely apologised, acknowledged the wrong, and assured me it won’t happen again.
civility.explanation: Measured, non-attacking response that engages with the standards issue respectfully.

civility.statement: The member is in a very dark and conspiratorial mood today. I just say, we have no plans to do any asset sales.
civility.explanation: Characterises the opponent's disposition as 'dark and conspiratorial' — a mild dismissive personal framing before answering the substance.

civility.statement: Has the Prime Minister seen any evidence of conspiracy theories being spread in New Zealand, and, if so, what is the Government doing to dispel them?
civility.explanation: A set-up question mocking the preceding Green questioner's 'conspiratorial' line; scores as a partisan dig rather than substantive inquiry.

civility.statement: Could I ask the Prime Minister as to whether he thinks it’d be in any way principled to sell a ferry that you haven’t bought yet?
civility.explanation: A sardonic rhetorical jab aimed at the Green line of questioning; needling but tied to a policy point.

civility.statement: If you follow that question very carefully, it’s loaded with innuendo and it’s also confusing, because when he finished the question, you weren’t certain whether it was the first event he was talking about or the second one. A bit of straight common sense and logic would be very helpful for those of us trying to follow the question.
civility.explanation: Criticises the opponent's question as 'loaded with innuendo'; targets the question's framing but edges toward disparaging the questioner.

civility.statement: Could the Minister confirm as to whether it’s a fact that the greatest percentage of migrant exploitation is being exploited by their own and that is the recent history of this country, sadly?
civility.explanation: Frames the issue pointedly but as a policy/factual inquiry rather than a personal attack.

civility.statement: It is, I think, a stretch for me to take responsibility for six years of a Labour Government that cranked up Government spending to irresponsible levels, driving up inflation, causing the Reserve Bank to have to crank up interest rates to levels which have had a very damaging effect on the economy. We’re here now; we’re cleaning up the mess. Our plan is working.
civility.explanation: Sharp partisan attack on the previous government's record, but aimed at policy/spending rather than personal insult.

civility.statement: When will she take responsibility for the economy declining, when liquidations are up; unemployment is up; rents, rates, and insurance premiums are up; and there is a record net migration of Kiwis moving overseas?
civility.explanation: Aggressive accountability question focused on economic policy outcomes rather than personal attack.

civility.statement: I’m advised that in September 2022, the ministry proposed a review of 950 bus routes to the then Minister to address a “significant number” of routes that were operating outside of policy settings and the appropriation. The Minister declined and paused proactive reviews for 18 months, coinciding with the election year.
civility.explanation: Legitimate criticism of the predecessor's decision, but the 'election year' aside is a pointed insinuation.

civility.statement: I would say to that mother that it’s unfortunate that the previous Government didn’t look at the policy settings and acted outside the appropriation.
civility.explanation: Deflects to a partisan criticism; policy-focused but sidesteps the human concern raised.

civility.statement: Did she talk to any exploited migrants, unions, workers’ rights advocates to substantiate those comments, or is she making those statements based off vibes and without information from the ground?
civility.explanation: The 'based off vibes' phrasing is a dismissive jab implying the Minister acts without evidence, tipping from substance toward mockery.

civility.statement: I accept the overall account of what happened between myself and the individual. I was certainly not drunk and I do not believe I swore. Regardless, I accept that I was wrong and that my actions caused hurt and offence, and that is why I’ve unreservedly apologised to the individual.
civility.explanation: Contrite, respectful acknowledgement of harm caused, focused on accountability.

civility.statement: What does she say to the Hawke’s Bay mother who, due to the cancellation of her local bus route near Kaiwaka, says that she has no other option but to allow her son to commit truancy?
civility.explanation: Pointed but legitimate scrutiny highlighting a real-world impact, without personal attack.

veracity.statement: The next sporting victory was the Black Caps, who won the first test against India, just our third win against India in India ever, and our first win in India since 1988
veracity.explanation: Factual sporting claim consistent with the record — NZ's win in Bengaluru was a rare test victory in India, first since 1988.

veracity.statement: the Black Caps’ bowling attack got rolling, and eventually skittled India out for 46—their lowest total at home, ever.
veracity.explanation: Accurate factual sporting claim; India were bowled out for 46, a record-low home total.

veracity.statement: The Prime Minister might want to take some lessons after his failure to achieve a free-trade agreement with India.
veracity.explanation: It is true no NZ–India FTA has been concluded, but 'failure' overstates a long-running negotiation as a personal defeat.

veracity.statement: It’s a reflection of the very successful Strategy for Women and Girls in Sport and Active Recreation established in 2018 by Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern and sport and recreation Minister Grant Robertson, and we are reaping the benefits now.
veracity.explanation: The strategy exists, but attributing current elite-sport wins directly to it is a causal claim that is plausible yet unproven.

veracity.statement: Converting a grid 19 start to a ninth-place finish is simply incredible.
veracity.explanation: Accurate description of Liam Lawson's result — a strong recovery drive from near the back of the grid.

veracity.statement: The Paddle Ferns, the women’s canoe polo team, the world champions who won the title, as we’ve heard, 6-1 over Italy. But they’ve had to do this the hard way. They’ve had to raise all their own money without local government or central government support.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with the account given repeatedly in the debate that the canoe polo team was self-funded.

veracity.statement: How does he justify the 133 percent increase in benefit sanctions over the last year when unemployment is the highest it has been in three years as a direct result of this Government cutting 7,000 public sector jobs?
veracity.explanation: The individual figures are broadly defensible, but attributing rising unemployment as a 'direct result' of public-sector cuts is an overstated single-cause claim.

veracity.statement: Is this Government upholding its Treaty obligations by removing Treaty provisions from 28 separate pieces of legislation?
veracity.explanation: The figure references a real review of Treaty clauses, but the precise count and framing are contested.

veracity.statement: Why does a Minister in his Government calling somebody a “loser” for working late and telling him to “Take some wine and [eff] off” not warrant any formal sanction from him as Prime Minister?
veracity.explanation: Repeats the substance of the complaint, most of which Bayly later confirms (the 'loser' remark), though the wine/'eff off' wording Bayly disputes.

veracity.statement: This Government is determined to do well for Māori. As we have talked about in this House before, it is utterly unacceptable that only 12 percent of Māori are ready to go to high school with their maths knowledge.
veracity.explanation: The '12 percent of Māori ready with maths' figure references a real attainment concern but is a stark statistic whose precise basis is arguable.

veracity.statement: Could the Minister confirm as to whether it’s a fact that the greatest percentage of migrant exploitation is being exploited by their own and that is the recent history of this country, sadly?
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that most migrant exploitation is by 'their own' communities; a contested generalisation the Minister only partially confirms.

veracity.statement: in 2023-24, core Crown expenses were $139 billion. That is a big number. It means core Crown expenses are 73 percent higher than they were just six years earlier. This increase in expenses is far greater than the increase in revenue over the same period. The financial statements show core Crown revenue of $133 billion in 2023-24, an increase of 54 percent.
veracity.explanation: Draws directly from published Treasury financial statements; the figures are verifiable, though 'six years earlier' framing is chosen to maximise the contrast.

veracity.statement: After 12 interest rate increases under the last Government, we have seen a 75 basis-point reduction, we have seen inflation return—to the target band, and we have delivered tax relief to 3.5 million working New Zealanders.
veracity.explanation: The numbers are broadly accurate, though the framing implies more direct government credit for rate movements than the independent Reserve Bank would support.

veracity.statement: Will she take responsibility for the economy declining under her watch when liquidations are up 19 percent year on year?
veracity.explanation: The liquidations figure reflects real reported trends, though 'the economy declining' is a broader characterisation attributed to one cause.

veracity.statement: When will she take responsibility for the economy declining, when liquidations are up; unemployment is up; rents, rates, and insurance premiums are up; and there is a record net migration of Kiwis moving overseas?
veracity.explanation: Each cited trend is broadly real, but bundling them all as the minister's responsibility overstates a single-actor causation.

veracity.statement: Well, the Hawke’s Bay Expressway carries 29,000 vehicles a day and links freight to one of New Zealand largest ports. The region’s growing population and economy means that the central section of this road is reaching capacity at peak times
veracity.explanation: Traffic and freight-linkage claims are the sort of verifiable NZTA data typically cited for this corridor.

veracity.statement: Fewer prison sentences have been imposed in recent years, and at the same time the prevalence of serious violent crime and sexual crimes has increased—which is why we are progressing a range of initiatives, including reforming the sentencing regime
veracity.explanation: Both underlying trends are broadly reflected in official data, but the implied causal relationship is not demonstrated.

veracity.statement: We know that in the year ending June 2024, more than 200,000 people have been victims of crime.
veracity.explanation: Broadly consistent with victimisation survey figures, though 'victims of crime' totals depend heavily on the measure used.

veracity.statement: I’m advised that in September 2022, the ministry proposed a review of 950 bus routes to the then Minister to address a “significant number” of routes that were operating outside of policy settings and the appropriation. The Minister declined and paused proactive reviews for 18 months, coinciding with the election year.
veracity.explanation: Presents an official-advice account, but the 'coinciding with the election year' framing implies political motive that is insinuated rather than shown.

veracity.statement: Why does the Minister blame the massive increase in exploitation claims on visa settings incentivising offshore agents to offer fake jobs, when her own Cabinet paper acknowledges that would only be 150 people compared to the 3,925 migrant exploitation claims?
veracity.explanation: Cites specific document-based figures; the contrast is compelling though the government's fuller rationale may add context.

specificity.statement: The next sporting victory was the Black Caps, who won the first test against India, just our third win against India in India ever, and our first win in India since 1988
specificity.explanation: Names the teams, the ranking (third ever), and a precise date (1988).

specificity.statement: the Black Caps’ bowling attack got rolling, and eventually skittled India out for 46—their lowest total at home, ever.
specificity.explanation: Precise figure (46) plus the concrete superlative claim (lowest home total ever).

specificity.statement: It’s a reflection of the very successful Strategy for Women and Girls in Sport and Active Recreation established in 2018 by Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern and sport and recreation Minister Grant Robertson, and we are reaping the benefits now.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific policy, year (2018), and the responsible ministers.

specificity.statement: Converting a grid 19 start to a ninth-place finish is simply incredible.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete grid and finishing positions (P19 to P9).

specificity.statement: These achievements represent more than just victories, they embody the Kiwi spirit of punching well above our weight and never backing down from a challenge.
specificity.explanation: Relies on the vague slogan-like phrase 'punching above our weight' with no concrete detail.

specificity.statement: The Paddle Ferns, the women’s canoe polo team, the world champions who won the title, as we’ve heard, 6-1 over Italy. But they’ve had to do this the hard way. They’ve had to raise all their own money without local government or central government support.
specificity.explanation: Concrete score line (6-1) and specific claim about the team self-funding without government support.

specificity.statement: How does he justify the 133 percent increase in benefit sanctions over the last year when unemployment is the highest it has been in three years as a direct result of this Government cutting 7,000 public sector jobs?
specificity.explanation: Cites precise figures (133% increase, 7,000 jobs) and a timeframe.

specificity.statement: Is this Government upholding its Treaty obligations by removing Treaty provisions from 28 separate pieces of legislation?
specificity.explanation: Concrete count (28 pieces of legislation) anchoring the question.

specificity.statement: Is he confident that Andrew Bayly had not consumed any alcohol when he berated an export worker for the very fact that he was working, and, if not, will he commit to removing Mr Bayly’s ministerial warrant if it’s proven that he indeed was under the influence of alcohol when he behaved inappropriately?
specificity.explanation: Asks a precise two-part question tied to a concrete condition (proof of alcohol influence) and consequence (warrant removal).

specificity.statement: Yes, and especially our action to deliver modern, reliable infrastructure for New Zealand. I was absolutely thrilled on Monday to announce—alongside the Minister of Transport, Simeon Brown—that work had started on our Government’s first road of national significance this week, which of course is the Hawke’s Bay Expressway.
specificity.explanation: Names the project, the minister, and that early works started this week, but no cost or completion figures here.

specificity.statement: Are the Government’s choices to under-fund critical infrastructure like our hospitals, our schools, and our ferries essentially just setting them up to fail to pave the way for an eventual sell-off of these crucial assets that we all own?
specificity.explanation: Names concrete assets (hospitals, schools, ferries) but the mechanism alleged is speculative.

specificity.statement: in 2023-24, core Crown expenses were $139 billion. That is a big number. It means core Crown expenses are 73 percent higher than they were just six years earlier. This increase in expenses is far greater than the increase in revenue over the same period. The financial statements show core Crown revenue of $133 billion in 2023-24, an increase of 54 percent.
specificity.explanation: Dense with precise figures: $139b expenses, $133b revenue, 73% and 54% growth over six years.

specificity.statement: After 12 interest rate increases under the last Government, we have seen a 75 basis-point reduction, we have seen inflation return—to the target band, and we have delivered tax relief to 3.5 million working New Zealanders.
specificity.explanation: Concrete figures: 12 rate increases, 75 basis-point cut, 3.5 million recipients of tax relief.

specificity.statement: Will she take responsibility for the economy declining under her watch when liquidations are up 19 percent year on year?
specificity.explanation: Anchored to a concrete metric (liquidations up 19% year on year).

specificity.statement: When will she take responsibility for the economy declining, when liquidations are up; unemployment is up; rents, rates, and insurance premiums are up; and there is a record net migration of Kiwis moving overseas?
specificity.explanation: Enumerates multiple concrete indicators (liquidations, unemployment, rents, rates, premiums, net migration).

specificity.statement: Well, the Hawke’s Bay Expressway carries 29,000 vehicles a day and links freight to one of New Zealand largest ports. The region’s growing population and economy means that the central section of this road is reaching capacity at peak times
specificity.explanation: Concrete traffic volume (29,000 vehicles/day) and a clear rationale tied to capacity and freight linkage.

specificity.statement: Starting early works now allows the New Zealand Transport Agency (NZTA) to maximise the 2025-26 construction season and bring forward the construction of this critical four-lane road of national significance by 12 to 15 months.
specificity.explanation: Names the construction season and a precise acceleration (12–15 months).

specificity.statement: We know that in the year ending June 2024, more than 200,000 people have been victims of crime.
specificity.explanation: Precise figure and timeframe (200,000+, year ending June 2024).

specificity.statement: It caps sentence discounts, prevents repeat discounts for youth and remorse, and introduces a bundle of new aggravating factors and a range of other initiatives.
specificity.explanation: Lists concrete mechanisms of the bill (discount caps, no repeat youth/remorse discounts, new aggravating factors), though 'a range of other initiatives' is vague.

specificity.statement: That’s why in April, in response to the Bestwick review and the surge in complaints, this Government made immediate changes to reduce the opportunity for unscrupulous actors to exploit migrants. This included introducing minimum English requirements and the relevant experience requirements for low-skilled roles.
specificity.explanation: Names the timing, the triggering review, and concrete measures (English and experience requirements).

specificity.statement: if they do not have the skills and experience to find employment after six months, then it’s time to leave New Zealand.
specificity.explanation: Concrete threshold (six months) and consequence (departure).

specificity.statement: I’m advised that in September 2022, the ministry proposed a review of 950 bus routes to the then Minister to address a “significant number” of routes that were operating outside of policy settings and the appropriation. The Minister declined and paused proactive reviews for 18 months, coinciding with the election year.
specificity.explanation: Detailed: 950 routes, September 2022, an 18-month pause.

specificity.statement: Why does the Minister blame the massive increase in exploitation claims on visa settings incentivising offshore agents to offer fake jobs, when her own Cabinet paper acknowledges that would only be 150 people compared to the 3,925 migrant exploitation claims?
specificity.explanation: Uses precise figures (150 vs 3,925) drawn from a named source (the Cabinet paper).

specificity.statement: What does she say to the Hawke’s Bay mother who, due to the cancellation of her local bus route near Kaiwaka, says that she has no other option but to allow her son to commit truancy?
specificity.explanation: Grounds the question in a concrete case (a named locality, Kaiwaka, and a specific human consequence).

charisma.statement: To all the athletes who did so well on the world stage this weekend, the House would like you to know, and the Government would like you to know, that New Zealand is very proud of you.
charisma.explanation: Inclusive, unifying congratulation on behalf of the whole House; builds national common ground rather than partisan division.

charisma.statement: I rise to support the Government’s motion to congratulate the country’s sporting success over the weekend.
charisma.explanation: Cross-party endorsement of a Government motion; explicitly reaches across the aisle to find common ground.

charisma.statement: These achievements represent more than just victories, they embody the Kiwi spirit of punching well above our weight and never backing down from a challenge.
charisma.explanation: Inclusive national framing that celebrates a shared identity; unifying but appeals to broadly shared sentiment.

charisma.statement: let’s also remember we also need to back our creativity, our innovation, right across our country, right across our economic performance as well, because if we don’t do that, we’re never going to lift the productivity that we need to lift.
charisma.explanation: Constructive, forward-looking appeal to shared national improvement rather than partisan attack.

charisma.statement: I think it’s really important that we start the week with something we all agree on.
charisma.explanation: Explicitly seeks common ground across the House; consensus-building framing.

forthrightness.statement: Well, as I’ve said publicly, I was disappointed in the Minister’s conduct. It didn’t meet my standards; it didn’t meet the standards of what we expect from Ministers. But he has subsequently genuinely apologised, acknowledged the wrong, and assured me it won’t happen again.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked why the conduct warranted no formal sanction, he expresses disappointment and points to the apology but never addresses the actual question of sanction.

forthrightness.statement: Yes, and especially our action to deliver modern, reliable infrastructure for New Zealand. I was absolutely thrilled on Monday to announce—alongside the Minister of Transport, Simeon Brown—that work had started on our Government’s first road of national significance this week, which of course is the Hawke’s Bay Expressway.
forthrightness.explanation: Directly answers 'yes' to the standby question but immediately pivots into promotional messaging about roads.

forthrightness.statement: The member is in a very dark and conspiratorial mood today. I just say, we have no plans to do any asset sales.
forthrightness.explanation: Does give a direct denial ('no plans to do any asset sales') though prefaced by dismissing the questioner's framing.

forthrightness.statement: Well, again, that is not on our agenda. What we are focused on is our quarterly action plans. We take delivery and execution very seriously, on this side of the House.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to commit outright to not privatising assets, he repeats 'not on our agenda' and pivots to action plans without giving the requested firm commitment.

forthrightness.statement: This Government is determined to do well for Māori. As we have talked about in this House before, it is utterly unacceptable that only 12 percent of Māori are ready to go to high school with their maths knowledge.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked directly whether removing Treaty provisions from 28 statutes honours Treaty obligations, he ignores the question entirely and pivots to Māori maths achievement.

forthrightness.statement: I’m actually proud that we’re actually enforcing rights and responsibilities in this country. What we’re making sure is that there will be sanctions on benefits for people who do not uphold their basic obligations to this country and to each other.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to justify a specific 133% rise in sanctions, he defends the policy in principle without engaging the figure or the unemployment context raised.

forthrightness.statement: I’m not sure what my schedule will be at that time; I have a funny feeling I might be overseas, but the point would be, very clearly, people are free to protest as long as it’s done legally and peacefully.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked if he will front up to the hīkoi on 19 November, he neither commits nor declines, deflecting with schedule uncertainty.

forthrightness.statement: They’re completely different things.
forthrightness.explanation: Responds to the question about the difference between running a company and a country with a dismissive non-answer that supplies no substance.

forthrightness.statement: As the member knows, State-owned enterprises make operational decisions independent of the Government. The Government’s decision was to not provide additional funding for the Project iReX. Operational decisions thereafter are the responsibility of the State-owned enterprise.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to take responsibility for 50+ job losses from cancelling the ferries, she deflects to the SOE's operational autonomy rather than owning the consequence.

forthrightness.statement: It is, I think, a stretch for me to take responsibility for six years of a Labour Government that cranked up Government spending to irresponsible levels, driving up inflation, causing the Reserve Bank to have to crank up interest rates to levels which have had a very damaging effect on the economy. We’re here now; we’re cleaning up the mess. Our plan is working.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked to take responsibility for rising liquidations under her watch, she declines and redirects blame to the previous government.

forthrightness.statement: Ministers are focused on getting the right solution for a safe, reliable, and resilient Cook Strait ferry service. An announcement will be made when Cabinet has made a decision.
forthrightness.explanation: The question asked why, after 315 days, no ferry decision has been announced; she restates the goal and defers to an unspecified future announcement without addressing the delay.

forthrightness.statement: the advice given to me was to make sure that we are limiting the amount of time given for a migrant to be in the country without a job. I would note that six months is a reasonable amount of time for someone to look for work and gain meaningful employment with an accredited employer.
forthrightness.explanation: Explains the reasoning for six months but does not squarely address the challenge that she reversed her own earlier commitment.

forthrightness.statement: if they do not have the skills and experience to find employment after six months, then it’s time to leave New Zealand.
forthrightness.explanation: A clear, unhedged statement of the policy consequence.

forthrightness.statement: I haven’t made any decisions to close bus routes. As the previous Minister well knows, that is an operational matter for the ministry to make sure they’re operating within their appropriation.
forthrightness.explanation: Denies personally deciding closures and reframes as operational/legal necessity, partly answering while shifting responsibility to the ministry.

forthrightness.statement: I would say to that mother that it’s unfortunate that the previous Government didn’t look at the policy settings and acted outside the appropriation.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked what she says to a specific affected mother, she redirects to blaming the previous government rather than addressing the family's situation.

forthrightness.statement: I accept the overall account of what happened between myself and the individual. I was certainly not drunk and I do not believe I swore. Regardless, I accept that I was wrong and that my actions caused hurt and offence, and that is why I’ve unreservedly apologised to the individual.
forthrightness.explanation: Largely direct: accepts the overall account and admits wrongdoing, while clearly contesting the specific 'drunk' and swearing elements.

forthrightness.statement: Yes. I was wrong, but I intended the comments in a light-hearted manner; unfortunately, it has caused hurt and offence, and for that reason I’ve apologised unreservedly to the individual.
forthrightness.explanation: Asked directly if he called the worker a loser, he answers 'Yes' immediately and owns it, with context.

forthrightness.statement: They are unrelated. You asked me whether I had alcohol and I said no.
forthrightness.explanation: Restates a denial but bristles at the follow-up about visiting a beer garden and winery, treating the connection as illegitimate rather than fully addressing it.

strength.statement: Yes, and especially our action to deliver modern, reliable infrastructure for New Zealand. I was absolutely thrilled on Monday to announce—alongside the Minister of Transport, Simeon Brown—that work had started on our Government’s first road of national significance this week, which of course is the Hawke’s Bay Expressway.
strength.explanation: Claims credit for starting works, but 'work had started' / early works is commencement of an announced project, not delivered completion.

strength.statement: After 12 interest rate increases under the last Government, we have seen a 75 basis-point reduction, we have seen inflation return—to the target band, and we have delivered tax relief to 3.5 million working New Zealanders.
strength.explanation: Claims delivery of a promised tax cut to 3.5 million people — a concrete, largely enacted commitment.

strength.statement: Starting early works now allows the New Zealand Transport Agency (NZTA) to maximise the 2025-26 construction season and bring forward the construction of this critical four-lane road of national significance by 12 to 15 months.
strength.explanation: Describes early works commencing and a scheduling benefit; concrete progress but delivery of the full road is still prospective.

strength.statement: That’s why in April, in response to the Bestwick review and the surge in complaints, this Government made immediate changes to reduce the opportunity for unscrupulous actors to exploit migrants. This included introducing minimum English requirements and the relevant experience requirements for low-skilled roles.
strength.explanation: Points to specific changes already enacted (April) in response to a named review — action delivered rather than merely promised.

divination.statement: It is clear that a very small number of prolific offenders create many, many victims. Three strikes will stop them—for longer—from adding more victims to their list.
divination.explanation: Predicts that reinstating three strikes will reduce future victims; the evidence on three-strikes deterrence/incapacitation effects is mixed and often unfavourable, so an optimistic estimate.

authenticity.statement: the advice given to me was to make sure that we are limiting the amount of time given for a migrant to be in the country without a job. I would note that six months is a reasonable amount of time for someone to look for work and gain meaningful employment with an accredited employer.
authenticity.explanation: Directly at odds with her pre-election position (reported as promising a three-year open work visa for exploited migrants); she now defends halving protection to six months, a clear reversal.

authenticity.statement: Yes. I was wrong, but I intended the comments in a light-hearted manner; unfortunately, it has caused hurt and offence, and for that reason I’ve apologised unreservedly to the individual.
authenticity.explanation: Admission aligns with his acceptance of the account and his apology; consistent conduct, though the 'light-hearted' framing softens the admitted wrong.

veracity.statement: It brought 390 schools to the Bay of Plenty, and over 12,900 athletes—that's more than the Paris Olympics had at 10,700 athletes
veracity.explanation: The AIMS Games athlete count (~12,900) and the Paris 2024 figure (~10,500) are both close to reality; the comparison is broadly accurate, with the Olympic number very slightly overstated.

veracity.statement: to our local economy it brought a million dollars a day and nearly 25,000 people to our region
veracity.explanation: Plausible economic-impact figures for a large youth sports event, but presented as round numbers without a cited source; hard to verify precisely.

veracity.statement: The Sands town centre in Pāpāmoa East is being opened. This is going to be four times the size of Bayfair
veracity.explanation: A promotional size comparison relative to Bayfair that is plausible but unverified from the text.

veracity.statement: I saw the new iteration of solar farms by the airport there—14,500 thousand solar panels that are going to help to power more than 2,000 homes.
veracity.explanation: Plausible figures for a New Plymouth solar farm, though the '14,500 thousand' phrasing is garbled and the home-equivalent count is an estimate.

veracity.statement: we've brought international investors over such as BlueFloat Energy, who sadly today have chosen to exit New Zealand because they cannot see that it's viable.
veracity.explanation: BlueFloat Energy did announce its withdrawal from the New Zealand offshore wind market around this time; the claim matches the public record, with the stated reason his interpretation.

veracity.statement: the uncertainty that the fast-track bill brings; the uncertainty that Trans-Tasman Resources and their sea mining brings; the uncertainty of the fact that nowhere in the world have we seen the ability to do seabed mining and to do offshore wind at the same time. They have left New Zealand
veracity.explanation: The tension between offshore wind and seabed mining in the same area is real, but 'nowhere in the world' is a sweeping claim that is hard to substantiate.

veracity.statement: the previous Labour Government invested heavily in green hydrogen and Hiringa Energy—which is based, again, locally in Taranaki
veracity.explanation: The previous Labour government did back green hydrogen initiatives including Hiringa Energy in Taranaki; broadly accurate.

veracity.statement: categorisation is almost complete, with buyouts currently occurring. There are just a few points in the area where some gaps have left people uncertain about how to deal with their properties
veracity.explanation: A measured, plausible progress description acknowledging both movement and remaining gaps; hard to verify precisely but not overstated.

veracity.statement: Takanini has over 50 percent of its residents born overseas, including myself.
veracity.explanation: Consistent with census data for this highly diverse South Auckland area; plausible and likely accurate.

veracity.statement: one of the biggest issues for them is the lack of law and order that was allowed to run rampant in the last six years under the former Government.
veracity.explanation: A loaded partisan framing ('run rampant') that overstates and lacks supporting statistics.

veracity.statement: it's 80 years since Peter Fraser brought in 733 children and 105 adults to look after them. They came in because Stalin was going to send those children off to Siberia.
veracity.explanation: Substantially accurate: in 1944 the Fraser government took in the Polish refugee children at Pahīatua (about 733 children plus accompanying caregivers); the figures and context are close to the historical record.

veracity.statement: These helicopters were going to land 28 times a week, and it affects the whole community.
veracity.explanation: A specific claim about the consent application's proposed landings; plausible and presumably drawn from the application, though unverified here.

veracity.statement: There was actually a crash that occurred in New York a few years ago, where shrapnel landed in, I think, Madison Ave, and killed somebody.
veracity.explanation: Loosely gestures at a real NYC helicopter incident but the specifics (shrapnel on Madison Ave killing a bystander) are hazy and self-hedged ('I think'); details do not cleanly match a known event.

veracity.statement: I had 1,000 people respond, or just over, to that survey; the majority wanting 12 concerts—I've been able to identify ways that I could help that community, by talking to them.
